name: Terravox
tagline: Your codebase, speaking back to you
description: Terravox turns codebases into conversational interfaces. Engineers ask questions in plain English and get answers grounded in their actual code — not generic docs. Built for teams drowning in tribal knowledge.
mission:
Every engineering team has a dark matter problem. The most critical knowledge — why that service was split, which edge case broke prod last November, how the auth flow actually works — lives in Slack threads, PR comments, and the heads of three people who've been here since day one.

Terravox exists because we believe code should be its own documentation. Not through comments or wikis that rot the moment they're written, but through a living intelligence layer that reads your entire codebase, your git history, your design docs, and your incident reports — and answers questions as if it were your most senior engineer.

We're not building another code search tool. We're building institutional memory for engineering organizations. When a new hire asks "how does billing work?", they should get the same quality answer at 2am on a Saturday that they'd get sitting next to your staff engineer on a Tuesday.

Our founding team spent a combined 30 years at infrastructure companies watching brilliant engineers waste hours reverse-engineering systems that someone else already understood. We're fixing that by making codebases conversational — not as a novelty, but as the primary interface for understanding complex software systems.

The future we're building toward is one where onboarding takes days instead of months, where incident response is guided by full system context, and where the bus factor of any team approaches infinity.
marketResearch:
The developer productivity market has ballooned to $22B globally, with AI-assisted development tools growing at 34% CAGR. The specific niche of codebase intelligence — tools that provide deep understanding of existing codebases rather than generating new code — is nascent but rapidly emerging, with an addressable market of roughly $6B across enterprise engineering teams.

Our SAM focuses on engineering organizations with 30+ developers running microservice architectures where knowledge fragmentation is acute. This represents approximately $2.1B in annual spend. Our initial SOM targets Series B-D startups and mid-market tech companies in North America, representing $350M in near-term opportunity.

The competitive landscape is bifurcated: on one side, code search tools like Sourcegraph and GitHub Code Search offer syntactic search but no semantic understanding. On the other, AI coding assistants like GitHub Copilot and Cursor focus on code generation rather than comprehension. Terravox occupies the gap — deep codebase understanding delivered through natural language. Our moat is the proprietary knowledge graph that connects code, git history, CI/CD data, and documentation into a unified semantic model.

Early traction includes design partnerships with two Series C infrastructure companies and one public fintech, all reporting 60%+ reduction in time spent on code archaeology. Our PLG motion starts with a free tier for open-source projects, converting to team plans when private repos are connected. Enterprise contracts include SSO, audit logs, and self-hosted deployment.

name: Patchwork
tagline: Stitch your tools together without writing glue code
description: Patchwork is a visual workflow builder that connects internal tools, APIs, and databases into automated pipelines. Think Zapier, but for engineering teams who need conditional logic, error handling, and observability built in.
mission:
Engineering teams are drowning in glue code. For every core system they build, there are dozens of scripts, cron jobs, and webhook handlers that shuttle data between tools, trigger notifications, and keep the machine running. This connective tissue is unglamorous, undertested, and the first thing to break.

Patchwork was born from a simple observation: most of this glue code follows predictable patterns. Extract data from A, transform it, load it into B, handle errors, alert if something breaks. Yet every team rebuilds these patterns from scratch, scattered across Lambda functions and GitHub Actions that nobody wants to own.

We're building a visual workflow engine that treats integrations as first-class infrastructure. Our canvas lets engineers design complex, multi-step automations with branching logic, retry policies, and real-time observability — all without sacrificing the power that code provides. When you need custom logic, drop into TypeScript or Python within any node.

We're not trying to replace engineering. We're trying to free engineers from the maintenance burden of the 80% of automation that shouldn't require bespoke code. Our dream is that every internal process — from onboarding flows to data pipeline orchestration to incident response — lives in a Patchwork workflow that anyone on the team can understand, modify, and debug.
marketResearch:
The workflow automation and iPaaS market is valued at $13.4B in 2025, projected to hit $32B by 2030 at 19% CAGR. Consumer-oriented platforms (Zapier, Make) dominate SMB but lack the developer-grade features enterprises need. Enterprise iPaaS tools (MuleSoft, Boomi) are powerful but require months of implementation and cost six figures annually.

Patchwork targets the underserved middle: engineering teams at companies with 50-2,000 employees who need robust automation without enterprise iPaaS overhead. This segment represents a $4.8B SAM. Our initial SOM — Series A-C tech companies and mid-market SaaS businesses in North America — is approximately $600M.

Competitors include Zapier (40M+ users but lacks error handling, branching, and observability), n8n (open-source, strong community but limited enterprise features), Temporal (excellent for orchestration but requires deep engineering investment), and Retool Workflows (good UI but tightly coupled to Retool ecosystem). Patchwork differentiates by combining visual design with production-grade reliability — built-in retry policies, dead letter queues, execution traces, and version-controlled workflow definitions stored as code.

Our GTM strategy is bottom-up developer adoption. Engineers discover Patchwork when searching for workflow automation, start with the free tier (up to 1,000 executions/month), and upgrade when they need team collaboration, SSO, and higher throughput. We convert to annual contracts through platform engineering leads who see Patchwork reducing their team's operational burden.

name: Mintlayer
tagline: API docs that developers actually want to read
description: Mintlayer generates beautiful, interactive API documentation from your OpenAPI specs with built-in playground, SDK generation, and changelog tracking. No more stale Swagger pages.
mission:
Documentation is where developer experience goes to die. Companies invest millions in building elegant APIs, then ship them with auto-generated Swagger UIs that look like tax forms. The result: frustrated developers, endless support tickets, and integration timelines measured in weeks instead of hours.

Mintlayer exists because we believe API documentation should be a product, not an afterthought. We take your OpenAPI spec and transform it into a developer portal that's as polished as your landing page — with interactive request builders, real-time playground environments, auto-generated SDKs in seven languages, and changelogs that track every breaking change.

We're a team of developer advocates and API designers who spent years on the other side of bad documentation. We know that the difference between a 5-minute integration and a 5-day integration is almost never the API's complexity — it's how well the docs communicate the happy path, the edge cases, and the mental model behind the design.

Our long-term vision extends beyond documentation into the full API lifecycle. We want Mintlayer to be where developers discover, evaluate, and integrate with APIs — a developer portal that reduces time-to-first-API-call from hours to seconds.
marketResearch:
The API management market is projected to reach $41B by 2030, with developer portals and documentation tools representing roughly $3.2B of that. The shift toward API-first companies has created massive demand for better developer experience tooling. Our TAM includes every company with a public or partner API — estimated at $3.2B. Our SAM narrows to mid-market and enterprise API-first companies with 5+ public endpoints, representing $850M. Our SOM targets the US and European markets, roughly $200M.

Key competitors: Readme.com (market leader, strong brand but aging UI), Stoplight (design-first approach, weaker on hosted portals), Redocly (open-source core, limited collaboration features), and Swagger/SwaggerHub (ubiquitous but universally disliked UX). Mintlayer differentiates through three pillars: a design-forward portal that matches the quality of the best marketing sites, built-in SDK generation that stays in sync with spec changes, and a changelog system that auto-detects breaking changes and notifies affected consumers.

Our target buyer is the developer experience lead or VP Engineering at API-first companies. Sales motion is product-led: teams import their OpenAPI spec, see a beautiful portal in minutes, and upgrade for custom domains, team collaboration, and analytics. Enterprise deals add SSO, SLAs, and white-labeling.

name: Canopy
tagline: Feature flags with built-in experimentation
description: Canopy merges feature flagging with A/B testing in a single platform. Ship features behind flags, run experiments with statistical rigor, and make data-driven rollout decisions — all without stitching together LaunchDarkly and Amplitude.
mission:
The modern software release process is split-brained. Feature flags live in one tool. Experimentation lives in another. Analytics lives in a third. Engineers toggle flags in LaunchDarkly, set up experiments in Optimizely, and check results in Amplitude — switching between dashboards, duplicating targeting rules, and hoping the data lines up.

Canopy unifies this workflow. We believe that every feature rollout is an experiment, and every experiment needs a flag. By combining these capabilities in a single platform, we eliminate the coordination overhead that slows teams down and introduce statistical rigor into decisions that are currently made by gut feeling.

Our founders built experimentation infrastructure at Spotify and Netflix, where A/B testing is a cultural practice, not just a tool. We saw that even at these companies, the gap between "flag on" and "experiment complete" was filled with duct tape. At smaller companies, it's a chasm. Most teams ship features to 100% on day one and hope for the best.

We're building Canopy so that every team — not just those with dedicated experimentation platforms — can ship features safely, measure their impact, and make rollout decisions with confidence. Progressive rollouts should be the default, not a luxury.
marketResearch:
The feature management market is valued at $1.8B in 2025, growing at 25% CAGR to reach $5.5B by 2030. The experimentation/A/B testing market adds another $1.2B. The convergence of these categories — what we call "experimentation-aware feature management" — represents a $3B combined TAM. Our SAM targets product-led SaaS companies with 20+ engineers, approximately $900M. Initial SOM focusing on US-based Series A-C startups is $150M.

Primary competitors: LaunchDarkly ($3.4B valuation, market leader in flags but limited experimentation), Split.io (closest to our vision but complex setup and enterprise-only pricing), Statsig (strong experimentation but weaker flag management), and Eppo (analytics-first, less focus on flag operations). Open-source options like Unleash and Flagsmith cover basic flags but lack experimentation entirely.

Canopy's differentiation: unified flag+experiment lifecycle (create flag, define hypothesis, set rollout percentage, auto-analyze results, graduate or kill), Bayesian statistics engine that reaches significance faster than frequentist competitors, and a pricing model based on monthly tracked users rather than per-seat licensing.

GTM strategy: developer-led growth through excellent DX. Our SDK is a single line of code. Free tier supports up to 10,000 MTUs. We convert through product teams who want experiment results alongside their flag configuration. Enterprise motion targets VP Product and VP Engineering with compliance features and premium SLAs.

name: Overture
tagline: The operating system for product launches
description: Overture coordinates the chaos of product launches — syncing engineering, marketing, sales, and support across timelines, checklists, and go/no-go gates. One dashboard to replace the spreadsheet that nobody trusts.
mission:
Product launches are the highest-stakes cross-functional moment in any company. They involve engineering shipping code, marketing preparing campaigns, sales enabling reps, support writing help docs, legal reviewing terms, and leadership making go/no-go decisions. And all of this is coordinated in... a Google Sheet.

Overture exists because we've lived through the pain of launches managed by spreadsheets and Slack threads. We've seen launches slip because marketing didn't know engineering was a week behind. We've seen support tickets spike because help docs weren't updated. We've seen revenue targets missed because sales enablement started too late.

We're building a purpose-built coordination layer for product launches. Overture provides a shared timeline that every team can see, checklists that auto-assign tasks based on launch type, dependency tracking that surfaces blockers before they become emergencies, and go/no-go dashboards that give leadership a single source of truth.

Our vision goes beyond launches into the broader category of cross-functional coordination. Every company has high-stakes moments that require multiple teams to execute in sync — launches, migrations, compliance deadlines, annual planning. These moments deserve better tooling than spreadsheets and prayer.
marketResearch:
The project management software market is $7.2B and growing at 13% CAGR, but the specific niche of launch management and cross-functional coordination is underserved by existing tools. Jira, Asana, and Monday.com handle individual team workflows well but struggle with the cross-team coordination that launches require. The TAM for launch/program management tools is approximately $2B. Our SAM — product-led companies with 100-5,000 employees doing 4+ launches per year — is $650M. Our initial SOM targeting Series B+ SaaS companies is $120M.

Competitors include generic PM tools (Asana, Monday.com — too flexible, require heavy customization for launches), LaunchNotes (focused on changelog/release notes, not coordination), and Productboard (roadmap-focused, no execution layer). Overture differentiates as the only purpose-built launch coordination platform with cross-functional templates, automated dependency tracking, and integrated go/no-go workflows.

Target buyers are Heads of Product, PMOs, and Chiefs of Staff who own launch coordination today. Our sales motion starts with a free tier for individual launches, expanding to team plans for recurring launch programs. Enterprise deals include custom templates, integrations with Jira/Asana/Slack, and launch analytics.

name: Steno
tagline: Meeting intelligence that writes itself into your workflow
description: Steno records, transcribes, and extracts structured data from meetings — then pushes action items to Jira, decisions to Notion, and summaries to Slack. It's not another transcript. It's meeting-to-workflow automation.
mission:
The modern knowledge worker attends 15-20 meetings per week. Each meeting generates decisions, action items, and context that need to flow into project management tools, documentation, and communication channels. Today, that flow depends on someone taking notes and manually updating five different tools afterward. It rarely happens.

Steno was built on a radical premise: meetings shouldn't create work — they should complete it. When your team decides to push the launch date by a week, that decision should automatically update the Jira epic, notify the Slack channel, and create a Notion entry. When your manager assigns you a follow-up, it should appear in your task list without anyone copying and pasting.

We're not building a better transcription tool. We're building the connective tissue between what happens in meetings and what happens after them. Steno uses AI to extract structured data — decisions, action items, blockers, owners, deadlines — and routes them to the right tools with the right context.

Our team comes from backgrounds in NLP research and workflow automation. We believe meetings are the most underutilized data source in any organization. They contain the real decisions, the nuanced context, and the unwritten agreements that never make it into documentation. Steno's job is to capture that signal and make it actionable.
marketResearch:
The meeting technology market (recording, transcription, intelligence) is valued at $5.8B in 2025, projected to reach $12.1B by 2030 at 16% CAGR. Within this, the meeting intelligence sub-segment — tools that go beyond transcription to extract insights and automate follow-ups — is growing at 28% CAGR and represents a $2.4B opportunity.

Our SAM targets knowledge-work organizations with 50-5,000 employees where meetings are a primary coordination mechanism. This represents approximately $1.1B. Our initial SOM focuses on product and engineering teams at Series B+ tech companies, roughly $180M.

Competitor landscape: Otter.ai (largest player, strong transcription but limited action extraction), Fireflies.ai (good integrations but AI extraction is surface-level), Grain (video clips, good for sales but not for engineering/product), Fathom (free note-taking, no workflow automation). Steno differentiates through deep workflow integration — we don't just identify action items, we create Jira tickets with the right project, assignee, and context. Our extraction model is trained on meeting-specific language patterns ("let's circle back on this" = action item, "we decided to go with option B" = decision).

GTM is PLG. Steno works with Zoom, Google Meet, and Teams. Free tier records and transcribes up to 10 meetings/month. The conversion trigger is workflow automation — when teams see the value of auto-created Jira tickets, they upgrade for unlimited meetings and custom routing rules.

name: Driftwood
tagline: Project management for teams that think in documents, not tickets
description: Driftwood is a document-first project management tool where specs, tasks, and status updates live in the same rich-text workspace. It's what happens when Notion and Linear have a baby that actually ships on time.
mission:
There are two types of project management tools in the world: ticket trackers and document platforms. Jira and Linear are great at tracking work items but terrible at capturing the context behind them. Notion and Coda are great at documentation but their project management features feel bolted on.

Driftwood merges these worlds. We believe that a task without context is just busywork, and a document without accountability is just a wiki page. Every Driftwood project starts with a spec — a rich document that captures the what, why, and how. Tasks are extracted from the spec and tracked inline. As the spec evolves, tasks stay in sync. As tasks are completed, the spec reflects progress.

Our founding team built product at companies where the gap between "the document" and "the board" caused real problems. Engineers worked off stale specs. PMs updated documents that nobody checked. Status meetings existed solely to bridge the gap between what was written and what was happening.

Driftwood eliminates that gap by making documents and tasks the same thing. Your spec is your project plan is your status dashboard. We're building for teams that think in prose and paragraphs, not just checkboxes and story points.
marketResearch:
The project management software market is $7.2B, growing at 13% CAGR. The knowledge management/collaborative docs market adds $3.4B. The intersection — document-centric project management — is an emerging category with an estimated TAM of $2.8B. Our SAM targets 10-200 person teams at product-led companies that use both Notion (or Confluence) and Linear (or Jira), representing $800M. Initial SOM targeting early-stage startups and SMBs is $130M.

Competitors: Linear (excellent task tracking, minimal document capabilities), Notion (strong docs, weak project tracking), Asana (feature-rich but complex), Height (AI-powered but still ticket-first). Driftwood differentiates by making the document the atomic unit of project management — tasks emerge from documents rather than existing in a separate system.

Target user: product managers, engineering leads, and founders at 10-200 person companies who currently maintain both a documentation tool and a project tracker. Our insight is that they'd prefer one tool that does both well rather than two tools that need constant syncing.

GTM: PLG with a generous free tier (up to 5 users). Teams adopt for a single project, realize the document-task integration saves them from maintaining two tools, and expand to team-wide adoption. Pricing is per-workspace-member, competitive with Linear + Notion combined pricing.

name: Arcline
tagline: Database branching for development teams
description: Arcline lets development teams branch their database the way they branch code. Create isolated database copies for every feature branch, run migrations safely, and merge schema changes without stepping on each other.
mission:
Git solved collaboration for code. But databases are still a shared mutable resource that everyone tiptoes around. Every developer on the team either shares a staging database (and breaks each other's work) or maintains a local database (and falls out of sync). Migrations are tested by crossing fingers. Schema conflicts are discovered at merge time.

Arcline brings the branching paradigm to databases. When you create a feature branch, Arcline creates a corresponding database branch — an isolated, full-fidelity copy of your database that you can migrate, seed, and test against without affecting anyone else. When your code merges, your database changes merge too, with conflict detection and resolution built in.

We're not building another database hosting platform. We're building a workflow layer that sits between your application and your database, making the development experience match what engineers already expect from their code workflow. Branch, develop, test, merge — for data, not just code.

Our team built developer tools at PlanetScale and Neon and saw firsthand that database branching isn't just a nice-to-have — it's the missing piece of the modern development workflow. We started Arcline because we believe databases should be as easy to collaborate on as code.
marketResearch:
The database-as-a-service market is $18B and growing at 20% CAGR. Within this, developer workflow tools for databases — migration management, branching, schema design — represent an emerging $1.5B segment. Our TAM spans all development teams using relational databases, roughly $1.5B. Our SAM focuses on teams of 10-200 developers using PostgreSQL or MySQL in cloud environments, approximately $500M. Initial SOM targeting mid-market tech companies is $80M.

Competitors: PlanetScale (branching for MySQL, shutting down free tier, Vitess complexity), Neon (PostgreSQL branching but focused on serverless compute, not workflow), Atlas (Terraform for databases, migration-focused), Prisma (ORM with migrate tool, no branching). Arcline differentiates by supporting multiple database engines (Postgres, MySQL, SQLite) and focusing on the complete branch-develop-merge workflow rather than just infrastructure.

Target users: backend engineers and platform teams at companies running relational databases. Our wedge is migration safety — teams adopt Arcline to test migrations on branched databases before running them in production. The expansion motion is full branching adoption for development workflows.

GTM: open-core model. The CLI and local branching are free and open-source. Cloud sync, team collaboration, and CI/CD integration are paid features. Pricing is per-developer-seat plus storage.

name: Haystack
tagline: Internal search that actually finds things
description: Haystack is a unified search engine for your company's internal tools. Search across Notion, Slack, Google Drive, Jira, Confluence, and GitHub from a single bar. Find the thing, not ten tabs.
mission:
The average knowledge worker uses 13 different SaaS tools. Each tool has its own search — and each search only sees what's inside that tool. When you're looking for "that doc Sarah shared about the Q3 pricing strategy," you have to guess whether it's in Notion, Google Docs, Slack, or email. You open four tabs and search four times.

Haystack replaces those four searches with one. We index your company's internal tools — Notion, Slack, Google Drive, Jira, Confluence, GitHub, Linear, and more — into a unified search layer that understands context, permissions, and relevance. One search bar. One answer.

But search is just the beginning. Once we've indexed your company's knowledge, we can do things that individual tool search can't: find information that spans multiple tools, surface knowledge that's about to become stale, and answer questions using your company's collective intelligence.

We started Haystack because we lived in the world of tab-switching and context-guessing that every knowledge worker experiences. We believe that internal search should be as good as Google — but for your company's private knowledge.

name: Litmus
tagline: Visual regression testing that doesn't cry wolf
description: Litmus catches UI bugs before users do. It takes intelligent screenshots of your app across browsers and screen sizes, diffs them against your baseline, and only alerts on visual changes that actually matter — ignoring dynamic content, animations, and rendering noise.
mission:
Visual regression testing has a reputation problem. Teams try it, get buried in false positives — a timestamp changed, a loading spinner was mid-rotation, an ad shifted by 2 pixels — and turn it off. The idea is right but the execution has been terrible.

Litmus fixes visual testing by being smart about what constitutes a real change. Our diffing engine uses perceptual comparison models trained on real UI components to distinguish meaningful visual regressions from harmless rendering variance. A button that moved from the left to the center of a card? That's a regression. A tooltip that rendered 1ms later? That's noise.

We're a team of frontend engineers and QA specialists who got tired of either maintaining flaky visual tests or shipping UI bugs to production. We built Litmus because we believe visual testing should be like a senior QA engineer: observant enough to catch real issues, experienced enough to ignore noise.

Our goal is to make visual testing a reliable, always-on part of every CI pipeline. Not something teams try and abandon, but something they trust as deeply as their unit tests.
marketResearch:
The testing tools market is valued at $8.3B in 2025 with visual testing tools representing approximately $600M of that, growing at 30% CAGR as frontend complexity increases. Our TAM is the broader visual testing market. Our SAM targets web application teams with CI/CD pipelines running automated tests, approximately $350M. Initial SOM focusing on React/Next.js teams is $60M.

Competitors: Percy (Browserstack-owned, market leader but plagued by false positives), Chromatic (Storybook-focused, great for component libraries but limited for full-page testing), Applitools (enterprise pricing, AI-based but expensive at $60+/user/month), and Playwright's built-in screenshot comparison (free but requires heavy manual configuration). Litmus differentiates through perceptual AI that reduces false positives by 85% compared to pixel-based diffing, sub-10-minute feedback in CI, and pricing accessible to small teams ($19/month flat for up to 5,000 snapshots).

Target users: frontend engineers and QA leads at companies with 5-50 developers. Our wedge is the team that tried Percy, got burned by false positives, and turned off visual testing. Litmus gives them a second chance with testing that actually works.

GTM: developer-led. Free tier supports 500 snapshots/month. Integration with GitHub, GitLab, and Bitbucket PRs. Screenshots appear inline as PR checks, making adoption frictionless.

name: Conduit
tagline: Real-time data pipelines you can set up in an afternoon
description: Conduit is a managed data streaming platform that connects databases, APIs, and SaaS tools into real-time pipelines. Change data capture, transformations, and delivery — without managing Kafka or writing Flink jobs.
mission:
Every company is a data company now. But moving data between systems in real-time still requires a PhD in distributed systems or a six-figure Confluent contract. Teams that need their Postgres changes reflected in Elasticsearch within seconds — not hours — are stuck choosing between managed Kafka (expensive, complex) or batch ETL (slow, stale).

Conduit makes real-time data movement as simple as connecting two endpoints and defining a transformation. We handle the hard parts — change data capture, exactly-once delivery, schema evolution, backpressure, and failure recovery — so your team can focus on what the data does, not how it moves.

We're engineers who spent years building and maintaining data infrastructure at companies where Kafka was simultaneously the most critical and most feared system in the stack. We saw teams avoid real-time architectures because the operational overhead was too high, even when their products desperately needed fresh data.

Conduit's mission is to democratize real-time data. Not just for companies that can afford a dedicated data platform team, but for any team that needs data in the right place at the right time.
marketResearch:
The data integration and ETL market is valued at $14.2B, with real-time streaming and CDC representing the fastest-growing segment at 28% CAGR. Our TAM includes all companies needing real-time data movement between systems, approximately $6B. Our SAM focuses on mid-market companies (100-5,000 employees) that need real-time pipelines but can't justify dedicated data platform teams, roughly $2B. Initial SOM targeting tech companies replacing batch ETL with streaming is $300M.

Competitors: Confluent/Kafka (the default for streaming, but complex and expensive for mid-market), Fivetran (dominant in batch ETL, adding streaming but it's not their strength), Airbyte (open-source ETL, good community but limited real-time capabilities), Estuary (CDC-focused, closest to our positioning). Conduit differentiates through radical simplicity — a web UI where you connect source to destination, define transforms in SQL, and deploy in minutes — combined with production-grade reliability underneath.

Target buyer: data engineers and backend engineers who need real-time data movement but don't want to operate Kafka. Our PLG motion offers a free tier with up to 1M events/month. Teams upgrade when they need higher throughput, more connectors, and SLAs.

name: Ledger & Lime
tagline: Bookkeeping that feels like a conversation, not a chore
description: Ledger & Lime is an AI bookkeeping companion built specifically for freelancers, contractors, and solo business owners. It watches your transactions, asks smart clarifying questions, and keeps your books clean year-round so tax season is just another Tuesday.
mission:
There are over 70 million freelancers in the United States alone. They design logos, write code, consult on strategy, teach yoga, and build furniture. What almost none of them signed up for is spending their Sunday evenings reconciling bank statements.

Ledger & Lime was founded on a simple belief: financial clarity should not require a finance degree. We watched friends — talented photographers, brilliant copywriters, skilled therapists — lose sleep over whether they had set aside enough for quarterly taxes. We watched them pay $400/hour CPAs to fix problems that never should have happened. And we watched a generation of independent workers slowly accept that financial anxiety was just the price of freedom.

We reject that premise entirely. Ledger & Lime is an AI bookkeeper that speaks human. It connects to your bank accounts and payment platforms, categorizes every transaction, and when something is ambiguous, it asks — in plain language, through the channel you prefer. "Was that $47 at Office Depot for your photography business or personal?" One tap, done. Over time, it learns your patterns and stops asking.

Our founding team combines backgrounds in public accounting, consumer product design, and natural language AI. We built Ledger & Lime because we believe the warmth and judgment of a great bookkeeper can coexist with the speed and accuracy of modern AI. The organic, approachable brand you see is not decoration — it reflects our core product philosophy that financial tools should feel welcoming, not intimidating.

We are building toward a future where every independent worker has a financial copilot that knows their business inside out, anticipates tax obligations, flags unusual spending, and delivers a year-end package so clean their CPA sends a thank-you note.
marketResearch:
The SMB accounting software market reached $16.8 billion in 2025 and is growing at 10.8% CAGR, with the freelancer sub-segment representing approximately $4.2 billion in TAM. The shift toward independent work — accelerated by remote work normalization — means this segment is expanding faster than the overall market at roughly 15% annually.

Direct competitors include QuickBooks Self-Employed (dominant but notoriously complex for non-accountants, $15/month), FreshBooks (strong invoicing but limited automated categorization), Bench (human bookkeepers starting at $299/month), and newer entrants like Keeper Tax (narrow focus on tax deductions only). Ledger & Lime differentiates through its conversational interface — instead of forcing users into accounting workflows, it meets them where they are with natural language interactions across SMS, WhatsApp, and in-app chat.

Our serviceable addressable market focuses on English-speaking freelancers in the US, UK, Canada, and Australia earning $30K-$500K annually, representing roughly $1.1 billion. Our initial SOM targets US-based freelancers active on platforms like Upwork, Fiverr, Contra, and Toptal — a $180 million near-term opportunity. Customer research across 400+ freelancers revealed that 73% would pay $15-25/month for bookkeeping they never had to think about.

Our go-to-market strategy relies on community-led growth through freelancer Slack groups, subreddits, and partnerships with coworking spaces. A generous free tier (up to 50 transactions/month) creates a natural upgrade path, and our referral program offers a free month for both parties — leveraging the tight-knit nature of freelancer networks.

name: Vaultstream
tagline: See every dollar moving through your startup in real time
description: Vaultstream is a real-time treasury management platform built for startups and growth-stage companies. It consolidates bank accounts, tracks burn rate, and automates cash positioning so finance teams always know exactly where their money is and where it is going.
mission:
Most startups die not because they run out of ideas, but because they run out of cash. And the cruelest irony is that many of them had enough cash — they just could not see it clearly enough to make the right decisions at the right time.

Vaultstream was born in the aftermath of the 2023 banking crisis, when our founders watched startup after startup scramble to figure out basic questions: How much cash do we actually have? Across which banks? What is our real burn rate this month versus what the model says? These questions should have instant answers. Instead, CFOs were exporting CSVs from four different banking portals and pasting them into spreadsheets at 11pm.

We are building the treasury operating system that every startup deserves from day one. Vaultstream connects to every bank account, every credit card, every payment processor, and every line of credit your company touches. It normalizes that data into a single real-time dashboard where your CFO, your CEO, and your board can see cash position, runway, burn rate, and liquidity risk at a glance.

But visibility is just the beginning. Vaultstream also automates cash positioning — sweeping idle balances into yield-bearing accounts, flagging concentration risk, and alerting your team when spending patterns deviate from plan. We are building the infrastructure layer that makes startup treasury as sophisticated as enterprise treasury, without the enterprise headcount.

Our long-term vision is a world where no startup is surprised by its own finances. Where every board meeting starts with a shared, real-time understanding of the company's financial position. Where the question "how much runway do we have?" has a precise, live answer — not a spreadsheet estimate from last Tuesday.
marketResearch:
The treasury management systems market is projected to reach $7.4 billion by 2028, growing at 13.2% CAGR. However, the startup and SMB segment has been historically underserved — legacy TMS platforms like Kyriba, FIS, and ION are designed for enterprises with $500M+ in revenue and cost $100K-$500K annually. This gap has created a $1.8 billion opportunity for modern, startup-first treasury solutions.

The competitive landscape is evolving rapidly. Mercury and Brex have built banking products that include basic cash management features but lack sophisticated multi-bank treasury capabilities. Trovata offers bank data aggregation but is focused on mid-market and enterprise. Puzzle provides accounting automation but does not address treasury operations. Vaultstream occupies the specific intersection of multi-bank visibility, automated cash positioning, and startup-native UX — a combination no current player delivers.

Our serviceable market focuses on venture-backed startups in the US and Europe with $2M-$100M in annual revenue and 2+ bank relationships, representing approximately $600M in annual spend. Our initial SOM targets Series A-C startups in the US with active finance teams, a $120M near-term market.

The go-to-market motion is CFO-led: we reach finance leaders through VC portfolio support programs, CFO communities (like those run by First Round and a16z), and content marketing around cash management best practices. Our free tier for companies with under $5M in tracked balances creates a land-and-expand opportunity as companies grow.

name: Pennyfold
tagline: Investing your spare change into your actual future
description: Pennyfold is a micro-investing app designed for Gen Z. It rounds up purchases, invests spare change into diversified portfolios, and gamifies the saving habit with streaks, challenges, and social features that make building wealth feel less like adulting and more like leveling up.
mission:
Gen Z is the first generation to grow up with Venmo in one hand and student debt in the other. They are financially aware — TikTok finance creators have billions of views — but they are also paralyzed by the gap between knowing they should invest and actually doing it. The median Gen Z savings account balance is under $1,000. Not because they do not care, but because every investing app feels like it was designed for someone with a six-figure portfolio.

Pennyfold exists to close that gap. We built a micro-investing platform that meets Gen Z where they are: small amounts, high frequency, zero jargon. Every purchase you make gets rounded up to the nearest dollar, and the difference goes into a diversified portfolio tailored to your risk tolerance and time horizon. Spend $4.30 on coffee, invest $0.70 in your future. It adds up — our average user invests $47/month without ever making a conscious deposit.

But Pennyfold is not just a round-up app. We built investing into a social experience because that is how this generation learns and stays motivated. You can see how your friends' portfolios are performing (without dollar amounts — just percentages), join savings challenges, maintain investment streaks, and earn badges for hitting milestones. It sounds gamified because it is. We studied what keeps people opening Duolingo and applied those same behavioral loops to wealth building.

Our founding team includes a behavioral economist from Duke, a former Robinhood product designer, and two engineers who built payment systems at Cash App. We are not building a toy. We are building the on-ramp to financial independence for an entire generation — and we believe that on-ramp needs to feel native to how they already live their lives.
marketResearch:
The micro-investing market is projected to grow from $1.7 billion in 2024 to $6.2 billion by 2030, driven by Gen Z entering their prime earning years and demanding mobile-first investment experiences. There are approximately 68 million Gen Z individuals in the US alone, with 45 million of earning age — representing a massive greenfield opportunity.

Key competitors include Acorns (pioneer in round-up investing, 12M+ users, but brand feels dated and targets millennials), Stash ($3-$9/month, broader financial platform but lacks social features), and Robinhood (powerful but intimidating for true beginners with <$1K to invest). International players like Moneybox (UK) and Raiz (Australia) validate the model but have not cracked the US Gen Z segment. Pennyfold differentiates through its social layer, gamification mechanics, and a brand identity that feels native to the TikTok generation rather than adapted from a millennial playbook.

Our SAM focuses on US Gen Z individuals aged 18-27 with smartphone access, earning income, and not yet actively investing — approximately 22 million people representing $880M in potential annual subscription revenue at our $3.33/month price point. Our initial SOM targets digitally native Gen Z in urban and suburban markets who follow finance content creators, roughly $110M.

Go-to-market leverages creator partnerships (finance TikTokers, YouTube educators), campus ambassador programs at 50 universities, and viral referral mechanics built into the product. Our free tier includes basic round-ups; the premium tier ($3.99/month) unlocks social features, advanced portfolios, and savings challenges.

name: Tidewater
tagline: Growth capital that rises with your revenue
description: Tidewater is a revenue-based financing platform that provides non-dilutive growth capital to SaaS and e-commerce companies. Instead of giving up equity or taking on rigid debt, founders repay as a percentage of monthly revenue — when revenue dips, payments dip with it.
mission:
The venture capital model works beautifully for a small number of companies pursuing exponential, winner-take-all outcomes. But it is a terrible fit for the vast majority of profitable, growing businesses that simply need capital to scale. A SaaS company doing $2M ARR growing at 40% annually should not have to give up 20% of their company to fund their next marketing hire.

Tidewater was founded to give these companies a better option. Revenue-based financing aligns the incentives of the capital provider and the business in a way that traditional debt and equity simply do not. When your revenue grows, your payment amount grows proportionally. When you have a slow month, your payment shrinks. There is no personal guarantee, no board seat, no preference stack, and no dilution.

Our founding team spent a decade in venture lending and saw the same story repeat: founders who took equity financing not because they wanted to, but because they thought it was their only option. Banks would not lend without two years of profitability and hard assets. Revenue-based financing existed in theory but was dominated by predatory players with opaque terms and aggressive collection practices.

We built Tidewater to be different. Transparent pricing with a single flat fee disclosed upfront. No hidden covenants. A purpose-built underwriting engine that evaluates real-time revenue data, cohort retention, and unit economics — not just credit scores and tax returns. We can issue term sheets in 24 hours and fund in under a week because we built the entire stack in-house.

Our north star is a world where profitable growth companies never have to choose between dilution and deprivation. Capital should be a utility, not a transaction that reshapes your cap table.
marketResearch:
The alternative lending market for SMBs is valued at $300 billion globally, with revenue-based financing emerging as the fastest-growing sub-segment at 28% CAGR. The specific niche of RBF for SaaS and digital businesses represents approximately $18 billion in annual origination volume in North America, with significant room for growth as awareness increases.

Direct competitors include Pipe (pioneered revenue-as-collateral trading but pivoted after operational challenges), Clearco (formerly Clearbanc, focused on e-commerce and recently restructured), Capchase (SaaS-focused RBF with strong traction in mid-market), and Lighter Capital (established player but slow underwriting and traditional approach). Traditional alternatives include venture debt from Silicon Valley Bank successors and HSBC Innovation Banking, which require more collateral and come with warrants. Tidewater differentiates through speed (24-hour term sheets), transparency (single flat fee, no covenants), and a proprietary underwriting model that evaluates real-time Stripe, Chargebee, and Shopify data.

Our SAM targets SaaS and e-commerce companies in the US with $500K-$20M in ARR, representing approximately $8 billion in annual financing demand. Our initial SOM focuses on Stripe-integrated SaaS companies in the $1M-$5M ARR range seeking $100K-$1M in growth capital — roughly $1.2 billion in near-term opportunity.

Distribution leverages partnerships with SaaS-focused accountants, fractional CFO firms, and startup communities. We also integrate directly with billing platforms — when a Stripe-connected company hits certain revenue thresholds, Tidewater can present a pre-qualified offer within their existing workflow.

name: Clearance
tagline: Turn unpaid invoices into cash before lunch
description: Clearance is an instant invoice factoring platform for small and medium-sized businesses. Upload an outstanding invoice, get up to 95% of its value deposited into your account within hours — not weeks. Built for businesses tired of waiting 30, 60, or 90 days to get paid.
mission:
There is a quiet crisis in small business that rarely makes headlines. It is not about funding rounds or market conditions — it is about the gap between doing the work and getting paid for it. A construction contractor finishes a $50,000 job in March and waits until June to see the money. A marketing agency delivers a campaign in January and invoices net-60. Meanwhile, payroll is due Friday.

This cash flow gap kills more small businesses than competition, bad products, or economic downturns combined. The U.S. Small Business Administration estimates that 82% of small businesses fail due to cash flow problems. Not revenue problems — cash flow problems. They have the contracts. They have the clients. They just cannot survive the waiting.

Clearance was built to eliminate that waiting. We are an invoice factoring platform that advances up to 95% of an invoice's value within hours of submission. No multi-week underwriting process. No requirement to factor your entire receivables book. No long-term contracts. You pick the invoices you want to advance, one at a time or in batches, and we handle the rest.

Traditional factoring companies are built on information asymmetry and lock-in. Opaque fee structures, mandatory minimums, long-term contracts, and notification requirements that can damage client relationships. We built Clearance as the antidote: transparent per-invoice pricing displayed before you commit, no minimums, no contracts, and a confidential option where your clients never know you factored.

Our underwriting engine uses real-time business data — accounting software connections, payment history, and client creditworthiness — to make decisions in minutes instead of weeks. We believe that working capital should be as accessible as any other business tool, and that no business should suffocate while waiting for money it has already earned.
marketResearch:
The global invoice factoring market was valued at $3.1 trillion in 2024 and is expected to reach $4.6 trillion by 2030, growing at 6.8% CAGR. The SMB segment, specifically businesses with $500K-$50M in annual revenue, represents the fastest-growing sub-market as traditional banks continue tightening lending standards and fintech platforms lower access barriers.

The competitive landscape includes traditional factoring companies (BlueVine, Riviera Finance, TCI Capital), bank-affiliated programs (Wells Fargo Capital Finance, JPMorgan Chase Commercial), and newer fintech entrants (Fundbox, C2FO, and Prevail Capital). Traditional players typically require long-term contracts, full-book factoring, and notification to debtors. Clearance differentiates through single-invoice factoring with no contracts, confidential processing, and same-day funding — a combination that no major competitor currently offers at scale.

Our TAM encompasses US-based SMBs with outstanding receivables, roughly $1.2 trillion in annual factoring volume. Our SAM narrows to businesses with $1M-$30M in revenue across construction, professional services, staffing, and manufacturing — sectors with chronically long payment terms — representing approximately $180 billion. Our initial SOM targets QuickBooks- and Xero-connected businesses in construction and professional services, roughly $8 billion in near-term opportunity.

Distribution strategy combines direct partnerships with accounting software providers (in-app "advance this invoice" buttons), a content marketing engine targeting business owners searching for cash flow solutions, and referral relationships with bookkeepers and fractional CFOs who see cash flow problems firsthand.

name: Basis
tagline: The banking layer your product is missing
description: Basis is a banking-as-a-service API platform that lets any company embed financial features — accounts, cards, payments, and lending — directly into their product. One API, one compliance layer, full banking capabilities without a banking license.
mission:
Every SaaS platform eventually reaches a moment where its users need to move money. A property management tool needs to collect rent. A gig platform needs to pay workers instantly. A marketplace needs to hold escrow funds. And at that moment, every platform faces the same brutal realization: building financial features from scratch requires a banking license, a compliance team, a relationship with a sponsor bank, and twelve months of integration work.

Basis exists to collapse that timeline from years to weeks. We provide a single, well-documented API that gives any software company the ability to embed bank accounts, issue cards, process payments, and offer lending products directly within their existing product. Behind our API sits a complete compliance and regulatory layer — KYC/KYB verification, BSA/AML monitoring, FDIC insurance through our partner banks, and ongoing regulatory reporting — all managed by Basis so you do not have to.

We are not the first BaaS platform, but we are building for the next wave. Early BaaS players like Synapse collapsed under regulatory pressure. Others like Treasury Prime and Unit have strong products but require months of onboarding and custom integration. Basis was designed from the ground up for developer speed and regulatory durability. Our sandbox is live in five minutes. Our production onboarding takes two weeks, not six months. And our compliance infrastructure is built to withstand the heightened regulatory scrutiny that the entire BaaS industry now faces.

Our founding team includes a former OCC examiner, two ex-Plaid engineers, and a product leader from Marqeta. We understand both sides of the equation: the developers who need elegant APIs and the regulators who need bulletproof compliance. Basis is the bridge.

We envision a future where every software platform can offer financial services as naturally as they offer user authentication today. Banking should be a feature, not a separate app.
marketResearch:
The banking-as-a-service market is projected to reach $74 billion by 2030, growing at 17% CAGR. The embedded finance opportunity — financial features built into non-financial products — is even larger at an estimated $230 billion by 2030. The collapse of Synapse in 2024 and subsequent regulatory tightening has actually increased demand for well-capitalized, compliance-first BaaS providers.

Key competitors include Unit (strong API, compliance-focused, but slow onboarding and high minimums), Treasury Prime (established bank partnerships but enterprise-only), Solid (developer-friendly but limited product breadth), and Bond (card issuing focus). Legacy payment processors like Stripe Treasury and Adyen Platforms offer partial solutions but lack full banking capabilities. Basis differentiates through a combination of developer experience (sandbox in 5 minutes, production in 2 weeks), comprehensive product coverage (accounts, cards, ACH, wires, and lending through one API), and a compliance infrastructure specifically designed for the post-Synapse regulatory environment.

Our TAM encompasses all software platforms that could benefit from embedded finance, approximately $74 billion. Our SAM focuses on US-based vertical SaaS platforms, marketplaces, and gig economy companies with 10K+ end users, representing roughly $12 billion. Our initial SOM targets Series A-C vertical SaaS companies in property management, healthcare, and professional services — markets where money movement is core to the workflow — approximately $1.5 billion.

Go-to-market is developer-first: comprehensive documentation, a free sandbox tier, and an active presence in engineering communities. We convert to revenue through usage-based pricing (per account, per transaction) that scales with our customers' growth.

name: Splitwise Pro
tagline: Team expenses, split fairly, settled instantly
description: Splitwise Pro is an expense splitting and reimbursement platform purpose-built for remote and distributed teams. From team dinners and conference travel to shared software subscriptions, it tracks who owes what, settles balances automatically, and integrates with your company's expense policy.
mission:
Remote work solved a lot of problems. It also created a new one that nobody talks about enough: how do distributed teams handle shared expenses? When five people go to a team offsite and someone puts the Airbnb on their personal card, the resulting chain of Venmo requests, Slack messages, and forgotten reimbursements creates friction that compounds over time.

Splitwise Pro was born from this exact frustration. Our co-founders ran a 40-person remote company and watched their team spend hours every month chasing expense splits, submitting reimbursement requests, and reconciling who owed what from the last team dinner. The consumer version of expense-splitting apps got them halfway there, but none were built for the workplace context — where expense policies, corporate cards, tax implications, and manager approvals add layers of complexity.

We built Splitwise Pro to handle all of it. Create a group for any shared expense scenario — offsite travel, team meals, conference attendance, shared subscriptions. Add expenses naturally by snapping receipts or forwarding email confirmations. The platform calculates optimal splits (equal, proportional, or custom), routes approval requests according to your company's expense policy, and settles balances through direct deposit or corporate card credits.

What makes us different is not just the splitting — it is the settlement. Other tools tell you who owes what and then leave you to figure out the Venmo dance. Splitwise Pro actually moves the money, integrates with your payroll provider to add reimbursements to the next pay cycle, and generates the accounting entries your finance team needs. End to end, no loose threads.
marketResearch:
The expense management market is valued at $7.5 billion in 2025, projected to reach $14.2 billion by 2030. Within this, the team expense splitting niche — distinct from traditional individual expense reporting — is an emerging category driven by the rise of remote and distributed workforces. An estimated 35% of US workers operate in hybrid or fully remote arrangements, creating over 50 million potential users for team expense tools.

Competitors include Splitwise (consumer app with 100M+ users, no enterprise features), Expensify (enterprise expense management but no group splitting), Brex (corporate cards with spend management but not designed for peer-to-peer splits), and Ramp (excellent corporate card product but focused on top-down expense control, not bottom-up team splitting). Splitwise Pro occupies the whitespace between consumer splitting apps and enterprise expense management — purpose-built for the group expense scenarios that remote teams face weekly.

Our SAM targets remote and hybrid companies with 20-500 employees in the US, UK, and EU who regularly incur shared team expenses, representing approximately $1.2 billion. Our initial SOM focuses on remote-first tech companies in the 50-200 employee range, roughly $150M in near-term opportunity.

Go-to-market strategy combines a freemium model (free for teams under 10), integration partnerships with popular remote team tools (Slack, Notion, Gusto), and a content strategy targeting operations managers and team leads who manage offsite budgets. Viral adoption is built into the product: when one person creates a split, everyone involved joins the platform.

name: Ironclad Pay
tagline: Payment processing where fraud goes to die
description: Ironclad Pay is a payment processing platform built from the ground up around fraud prevention. Every transaction passes through a multi-layered detection engine that stops fraud before it clears — without adding friction for legitimate customers. Built for e-commerce merchants losing sleep over chargebacks.
mission:
Online fraud is a $48 billion problem, and it is getting worse. Every year, attack vectors become more sophisticated. Synthetic identities pass KYC checks. Stolen card credentials are tested against thousands of merchants simultaneously. Friendly fraud chargebacks eat into margins. And the merchants — especially mid-market e-commerce businesses doing $5M-$200M in annual GMV — bear the brunt of it.

The existing solutions force merchants into an impossible choice: block aggressively and lose legitimate customers, or accept more risk and eat the chargebacks. Fraud prevention has been bolted onto payment processing as an afterthought — a third-party integration that adds latency, complexity, and cost without fundamentally solving the problem.

Ironclad Pay takes a different approach. We built fraud detection into the payment processing layer itself, not on top of it. Every transaction is evaluated by our multi-signal engine that analyzes device fingerprints, behavioral biometrics, network patterns, and transaction history in under 100 milliseconds. Legitimate customers experience zero additional friction. Fraudulent transactions are blocked before they clear, not disputed after the fact.

Our founding team includes the former head of fraud at a top-five US payment processor, a machine learning engineer who built anomaly detection systems at Palantir, and a payments infrastructure veteran from Adyen. We have seen the fraud problem from every angle — processor, merchant, and issuer — and we built Ironclad Pay to solve it holistically.

Our vision is simple but ambitious: a world where accepting online payments does not require accepting online fraud. Where every merchant, regardless of size, has access to the same caliber of fraud prevention that was previously reserved for the world's largest retailers.
marketResearch:
The global payment fraud detection and prevention market reached $32 billion in 2025 and is projected to grow to $62 billion by 2030 at 14% CAGR. E-commerce fraud losses alone exceeded $48 billion in 2024, with mid-market merchants suffering disproportionately due to limited fraud prevention resources. The average chargeback rate for mid-market e-commerce is 0.6-1.2%, translating to hundreds of thousands in lost revenue annually.

Competitors fall into two categories: standalone fraud prevention tools (Forter, Signifyd, Riskified) that sit on top of existing processors, and payment processors with built-in fraud features (Stripe Radar, Adyen Risk, Checkout.com). Standalone tools add latency and cost ($0.05-$0.10 per transaction plus chargeback guarantees), while built-in processor tools are typically basic rule-based systems. Ironclad Pay is the first to deeply integrate ML-powered fraud detection into the payment rail itself, eliminating the latency penalty while delivering detection accuracy that rivals standalone specialists.

Our SAM targets US and European e-commerce merchants processing $5M-$500M in annual GMV, representing approximately $4.8 billion in payment processing and fraud prevention spend. Our initial SOM focuses on DTC e-commerce brands in fashion, electronics, and luxury goods — categories with the highest fraud rates — roughly $800M in near-term opportunity.

Go-to-market leverages the pain of chargeback costs: we offer a chargeback rate guarantee and charge a blended processing fee that is competitive with Stripe while including fraud prevention that would otherwise cost extra. Merchants adopt because the total cost of payments decreases, not increases.

name: Numera
tagline: Financial models for founders who think in products, not spreadsheets
description: Numera is a financial modeling platform built for non-finance founders. It replaces the intimidating blank spreadsheet with guided, interactive models that help early-stage founders build investor-ready projections, understand their unit economics, and make better capital allocation decisions.
mission:
Here is a truth that nobody in venture capital wants to admit: most early-stage financial models are fiction. Not because founders are dishonest, but because they are forced to express their business intuition in a medium they do not understand. A brilliant product founder who can articulate exactly why their users will grow and how their margins will expand gets handed a blank Google Sheet and told to "build a three-year model." The result is a spreadsheet full of made-up numbers that satisfies nobody.

Numera was created to fix this disconnect. We believe that financial modeling should start with the business, not the spreadsheet. Our platform asks founders the questions they actually know the answers to: How much does it cost to acquire a customer? How long do they stay? What is your average contract value? Then it builds the model — revenue projections, cash flow forecasts, headcount plans, and runway calculations — using established SaaS and e-commerce frameworks that investors actually trust.

But Numera is not a template. It is an interactive modeling environment where founders can explore scenarios by adjusting the inputs they understand. "What if we increase prices 20% but churn goes up 5%?" "What if we hire three engineers instead of two sales reps?" "What happens to runway if revenue growth slows from 15% to 8% monthly?" These questions get instant visual answers, not another hour in a spreadsheet.

Our founding team spent years watching the gap between great founders and great financial communication destroy fundraising outcomes. A seed-stage CEO should not need a fractional CFO to build a model that makes sense. Numera is the tool that makes financial literacy accessible without requiring financial expertise.

The future we are building is one where every founder — technical or non-technical, finance background or not — can confidently walk into an investor meeting understanding their numbers inside out, because they built their model by thinking about their business rather than fighting a spreadsheet.
marketResearch:
The financial planning and analysis software market is valued at $8.3 billion globally, but the vast majority of that spend is enterprise-focused (Anaplan, Adaptive Planning, Vena). The early-stage founder segment — companies pre-Series B with limited finance headcount — is dramatically underserved. An estimated 1.5 million startups are founded annually in the US alone, and virtually all need financial models for fundraising, yet no purpose-built tool exists for non-finance founders.

Competitors include generic spreadsheet tools (Google Sheets, Excel — the default, but intimidating and error-prone), financial model templates (Slidebean, Coda templates — better starting points but still require spreadsheet proficiency), fractional CFO services ($3K-$10K/month — excellent but expensive), and emerging tools like Caena and Pry (which was acquired by Brex but focused on post-revenue companies). Numera differentiates by targeting pre-revenue to early-revenue founders with a guided, conversational interface that does not require spreadsheet skills.

Our TAM encompasses all early-stage startups globally that need financial models, approximately $2.4 billion. Our SAM focuses on English-speaking founders in the US, UK, and Canada at pre-seed through Series A, representing roughly $400 million. Our initial SOM targets founders active in accelerator programs (Y Combinator, Techstars, 500 Global) and startup communities, approximately $60 million.

Go-to-market centers on accelerator partnerships (offering Numera as the standard modeling tool for cohort companies), content marketing around fundraising financial models, and integrations with cap table tools (Carta, Pulley) and banking platforms (Mercury, Brex) where founders already manage their finances.

name: Denari
tagline: One payroll run. Every currency. Every country.
description: Denari is a multi-currency payroll platform for distributed teams. Pay employees and contractors in 80+ countries in their local currency, with automated tax compliance, benefits administration, and real-time FX rates — all from a single dashboard.
mission:
The way companies pay people has not caught up with the way companies hire people. A 50-person startup might have engineers in Poland, designers in Argentina, a marketing lead in Nigeria, and customer success in the Philippines. Each of those countries has different tax codes, labor laws, mandatory benefits, and payment rails. Today, paying that team means juggling three or four vendors, maintaining separate payroll calendars, and accepting FX markups that quietly eat 3-5% of every international payment.

Denari was founded because we lived this problem. Our CEO ran payroll for a 120-person distributed team across 22 countries and spent more time on payroll operations than on product strategy. The tools that existed were either enterprise-grade solutions with six-figure minimums and months of onboarding, or patchwork combinations of contractor platforms and wire transfers that created compliance blind spots.

We are building the payroll infrastructure that the distributed workforce deserves. One platform where you can pay full-time employees in Germany (with proper social security contributions), contractors in Brazil (with compliant service agreements), and freelancers in India (with TDS handling) — all in a single payroll run. Every payment goes out in local currency at wholesale FX rates. Every tax obligation is calculated and filed automatically. Every worker gets a payslip in their language.

Denari is not just about moving money across borders. It is about making distributed teams operationally viable for companies that are not large enough to have a global payroll department. We handle employer-of-record services in countries where you do not have an entity, and we integrate with your existing HR and accounting stack so payroll does not become another silo.

Our long-term vision is a world where hiring the best person for the job is never constrained by where they live, because paying them correctly is as simple as adding them to your Denari dashboard.
marketResearch:
The global payroll outsourcing market is valued at $24.6 billion in 2025, with the multi-country payroll segment growing at 18% CAGR as distributed work becomes the norm. The specific intersection of multi-currency payroll and employer-of-record services represents a $9.2 billion TAM, driven by the 40% increase in cross-border hiring since 2020.

Key competitors include Deel (dominant player with $500M+ ARR, strong brand but increasingly complex pricing), Remote.com (well-funded, strong EOR capabilities but limited payroll customization), Papaya Global ($250M+ raised, enterprise-focused with complex onboarding), and Rippling (expanding internationally but primarily a US-centric HRIS). Traditional global payroll providers like ADP GlobalView and Safeguard Global serve enterprise but require six-figure annual commitments. Denari differentiates through transparent per-employee pricing ($49-$99/employee/month with no hidden FX markup beyond 0.5%), a purpose-built dashboard for companies with 10-500 international workers, and an onboarding process that takes days rather than months.

Our SAM targets venture-backed startups and mid-market tech companies in the US, UK, and EU with 10-500 employees across multiple countries, representing approximately $3.1 billion. Our initial SOM focuses on US-headquartered remote-first tech companies hiring in Latin America, Eastern Europe, and South/Southeast Asia — roughly $450M in near-term opportunity.

Go-to-market combines partnerships with remote work communities and publications (Remote OK, We Work Remotely, Running Remote), integration partnerships with HRIS platforms (BambooHR, Gusto, Personio), and content marketing targeting heads of people operations at scaling startups. Our free trial lets companies run their first international payroll at no cost.

name: Vessel
tagline: Know what's happening inside you before symptoms show up
description: Vessel is an at-home blood biomarker testing platform that makes preventive health accessible. Users collect a finger-prick sample, mail it in, and receive clinician-reviewed results with actionable wellness plans within 48 hours. No lab visit. No guessing.
mission:
Modern medicine is built around treating sickness, not maintaining health. By the time you feel symptoms, the underlying issue has often been progressing for months or years. Blood biomarkers tell a different story — they reveal metabolic shifts, nutrient deficiencies, hormonal imbalances, and inflammatory markers long before you'd ever think to see a doctor.

Vessel was founded on a conviction that blood testing should be as routine as checking your phone. Not an annual event gatekept by insurance codes and 6-week appointment waits, but a regular practice you do from your kitchen table. We've engineered a clinical-grade dried blood spot collection kit that captures over 40 biomarkers from a single finger prick, processed in our CLIA-certified partner labs with the same rigor as a hospital draw.

But data without context is just noise. Every Vessel report is reviewed by a licensed clinician who translates your numbers into plain language — what's optimal, what needs attention, and what to do about it. We pair results with personalized nutrition, supplement, and lifestyle recommendations that evolve as your biomarkers change over time.

We believe preventive health shouldn't be a luxury reserved for biohackers and concierge medicine patients. Our pricing starts lower than a single copay, and our longitudinal tracking means each test builds on the last, creating a biological timeline that gets smarter the longer you use it.

The healthcare system won't fix prevention. It's not designed to. Vessel is building the infrastructure for a world where understanding your own biology is effortless, affordable, and empowering.

The competitive landscape includes Everlywell (broad DTC testing, brand awareness but limited longitudinal tracking), InsideTracker (strong science but premium pricing excludes most consumers), and Quest/Labcorp's DTC arms (clinical credibility but terrible UX). Vessel differentiates through three axes: a genuinely painless collection experience with dried blood spot technology, longitudinal tracking that surfaces trends across tests, and clinician-reviewed reports at a price point 60% below InsideTracker.

Our GTM motion is subscription-first. Users start with a comprehensive baseline panel ($79), then subscribe to quarterly monitoring ($49/test). Retention is strong because each test adds context to previous results. B2B channels include employer wellness programs and health coaches who white-label our testing under their practice.

name: Meadow
tagline: Menopause care designed by women who've been there
description: Meadow is a comprehensive menopause care platform combining board-certified menopause specialists, evidence-based treatment plans, and a supportive community. From perimenopause through postmenopause, Meadow provides personalized hormonal and non-hormonal interventions, symptom tracking, and ongoing clinical guidance.
mission:
Menopause affects every woman who lives long enough to experience it — roughly 1.3 billion worldwide by 2030. Yet it remains one of the most undertreated, under-researched, and poorly understood transitions in medicine. The average woman sees three doctors before getting adequate menopause care. Many never do.

Meadow exists because this is unacceptable. We've built a clinical platform purpose-designed for menopause — not a general telehealth service that treats it as an afterthought. Every provider on our platform is a board-certified menopause specialist. Every treatment protocol reflects the latest evidence, not the outdated fear-based guidance that still dominates primary care.

We meet women where they are. Whether you're experiencing your first hot flash at 43 or navigating bone density concerns at 58, Meadow creates a personalized care plan that considers your complete health picture — hormonal therapy when appropriate, non-hormonal alternatives when preferred, and lifestyle interventions that actually move the needle.

But clinical care is only half the equation. Menopause is isolating in a way that few health transitions are. Friends don't talk about it. Partners don't understand it. Meadow's community brings together women at every stage — sharing experiences, asking questions, and proving that this transition can be powerful rather than diminishing.

We're building the menopause care infrastructure that should have existed decades ago. Not incremental improvement, but a fundamental reimagining of how women experience this chapter of their health.

tagline: Sleep isn't rest. It's engineering.
description: Kairos is a precision sleep optimization platform that combines clinical-grade sleep diagnostics, circadian rhythm analysis, and personalized intervention protocols. Using data from wearables, environmental sensors, and validated questionnaires, Kairos builds a sleep architecture profile and delivers evidence-based protocols to optimize each stage of sleep.
mission:
We spend a third of our lives asleep, yet treat it as dead time. The sleep industry is split between two extremes: consumer gadgets that count hours without understanding physiology, and clinical sleep labs that are expensive, inconvenient, and designed to diagnose disorders rather than optimize performance.

Kairos bridges that gap. We're building a precision sleep platform grounded in chronobiology — the science of how biological rhythms govern every system in your body. Your sleep architecture isn't random. It follows patterns shaped by your genetics, light exposure, meal timing, stress physiology, and circadian chronotype. Understanding these patterns is the key to sleeping better, not just longer.

Our platform ingests data from the devices you already wear — Oura, Whoop, Apple Watch — and layers in environmental data from our optional bedroom sensor. We analyze sleep staging, HRV patterns, respiratory metrics, and room conditions to build a comprehensive sleep architecture profile. Then we deliver personalized protocols: light exposure timing, temperature adjustments, supplement stacking, breathwork sequences, and meal timing windows calibrated to your unique circadian profile.

We don't believe in one-size-fits-all sleep hygiene tips. The person who naturally peaks at 10pm needs fundamentally different interventions than the person who's sharpest at 6am. Kairos makes that distinction and builds around it.

Our team includes sleep researchers from Stanford's Sleep Epidemiology Research Center, circadian biologists, and engineers obsessed with the intersection of data and human performance. We're here to turn sleep from a mystery into a controllable variable.

mission:
Plant-based eating is surging, but nutritional literacy hasn't kept pace. Millions of people are cutting out animal products for ethical, environmental, or health reasons, only to discover that avoiding deficiency is harder than Instagram makes it look. description: Solace is a therapy matching platform designed specifically for grief and loss. When someone experiences a significant loss, the last thing they should have to do is become a project manager for their own healing. Yet that's exactly what the mental health system demands: search directories, make cold calls, explain your story to voicemails, wait weeks for intake appointments, and hope the therapist you finally see actually understands grief beyond the five stages model that was never meant to be prescriptive.
