Our matching algorithm considers dimensions that generic directories ignore: the type of loss (partner, child, parent, pregnancy, suicide, ambiguous loss), the griever's cultural and spiritual framework, their attachment style, whether they prefer structured or open-ended therapy, and whether they need someone who's experienced a similar loss themselves.

We believe that grief therapy is not general therapy with a sad topic. It requires specialized training — in complicated grief, disenfranchised grief, meaning reconstruction, and continuing bonds. Every therapist on Solace has completed advanced bereavement training and dedicates at least 50% of their practice to grief work. We don't just check a box on a directory. We verify depth of specialization.

Beyond matching, Solace provides continuity. Grief doesn't resolve in 12 sessions. It resurfaces at anniversaries, holidays, and unexpected moments years later. Our platform maintains your therapeutic relationship and makes it easy to return when you need support again — even after a long gap.

Loss is universal. Good grief care shouldn't be a matter of luck.

name: Kinetic
tagline: Your phone is your physical therapist's eyes between visits
description: Kinetic uses smartphone camera-based motion tracking to monitor physical therapy exercise form, count reps, measure range of motion, and report adherence to care providers. No wearables, no special equipment — just the phone patients already have.
mission:
Physical therapy has an adherence crisis. Studies consistently show that only 35% of PT patients complete their prescribed home exercise programs. The result: slower recovery, repeated injuries, unnecessary surgeries, and billions in avoidable healthcare spending. The core problem isn't motivation — it's that patients go home with a printout of stick figures and no feedback on whether they're doing the exercises correctly.

Kinetic turns any smartphone camera into a real-time exercise coach. Using computer vision and pose estimation, our app tracks joint angles, movement speed, range of motion, and form quality as patients perform their prescribed exercises at home. Reps are counted automatically. Form deviations trigger gentle corrections. Progress is logged and shared with the prescribing PT in real time.

But we're not replacing physical therapists — we're extending their reach. Kinetic gives PTs visibility into what happens between visits, replacing the unreliable 'How did your exercises go this week?' with actual data: adherence rates, range of motion trends, and flagged form issues that need attention. Clinicians can adjust programs remotely based on objective progress data instead of patient self-report.

Our founding team includes a sports medicine physician, a computer vision researcher, and physical therapists who saw firsthand how much clinical value was being lost in the gap between visits. We believe the phone in every patient's pocket is the most powerful rehab tool nobody's using.

The goal isn't to make physical therapy virtual. It's to make home exercises actually work.

Patients download the free app. Clinics pay $199/month per clinician for the provider dashboard, adherence analytics, and EHR integration. Enterprise contracts with health systems and payers add remote therapeutic monitoring (RTM) billing support, which creates a direct reimbursement pathway for providers using the platform.

name: Bloom
tagline: What's growing inside you matters more than what you eat
description: Bloom is a gut microbiome testing and personalized meal planning platform. Using shotgun metagenomic sequencing, Bloom maps the bacterial species in your gut and creates meal plans designed to cultivate a healthier microbiome — reducing inflammation, improving digestion, and supporting immune function through food, not pills.
mission:
The gut microbiome is arguably the most important organ system that medicine still barely understands in clinical practice. Research has linked microbiome composition to everything from autoimmune disease and depression to metabolic health and cancer treatment response. Yet when a patient presents with IBS, bloating, fatigue, or skin issues, the standard medical response hasn't changed in decades: try elimination diets, take a probiotic, see if it helps.

Bloom is building the bridge between microbiome science and everyday nutrition. We use shotgun metagenomic sequencing — not the cheaper 16S rRNA method — to identify bacterial species in your gut at strain-level resolution. This matters because two people might both have Lactobacillus, but at different strains with completely different functional roles.

From your microbiome profile, we generate a personalized meal plan designed to shift your gut composition toward a healthier state. Not through restrictive elimination or expensive supplements, but through strategic inclusion of prebiotic fibers, fermented foods, and polyphenol-rich ingredients that feed the specific beneficial species your gut needs more of — and starve the inflammatory ones you have too much of.

Our science team includes microbiome researchers from the Human Microbiome Project, registered dietitians, and food scientists who translate genomic data into recipes you'll actually want to cook. We believe the gap between cutting-edge microbiome research and patient benefit can be closed with better technology and better food.

The gut isn't just a digestive organ. It's a garden. Bloom helps you grow the right things.

Bloom differentiates by being food-first — we don't sell supplements as the primary intervention. Our meal plans are clinically designed to reshape the microbiome through dietary fiber diversity, fermented food integration, and strategic polyphenol intake.

GTM combines DTC acquisition through gut-health content marketing with partnerships with functional medicine practitioners and registered dietitians who want to incorporate microbiome data into their nutrition counseling. name: Aegis
tagline: Rare disease patients deserve more than rare options
description: Aegis is a clinical trial matching platform for patients with rare diseases. By integrating electronic health records, genetic test results, and a comprehensive global trial database, Aegis identifies eligible clinical trials that patients and their physicians would otherwise never find — reducing the average rare disease diagnostic odyssey from 7 years of searching to days of matching.
mission:
There are over 7,000 known rare diseases affecting roughly 400 million people worldwide. For most, there is no FDA-approved treatment. Clinical trials represent the only path to potential therapy, yet fewer than 5% of rare disease patients ever participate in one. The reason isn't lack of trials — it's that patients can't find them, and trials can't find patients.

Aegis exists to solve the matching problem. A parent with a child diagnosed with a rare mitochondrial disorder shouldn't need to become a medical researcher to discover that a Phase II trial at a hospital 200 miles away is enrolling patients with exactly their child's genetic mutation. Yet that's the reality today — trial recruitment relies on physician awareness (which is spotty), ClinicalTrials.gov (which is impenetrable for non-experts), and patient advocacy groups (which are fragmented).

Our platform ingests patient health records, genetic test results, and diagnosis codes, and matches them against a continuously updated global database of rare disease clinical trials. We understand the nuanced eligibility criteria that make rare disease trials uniquely complex: specific genetic variants, biomarker thresholds, prior treatment history, and geographic constraints. Our matching engine doesn't just find trials — it pre-qualifies patients against inclusion and exclusion criteria, dramatically reducing the back-and-forth that delays enrollment.

For pharmaceutical sponsors, Aegis solves the existential challenge of rare disease drug development: finding enough patients. We partner with biotech companies running rare disease trials to accelerate enrollment timelines that often stretch years beyond projections, threatening the viability of programs that could bring life-changing therapies to patients with no other options.

Every rare disease patient is searching for hope. Many clinical trials are searching for patients. Aegis connects the two.
marketResearch:
The rare disease drug development market exceeds $209B in annual revenue, with the clinical trial recruitment segment valued at $2.1B. Rare disease trials face the most acute recruitment challenges in pharma — the average rare disease trial takes 2.5x longer to enroll than common disease trials, and 80% fail to meet enrollment timelines. This delays treatments, increases costs, and in many cases kills programs that would otherwise succeed.

Aegis's SAM targets pharmaceutical and biotech companies sponsoring rare disease clinical trials (approximately 2,800 active trials globally), representing $1.4B in recruitment spend. Our SOM focuses on US-based sponsors and CROs running Phase I-III rare disease trials, roughly $350M.

Competitors include TrialSpark (general trial matching, not rare-disease specialized), Antidote Technologies (patient matching, acquired by Precision Medicine Group), Clinical Trial GPS (physician-facing, limited patient engagement), and disease-specific registries (fragmented, single-disease). Aegis differentiates through rare disease specialization — our matching engine handles the genetic variant-level specificity that general platforms miss, and our patient-facing tools are designed for the unique complexity of rare disease populations.

GTM is dual-sided. Patient acquisition comes through partnerships with rare disease advocacy organizations (NORD, Global Genes, disease-specific foundations) and genetic testing companies who can surface matching opportunities at the point of diagnosis. Sponsor revenue comes from per-trial matching fees ($50K-200K depending on disease prevalence) and enrollment success bonuses. We've launched with partnerships covering 14 rare disease indications.

name: Primer
tagline: Where numbers come alive for curious kids
description: Primer is a visual math learning platform for children ages 6-12 that transforms abstract concepts into interactive, colorful adventures. Kids don't just memorize formulas — they discover mathematical thinking through play, puzzles, and stories that make every concept stick.
mission:
Most children don't hate math. They hate feeling lost. The moment a kid falls behind — misses a concept, gets confused by notation, or simply zones out during a lecture — math becomes a wall instead of a window. And traditional approaches respond with more worksheets, more drilling, more of exactly what made them disengage in the first place.

Primer was built by a team of former math teachers, game designers, and child psychologists who believe that mathematical thinking is as natural to children as language. Watch any five-year-old sort their Halloween candy or argue about who got the bigger slice of pizza — they're already doing math. The problem isn't ability, it's presentation.

Our platform turns every math concept into something you can see, touch, and play with. Fractions become pizza slices you actually divide. Multiplication becomes building blocks you stack into arrays. Geometry becomes treasure maps you navigate. Every interaction is designed around the way children's brains actually process spatial and numerical information — through pattern recognition, visual reasoning, and narrative context.

We work alongside school curricula rather than replacing them. Teachers assign Primer as practice and exploration, and our dashboard shows them exactly which concepts each student has internalized and which need more time. Parents see their kids asking to do math before bed — not because we've gamified it with hollow rewards, but because we've made it genuinely fascinating.

Our north star is a generation of kids who see math not as a subject to survive, but as a superpower to wield. Every child deserves to feel the thrill of a pattern clicking into place.
marketResearch:
The K-12 edtech market reached $28 billion in 2025 and is projected to grow at 16% CAGR through 2030. Within this, math-specific learning platforms represent approximately $5.2 billion, driven by persistent achievement gaps — only 36% of U.S. fourth graders tested proficient in math on the 2024 NAEP assessment. Our SAM of $1.8 billion focuses on supplemental math tools for elementary students in English-speaking markets. Our initial SOM targets U.S. households with children 6-12 and progressive elementary schools, representing roughly $240 million.

The competitive landscape includes established players like Khan Academy Kids (free, broad but not math-focused), Prodigy Math (game-based but relies on extrinsic rewards over genuine understanding), and DreamBox (adaptive but visually dated and enterprise-focused). Newer entrants like Photomath focus on homework help rather than conceptual understanding. Primer differentiates through its visual-first pedagogy — every concept is taught through spatial manipulation and interactive models rather than video lectures or drill-and-kill exercises.

Our primary customer segments are parents of elementary-age children seeking engaging math support (average willingness to pay $12-20/month for educational apps) and elementary schools looking to supplement core curricula with adaptive practice tools. The parental anxiety around math achievement creates strong demand — 78% of parents report concern about their child's math preparation.

Our GTM motion combines organic virality (kids sharing progress with classmates) with targeted digital advertising to parents of 6-8 year olds during back-to-school and report card seasons. School adoption follows a teacher-champion model: free classroom accounts convert to district licenses when principals see engagement data.

name: Fluent
tagline: Talk your way to fluency with AI conversation partners
description: Fluent pairs language learners with AI conversation partners that adapt to their level, interests, and goals. Instead of memorizing vocabulary lists, learners practice real dialogue — ordering coffee in Paris, negotiating in Mandarin, or debating philosophy in German.
mission:
The language learning industry has a dirty secret: most people who complete a course still can't hold a conversation. They can conjugate verbs on paper but freeze when a taxi driver asks where they're going. The gap between classroom knowledge and real-world fluency is enormous, and traditional apps have made it worse by optimizing for streak counts instead of speaking confidence.

Fluent exists because the only way to learn to speak is to speak. Our AI conversation partners simulate the messy, unpredictable, context-rich experience of talking to a real person — complete with slang, cultural nuances, and the occasional misunderstanding. They're patient when you struggle, challenging when you're ready, and always available at 3am when insomnia and ambition collide.

What makes our approach different from a chatbot is depth. Each AI partner has a persona, a backstory, and opinions. You're not practicing with a translation engine — you're having coffee with Sophia, a Roman architect who is passionate about urban design and will absolutely correct your subjunctive. The emotional engagement of genuine conversation is what makes language stick.

We build on decades of second-language acquisition research showing that comprehensible input — language slightly above the learner's current level — drives fluency faster than any other method. Our AI calibrates every response to sit in that sweet spot, pushing learners just enough to grow without overwhelming them into silence.

Our vision is a world where anyone can become conversationally fluent in a new language within six months, without ever booking a flight or finding a conversation partner. The technology is finally here. We're making it accessible.
marketResearch:
The global language learning market hit $67 billion in 2025, growing at 18% CAGR. Digital language learning specifically represents $22 billion, with mobile-first platforms dominating consumer spend. The AI-powered conversation practice segment is nascent but growing rapidly as LLM capabilities improve. Our TAM is $22 billion in digital language learning, SAM is $6.5 billion targeting adults learning the top 10 global languages via mobile apps, and our initial SOM is $350 million focused on English speakers learning Spanish, French, German, Japanese, and Mandarin.

Duolingo dominates with 100M+ monthly active users but is widely criticized for producing learners who can match pictures to words but struggle in real conversations. Babbel and Rosetta Stone offer more structured curricula but lack adaptive conversation practice. Italki and Preply connect learners with human tutors at $15-40/hour — effective but expensive and scheduling-dependent. Fluent occupies the gap: conversation-first practice at app pricing, available 24/7.

Our target users are motivated adults (25-45) learning a language for career advancement, travel, or personal enrichment. This demographic spends an average of $180/year on language learning and values speaking ability over test scores. Secondary segments include expatriates needing rapid functional fluency and professionals preparing for international roles.

GTM strategy starts with a freemium app offering 3 free conversations daily, converting to $16/month for unlimited practice and advanced personas. Viral growth comes from shareable conversation highlights and a referral program offering bonus conversation credits. B2B expansion targets corporate language training programs, replacing expensive tutor-based programs with scalable AI practice.

name: Meridian
tagline: The management training your company forgot to give you
description: Meridian is a leadership development platform designed specifically for first-time managers. Through cohort-based programs, 1-on-1 AI coaching, and real-world practice exercises, new managers learn to lead teams with confidence instead of faking it until they break.
mission:
Every year, millions of talented individual contributors get promoted into management with virtually no preparation. One day you're writing code or closing deals, and the next you're responsible for other people's careers, performance reviews, and emotional well-being. The assumption is that being great at your job means you'll be great at managing others. This assumption is catastrophically wrong.

Meridian was founded by three first-time managers who learned leadership the hard way — through painful feedback, lost team members, and years of trial and error that could have been compressed into months with the right guidance. We're building the training program we wish had existed on the day we first heard the words "you're the new team lead."

Our curriculum is ruthlessly practical. We don't teach leadership theory or make people read case studies about Jack Welch. We teach the specific, tactical skills that first-time managers need in their first 90 days: how to run a productive one-on-one, how to give feedback that doesn't destroy trust, how to manage someone who was your peer yesterday, how to have the performance conversation you've been dreading.

Every lesson comes with a practice exercise that managers complete with their actual team. Learn about effective delegation on Tuesday, practice it with a real project on Wednesday, debrief with your cohort on Thursday. The learning loop is tight, contextual, and immediately applicable.

We believe that good management is the single highest-leverage investment a company can make. One great manager affects eight to twelve people every single day. We're here to create more of them, faster.

name: Chalk
tagline: Flashcards that write themselves, schedules that actually work
description: Chalk is a spaced repetition platform that uses AI to generate high-quality flashcards from any source material — lecture notes, textbooks, PDFs, or even YouTube videos. Combined with a scientifically-optimized review schedule, Chalk ensures you remember everything you study.
mission:
Every student knows they should use flashcards and spaced repetition. The research is overwhelming — it's the most effective memorization technique ever studied. And yet most students don't use it, or they start and quit within a week. The reason is simple: creating good flashcards is tedious, and maintaining a review schedule requires discipline that vanishes during midterm season.

Chalk removes both barriers. Drop in your lecture slides, paste a textbook chapter, or link a YouTube lecture, and Chalk generates a complete flashcard deck in seconds — not just simple term-definition pairs, but cards that test understanding through cloze deletions, scenario questions, and conceptual connections. The AI doesn't just extract facts; it understands what's worth remembering and how to test for genuine comprehension.

Once your cards exist, Chalk's scheduling algorithm takes over. Built on a modernized version of the SM-2 algorithm enhanced with machine learning, it predicts exactly when you're about to forget each card and schedules a review at the optimal moment. Study ten minutes a day and retain months of material. The system learns your personal forgetting curves and adapts — everyone's memory works differently, and your schedule should too.

We're particularly focused on medical students, law students, and language learners — communities where the volume of memorization is immense and the stakes of forgetting are real. But the principles apply to anyone who needs knowledge to stick: certification preppers, professionals learning new domains, or curious people who are tired of reading books and remembering nothing.
marketResearch:
The digital flashcard and study tool market is valued at $3.8 billion, anchored by Quizlet's 60M monthly active users. The broader test prep and study aid market reaches $12 billion. Spaced repetition specifically is experiencing a renaissance driven by evidence-based learning advocates on social media and the growing demands of professional certification programs. Our TAM encompasses the $12 billion study tool market, SAM of $4.2 billion targets digital-first students and professionals in English-speaking markets, and SOM of $180 million focuses on medical students, law students, and IT certification preppers.

Quizlet dominates flashcards but lacks intelligent scheduling — reviews are random, not spaced. Anki is the gold standard for spaced repetition but has an interface from 2006 and requires manual card creation that takes longer than studying itself. RemNote and Mochi bridge the gap partially but lack AI card generation. Chalk is the first platform to combine Anki-grade scheduling algorithms with AI-powered card generation and a modern mobile-first interface.

Our primary users are medical students (1.1M in the U.S. alone, spending an average of $200/year on study tools), followed by law students, engineering students, and IT professionals pursuing certifications. These users face enormous memorization loads and are highly motivated to adopt evidence-based study methods. The medical student community in particular has a strong culture of tool-sharing, creating natural viral distribution.

GTM strategy leverages the study tool influencer ecosystem on YouTube and Reddit. We sponsor popular study-with-me creators and provide free premium accounts to student ambassadors. Organic growth comes from shared decks — when one med student creates a pharmacology deck, their entire class adopts Chalk to study it.

name: Orbit
tagline: A science experiment on your doorstep, every month
description: Orbit delivers monthly hands-on science experiment kits to kids ages 5-14, paired with a digital companion app that extends each experiment into deeper learning. From building volcanoes to growing crystals to coding simple robots, every box turns kitchens into laboratories.
mission:
Science education has a paradox. Kids are natural scientists — they ask why the sky is blue, how magnets work, and what would happen if you mixed everything under the kitchen sink. But by middle school, most of them think science is boring. Somewhere between their natural curiosity and the standardized curriculum, the magic gets squeezed out.

Orbit was created to protect that magic. Every month, we deliver a box that turns a kid's kitchen table into a laboratory. Inside is everything they need for a real experiment — not a craft project disguised as science, but a genuine investigation with a hypothesis, variables, and results that might actually surprise them. The baking soda volcano has its place, but we go further: kids extract DNA from strawberries, build simple circuits, grow bacterial cultures, and engineer bridges that hold real weight.

What makes Orbit different from other subscription boxes is the depth. Each kit comes with a companion app that extends the experiment into the underlying science. After building an electromagnet, kids explore how MRI machines use the same principles. After growing crystals, they learn how geologists study mineral formation. We connect the hands-on experience to the bigger scientific picture, building genuine understanding rather than just a fun afternoon.

We calibrate every kit for safety, mess tolerance, and adult involvement. A five-year-old can do most experiments with a parent nearby. A twelve-year-old can run them independently. The goal is autonomy — we want kids to feel like scientists, not like they're following instructions. Each kit includes open-ended extension challenges that push curious kids to design their own experiments.

Our dream is that every Orbit kid arrives at their first high school chemistry class already knowing what a hypothesis is, already comfortable with failure, and already hooked on the thrill of discovering something new.

KiwiCo is the dominant player with an estimated $200M+ in annual revenue across multiple age-segmented lines (Kiwi Crate, Tinker Crate, etc.). MEL Science focuses on chemistry with strong production quality but narrow scope. Little Passports covers geography rather than STEM. Orbit differentiates through the digital companion app that transforms a physical kit from a one-afternoon activity into weeks of extended learning, and through our focus on real scientific methodology rather than craft-oriented projects.

Our target customer is the "science-curious parent" — typically college-educated, household income above $80K, with children ages 5-10 as the primary entry point. These parents value educational enrichment and are willing to spend $25-40/month on quality STEM activities. Retention in subscription boxes averages 6-8 months; Orbit targets 10+ months by making each kit a building block that connects to previous experiments.

GTM strategy combines Instagram and YouTube influencer partnerships with targeted Facebook ads during gifting seasons (birthdays, holidays, back-to-school). Gift subscriptions represent 35% of initial purchases and convert to self-subscriptions at a 28% rate. School partnerships — where teachers recommend Orbit as supplemental home science — provide a trusted endorsement channel.

name: Folio
tagline: Assessment that showcases what students can actually do
description: Folio is a portfolio-based assessment platform for creative programs — design, art, writing, film, and architecture schools. Instead of reducing student work to letter grades, Folio lets students curate digital portfolios that demonstrate growth, process, and mastery to instructors and future employers.
mission:
Creative education has an assessment problem. You can't reduce a design thesis to a B+. You can't capture the evolution of a filmmaker's visual language in a percentage score. Yet most creative programs still rely on traditional grading systems that were designed for multiple-choice exams, forcing instructors to flatten nuanced, subjective evaluation into a number that tells students almost nothing about their growth.

Folio reimagines assessment for disciplines where the work is the evidence. Our platform lets students build living portfolios throughout their program — uploading projects, documenting process, reflecting on decisions, and receiving structured feedback from instructors and peers. Assessment happens through rubric-based evaluation directly on the portfolio, creating a rich record of growth that a transcript could never capture.

For instructors, Folio solves the logistics nightmare of creative assessment. Instead of juggling USB drives, email attachments, and physical submissions, everything lives in one platform with inline annotation tools, customizable rubrics, and cohort-wide analytics that reveal patterns in student development. Faculty spend less time on administration and more time on the mentorship that actually matters.

For students, the portfolio they build in Folio becomes a career asset. Graduating with a curated, feedback-annotated portfolio is infinitely more valuable than a GPA when applying for creative roles. Our industry partnerships let students share their Folio profiles directly with employers who are tired of evaluating candidates through resumes alone.

We started with design schools because the portfolio tradition is strongest there, but our vision extends to any discipline where showing your work matters more than answering questions about it.
marketResearch:
The educational assessment technology market is valued at $7.3 billion, but the vast majority serves standardized testing. Portfolio-based assessment tools represent a niche of approximately $800 million, growing at 28% CAGR as creative programs expand and competency-based education gains mainstream acceptance. Our TAM encompasses the $800 million portfolio assessment market, our SAM of $320 million targets post-secondary creative programs in North America and Europe, and our SOM of $45 million focuses on design, art, and architecture programs at accredited institutions.

Existing solutions include generic LMS platforms (Canvas, Blackboard) that treat portfolios as file uploads with no assessment workflow, Portfolium (acquired by Instructure, focused on career portfolios rather than formative assessment), and Seesaw (K-12 focused, lacks higher education features). Many programs use ad hoc solutions — Google Drive folders, WordPress sites, or physical exhibitions. Folio differentiates by integrating portfolio building, rubric-based assessment, peer review workflows, and industry-facing presentation into a single purpose-built platform.

Our primary buyers are department chairs and program directors at design schools, art colleges, architecture programs, and creative writing MFAs. There are approximately 2,400 accredited creative programs in the U.S. alone. Secondary buyers include K-12 districts adopting project-based learning that requires portfolio assessment. Average contract value is $8-15K per program annually.

GTM strategy targets the concentrated creative education community through conference sponsorships (AIGA, NASAD, CAA), partnerships with accreditation bodies that are increasingly requiring evidence-based assessment, and a faculty ambassador program. The pilot-to-adoption cycle in higher education averages 12-18 months, so we invest heavily in customer success during pilots to ensure department-wide rollout.

name: Beacon
tagline: New career. No lottery ticket required.
description: Beacon runs intensive career transition bootcamps for mid-career professionals. Unlike traditional bootcamps aimed at recent grads, Beacon's programs are designed around the constraints of working adults — family obligations, existing skills to leverage, and the need for income continuity during the transition.
mission:
Career transitions are terrifying. You've spent ten years building expertise in one field, and now the market has shifted, your industry is shrinking, or you've simply realized you want something different. The options feel binary: quit your job and burn through savings in a bootcamp designed for 22-year-olds, or stay stuck and let resentment build.

Beacon was founded by three people who made mid-career transitions themselves — a former journalist turned product manager, an accountant turned data scientist, and a teacher turned software engineer. We know the specific fears: Will anyone hire a 35-year-old junior developer? Can I afford to take a pay cut? Will my existing experience count for anything? The answers are yes, you probably won't have to, and absolutely — but only if the transition is designed around your reality, not a college sophomore's.

Our bootcamps are structured for working professionals. Evening and weekend cohorts. Twelve to sixteen weeks. Curriculum that explicitly bridges from what you already know to what you need to learn. A marketing manager learning data analytics isn't starting from zero — they already understand business context, stakeholder communication, and strategic thinking. We build on those strengths instead of ignoring them.

Every Beacon graduate enters the job market with more than just new technical skills. Our career placement team works with each person to reframe their career narrative — not as someone starting over, but as someone bringing a unique combination of domain expertise and new capabilities that no 22-year-old bootcamp grad can match.

We measure success not by enrollment numbers but by placement rates and salary outcomes. If our graduates don't land roles they're excited about at compensation that respects their experience, we haven't done our job.
marketResearch:
The professional reskilling and career transition market is valued at $32 billion globally, driven by AI-induced displacement, industry consolidation, and increasing career mobility expectations among millennials and Gen X. The bootcamp segment specifically represents $5.8 billion, but the vast majority targets early-career learners. The mid-career transition niche — professionals with 8+ years of experience seeking to change fields — is severely underserved despite representing the fastest-growing segment of career changers. Our TAM is $5.8 billion in bootcamps, SAM of $2.1 billion targets career-change bootcamps for experienced professionals, and SOM of $180 million focuses on U.S. professionals transitioning into tech-adjacent roles.

General Assembly and Flatiron School dominate traditional bootcamps but design for early-career learners — their pace, pedagogy, and career support don't account for mid-career constraints. Springboard and Thinkful offer flexible online programs but lack the cohort intensity and career narrative work that career changers need. Corporate reskilling programs (Coursera for Business, Udacity Enterprise) serve employers, not individuals making voluntary transitions. Beacon differentiates through its exclusive focus on experienced professionals, part-time schedule design, and career narrative coaching.

Our target learner is 30-45, has 8-15 years of professional experience, household income of $70-120K, and is seeking to transition into product management, data analytics, UX design, or software engineering. They need flexibility (can't quit their day job), credibility (want employer recognition), and confidence (need to believe their experience is an asset). Average willingness to pay is $6,000-12,000 per program.

GTM strategy combines SEO content targeting career transition queries ("how to switch careers at 35"), LinkedIn thought leadership from our founders' personal transition stories, and alumni referrals. Corporate partnerships with companies laying off workers provide a talent pipeline with employer-sponsored tuition.

name: Syllabus
tagline: Curriculum design tools that respect teachers' time and expertise
description: Syllabus is a curriculum design platform for K-12 teachers that streamlines lesson planning, standards alignment, and resource organization. Built by former teachers who understand that planning shouldn't take longer than teaching.
mission:
Teaching is one of the most intellectually demanding jobs on earth, and curriculum design is the invisible engine that makes it work. Great teachers spend hours every week crafting lessons, finding resources, aligning to standards, differentiating for diverse learners, and adjusting plans based on what actually happened in class. Yet the tools they're given for this work are shocking — most teachers still plan in Word documents, Google Docs, or printed binder pages.

Syllabus was built by a team of former classroom teachers who spent as many evenings planning lessons as we did teaching them. We experienced firsthand the absurdity of aligning a lesson to seventeen different standards by hand, the frustration of losing a great activity because it was buried in last year's Google Drive, and the guilt of using someone else's worksheet because we simply ran out of time to create something better.

Our platform brings curriculum design into the modern era. Teachers build lesson plans with drag-and-drop components — warm-ups, direct instruction, activities, assessments — that automatically align to state and national standards. A built-in resource library lets teachers save, tag, and search everything they've ever created or collected. AI assists with the tedious parts — generating differentiated versions of activities, suggesting formative assessment questions, and identifying gaps in standards coverage across a unit.

Critically, we don't try to replace teacher judgment. Syllabus is a power tool for skilled professionals, not a lesson-plan generator for anyone with a pulse. Teachers remain the architects. We just give them better blueprints, sharper tools, and a workspace that doesn't make them want to scream.

Our north star is giving teachers back five hours a week — time that goes back to their families, their health, or the creative lesson design that drew them to teaching in the first place.

Our TAM is $4.6 billion in K-12 teacher tools, SAM of $1.2 billion targets digital curriculum planning tools in English-speaking markets, and SOM of $85 million focuses on U.S. public school districts with 5,000+ students.

Current alternatives include Planbook (simple calendar-based planning, no AI or standards alignment), Teachers Pay Teachers (marketplace for resources, not a planning tool), and district-mandated curriculum platforms (rigid, top-down, despised by teachers). LMS platforms like Canvas and Schoology handle assignment distribution but not curriculum design. Syllabus differentiates by being the first platform that treats curriculum design as a professional practice — combining planning, standards alignment, resource management, and AI assistance in one workflow.

Our primary users are K-12 classroom teachers who take curriculum design seriously and are frustrated by inadequate tools. Early adopters are instructional coaches and curriculum coordinators who need to support teachers across a department or school. District-level buyers emerge when enough teachers within a district adopt Syllabus individually, creating bottom-up demand for institutional licenses.

GTM strategy follows a teacher-first viral model. Free individual accounts spread through teacher social media communities (Instagram teacher influencers, education Twitter, Facebook groups). School and district licenses are sold through instructional leadership — principals and curriculum directors who see teacher adoption data. Conference presence at ISTE, ASCD, and state-level education technology conferences builds credibility.

name: Cognia
tagline: Find what you don't know before the exam does
description: Cognia is an adaptive testing platform that identifies precise knowledge gaps in any subject area. Rather than scoring what you got right, Cognia maps what you don't know and generates a targeted study plan to fill those gaps before they cost you points.
mission:
Traditional tests are autopsy reports. They tell you what went wrong after the damage is done. You get a score, maybe see which questions you missed, and then you're on your own figuring out what to actually do about it. The problem isn't the test — it's the timing and the follow-through.

Cognia flips the model. Our adaptive assessments are designed not to grade you, but to diagnose you. Using item response theory and Bayesian knowledge modeling, each question is selected based on what will reveal the most about your understanding. A 20-minute Cognia assessment provides more diagnostic precision than a three-hour traditional exam because every question is chosen to maximize information about where your knowledge breaks down.

The output isn't a score. It's a knowledge map — a visual, topic-level breakdown showing exactly what you understand deeply, what you partially grasp, and what you've completely missed. Partial understanding is where Cognia shines. Most students don't have binary know-it-or-don't relationships with concepts. They understand the basics of photosynthesis but confuse the light and dark reactions. They can solve linear equations but fall apart with word problems. Cognia detects these nuances and builds study plans that target the specific sub-concepts where understanding breaks down.

We serve two audiences: students preparing for high-stakes exams who need to optimize limited study time, and instructors who want to understand where their class actually stands instead of waiting for the final exam to find out. For both, Cognia replaces guesswork with precision.

We believe assessment should be an act of care, not judgment. When it's done right, a test is a gift — it shows you exactly where to focus so you can grow as efficiently as possible.
marketResearch:
The assessment and testing market in education is valued at $18 billion, with formative and diagnostic assessment growing at 21% CAGR as educators shift from summative to learning-oriented testing. Adaptive testing specifically represents $2.8 billion, dominated by standardized test providers (ETS, College Board) and state assessment contractors. The niche of student-facing diagnostic assessment tools is smaller but growing rapidly at 35% CAGR. Our TAM is $2.8 billion in adaptive assessment, SAM of $900 million targets diagnostic assessment for college students and professional exam preppers, and SOM of $95 million focuses on U.S. students preparing for MCAT, LSAT, GRE, CPA, and similar high-stakes exams.

Competitors include UWorld (question banks with explanations but no adaptive diagnostics), Magoosh (test prep with basic analytics), and ALEKS (adaptive learning for math/chemistry, owned by McGraw-Hill). Standardized testing companies offer practice tests but not diagnostic assessments designed to reveal specific knowledge gaps. Cognia differentiates through its diagnostic-first approach — the purpose isn't to simulate the test but to surgically identify gaps — and its Bayesian modeling that provides confidence intervals on each topic's mastery level.

Our primary users are students preparing for graduate admissions exams (MCAT, LSAT, GRE), professional certifications (CPA, CFA, bar exam), and challenging undergraduate courses. These students face enormous content volumes and limited time — they need to know exactly where to focus. Secondary users are university instructors who want mid-semester diagnostic data on their class.

GTM strategy targets high-stakes exam prep communities through content marketing (study strategy blogs), Reddit and Discord community engagement, and partnerships with tutoring companies that use Cognia diagnostics to guide their sessions. Student referrals drive organic growth — when a study group discovers Cognia, the entire group adopts it.

name: Atelier
tagline: Learn from the best, together
description: Atelier is a platform for live, cohort-based courses taught by working creative professionals. Unlike pre-recorded content, Atelier courses are taught in real-time with small groups, peer feedback, and direct access to instructors who are actively practicing their craft.
mission:
The internet promised to democratize education, and in some ways it delivered. You can learn almost anything from YouTube and online courses. But the dirty secret of self-paced online learning is that almost nobody finishes. Completion rates for MOOCs hover around 5%. The content is there. The motivation isn't. And for creative skills — writing, design, illustration, photography, filmmaking — the feedback loop that self-paced learning can't provide is often more important than the content itself.

Atelier exists because creative learning is inherently social. The workshop model — small groups, live instruction, peer critique, iterative projects — has produced great artists, designers, and writers for centuries. We're bringing that model online with the production quality and accessibility that the internet makes possible.

Every Atelier course is taught live by a working professional, not a career educator. Our instructors are practicing designers at studios, published authors, exhibited photographers, and working filmmakers. They teach from current experience, share real client work as case studies, and provide the kind of candid industry feedback that no pre-recorded course can offer. Classes are capped at 20 students to ensure everyone participates, gets feedback, and builds genuine connections with their cohort.

The cohort model solves the completion problem. When you're learning alongside 19 peers who see your work, give you feedback, and expect you to show up, the social accountability transforms outcomes. Our completion rate is 87% — not because we've gamified engagement, but because humans are wired to show up for other humans.

We started with creative disciplines because the feedback loop is most critical there, but the cohort-based live learning model applies to any skill where practice and critique matter more than information transfer. We're building the future of professional education — and it looks a lot like the past, reimagined for the internet.
marketResearch:
The online professional education market is valued at $46 billion, but cohort-based course platforms (CBCs) represent a rapidly growing segment estimated at $1.2 billion, growing at 40%+ CAGR. The shift from self-paced to live learning is driven by employer demand for practical skills and learner demand for accountability and community. Our TAM encompasses the $1.2 billion CBC market, SAM of $480 million targets creative and professional skills courses for English-speaking adults, and SOM of $65 million focuses on design, writing, photography, and illustration courses for working professionals in North America and Europe.

Maven (founded by Gagan Biyani and Wes Kao) pioneered the cohort-based platform model but focuses broadly across business, tech, and creative skills. Skillshare offers creative courses but in a pre-recorded, self-paced format with low completion rates. MasterClass provides celebrity-taught content with no interactivity. Domestika offers high-quality creative courses but without live components. Atelier differentiates through its exclusive focus on creative professionals, strict 20-person cohort caps, and instructor-as-practitioner model that ensures teaching stays grounded in current industry practice.

Our primary students are creative professionals with 2-8 years of experience who want to level up specific skills — a graphic designer learning motion design, a writer exploring screenwriting, or a photographer transitioning to directing. These professionals earn $50-120K and are willing to invest $300-800 per course for high-quality live instruction. Secondary students include career changers entering creative fields and hobbyists seeking structured community.

GTM strategy leverages instructor audiences. Each Atelier instructor brings their existing social following (typically 10K-500K across Instagram, YouTube, and newsletters). We provide production support, curriculum design assistance, and a platform — they bring students and credibility. This instructor-led distribution keeps customer acquisition costs low while building a content moat that's impossible to replicate with pre-recorded courses.

name: Sequoia
tagline: The marketplace where every carbon credit tells a verifiable story.
description: Sequoia is a carbon credit marketplace connecting buyers with rigorously verified removal projects. We apply satellite monitoring, on-site audits, and AI-driven permanence modeling to ensure every credit represents real carbon removed from the atmosphere — not accounting tricks.
mission:
The voluntary carbon market is broken. Buyers spend millions on credits from projects that may never deliver real atmospheric impact. Registries self-certify. Brokers take 40% margins. And the projects doing genuinely transformative removal work — direct air capture, enhanced weathering, biochar — struggle to find buyers willing to pay their true cost.

Sequoia was founded to rebuild the carbon credit market on a foundation of radical verification. Every project listed on our marketplace undergoes satellite-based monitoring, independent field audits, and AI-driven permanence scoring before a single credit is issued. We don't just verify that carbon was captured — we model the probability it stays captured for 100, 500, and 1,000 years.

Our marketplace serves two constituencies that the current market fails. For buyers — corporations with net-zero commitments, compliance teams facing regulatory scrutiny, and individuals who want their offsets to matter — we provide the confidence that every dollar funds real removal. For project developers — the scientists, engineers, and land stewards doing the hard work of pulling carbon from the sky — we provide access to premium buyers and fair pricing.

We take a fundamentally different approach to credit quality. Rather than relying on registry standards alone, we layer our own verification stack: multispectral satellite imagery to monitor project sites continuously, IoT sensor networks for real-time measurement, and machine learning models trained on thousands of project outcomes to predict permanence risk.

The climate needs a carbon market that works. Not one built on hope and good intentions, but one built on measurement, transparency, and accountability. Sequoia is building that market.
marketResearch:
The voluntary carbon market reached $2.3 billion in 2025 and is projected to grow to $50 billion by 2030 as corporate net-zero commitments accelerate and regulatory pressure intensifies. Within this, the high-quality removal credit segment — credits from CDR projects rather than avoidance — is the fastest-growing subsegment at 45% CAGR, currently valued at $890 million.

Sequoia's serviceable addressable market focuses on corporate buyers in North America and Europe with active net-zero targets and procurement budgets exceeding $100K annually, representing approximately $8.2 billion by 2028. Our initial SOM targets Fortune 2000 sustainability teams and climate-focused funds, approximately $340 million in near-term opportunity.

Key competitors include Patch (API-first carbon credit purchasing, raised $55M), Cloverly (real-time offset API), Puro.earth (focused on engineered removal), and legacy brokers like South Pole. Marketplace incumbents like Xpansiv's CBL aggregate credits but offer limited transparency into project quality. Sequoia differentiates through three pillars: continuous satellite monitoring of project sites (not just point-in-time audits), AI permanence scoring that buyers can independently verify, and a transparent fee structure that passes 85%+ of credit revenue to project developers.

Our go-to-market strategy combines enterprise sales to corporate sustainability teams with an API for fintech and e-commerce platforms embedding carbon offsets into transactions. Early partnerships with three direct air capture facilities and two enhanced weathering projects give us exclusive access to premium removal credits that are consistently oversold on other platforms.

Regulatory tailwinds are significant: the EU Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism, evolving Article 6 rules under the Paris Agreement, and growing scrutiny of greenwashing claims by the SEC and FTC all drive demand for credits with bulletproof verification — exactly what Sequoia provides.

name: Ampère
tagline: Find the energy your building wastes before your utility bill does.
description: Ampère is an energy audit platform for commercial buildings that uses IoT sensor data, utility feeds, and machine learning to identify inefficiencies, model retrofit ROI, and generate audit-ready reports — turning months of manual assessment into days of automated intelligence.
mission:
Commercial buildings consume 35% of all electricity in the United States and waste roughly a third of it. Aging HVAC systems, poorly calibrated controls, lighting schedules nobody has updated since 2014, and envelope leaks that compound year after year. The waste is staggering — and almost entirely invisible to the people paying the bills.

Traditional energy audits are supposed to catch this waste. In practice, they are expensive ($15K-$80K), slow (8-12 weeks), and performed so infrequently that the recommendations are often outdated before the report is delivered. Most building owners get an audit when required by code, file the PDF, and change nothing.

Ampère exists to make energy intelligence continuous, automated, and actionable. We deploy lightweight IoT sensors across a building's mechanical and electrical systems, connect to existing BMS and utility data feeds, and apply machine learning models trained on 40,000+ commercial buildings to identify every source of waste — from the chiller that's short-cycling to the VAV box that's been stuck open for six months.

But finding waste is only half the problem. Building owners need to know what to fix first and what it will cost. Our platform models retrofit scenarios with payback periods, utility incentive eligibility, and financing options — turning an audit from a compliance exercise into a capital planning tool.

We believe the fastest path to decarbonizing the built environment isn't new construction — it's making the 6 million existing commercial buildings in the US dramatically more efficient. Ampère is the intelligence layer that makes that possible.
marketResearch:
The global building energy management systems market is valued at $7.8 billion in 2025, projected to reach $16.2 billion by 2030 at 15.7% CAGR. The energy audit services subsegment represents $4.1 billion, with increasing demand driven by building performance standards being adopted in major cities (NYC Local Law 97, Boston BERDO, DC BEPS) and federal incentives under the Inflation Reduction Act.

Ampère's SAM targets commercial building owners and property managers in the US with portfolios exceeding 50,000 square feet, representing approximately $2.8 billion in annual energy management spend. Our initial SOM focuses on Class A office buildings and multi-tenant retail properties in cities with active building performance standards — roughly $220 million.

Competitors include ENGIE Impact (enterprise energy consulting), Measurabl (ESG reporting for real estate), Audette (AI-driven building decarbonization, raised $8M), and incumbent engineering firms (AECOM, WSP) offering manual audit services. Legacy BMS vendors like Johnson Controls and Honeywell offer energy analytics but require proprietary hardware ecosystems. Ampère differentiates through hardware-agnostic IoT integration, ML models purpose-built for retrofit prioritization, and a pricing model tied to energy savings rather than upfront fees.

Our go-to-market strategy targets property management companies and REITs through compliance-driven sales. Building performance standards create hard deadlines — building owners face fines of $268 per ton of excess CO2 in New York starting in 2025. We partner with mechanical contractors and ESCOs who implement the retrofits our platform recommends, creating a referral flywheel. Our free benchmarking tool attracts building owners who discover their properties underperform peers.

name: Watershed Pro
tagline: See the emissions hiding in every link of your supply chain.
description: Watershed Pro is a Scope 3 emissions tracking platform that maps, measures, and manages supply chain carbon footprints. By combining supplier-specific data collection, spend-based estimation models, and industry benchmarks, we give procurement and sustainability teams the granular visibility they need to reduce emissions where they matter most.
mission:
For most companies, Scope 3 emissions — the indirect emissions from their supply chain, product use, and end-of-life — represent 70-90% of their total carbon footprint. Yet these emissions are the hardest to measure, the least understood, and the most frequently estimated with generic industry averages that bear little resemblance to reality.

The result is a bizarre situation: companies announce ambitious net-zero targets while having almost no idea what their actual emissions are. They report numbers based on spend-category averages, congratulate themselves when revenue grows faster than estimated emissions, and call it progress.

Watershed Pro was built to replace estimation with evidence. Our platform ingests real data from across your supply chain — procurement records, logistics manifests, supplier disclosures, product lifecycle assessments — and builds a granular emissions model that shows exactly where your carbon footprint concentrates. Not by spend category. By specific supplier, specific material, specific shipping lane.

We believe that measurement precision drives reduction action. When a CPG company can see that 40% of their Scope 3 comes from three packaging suppliers in Southeast Asia, they can have a real conversation with those suppliers about alternatives. When a tech company can trace emissions to specific components in specific SKUs, they can redesign products that actually move the needle.

Our vision is a world where every purchase order carries a carbon cost as visible and non-negotiable as the financial cost. Where procurement teams optimize for emissions the way they optimize for price. And where the supply chain — humanity's largest engine of economic activity — becomes the supply chain's largest lever for decarbonization.
marketResearch:
Scope 3 emissions management is the fastest-growing segment of the climate tech software market, projected to reach $4.8 billion by 2028 from $1.2 billion in 2025. This growth is driven by regulatory mandates (CSRD requires Scope 3 disclosure for 50,000+ EU companies), customer pressure (Apple, Microsoft, and Walmart now require supplier emissions data), and investor demand (Climate Action 100+ investors managing $68T in assets expect portfolio companies to report Scope 3).

Watershed Pro's SAM targets mid-to-large enterprises with complex supply chains in manufacturing, retail, CPG, and technology — approximately $2.6 billion in addressable spend. Our SOM focuses on companies with 100+ direct suppliers and annual procurement spend above $500M, representing $420 million.

The competitive landscape includes the original Watershed (raised $100M+, broad carbon accounting), Persefoni (financial-grade carbon data), Carbmee (supply chain focused, EU-based), and Altruistiq (UK-based, lifecycle assessment focus). ERP-adjacent players like SAP and Siemens are adding Scope 3 modules. Watershed Pro differentiates through supplier-level granularity — rather than allocating emissions by spend category, we build supplier-specific emission profiles using a combination of direct data collection, public disclosure mining, and ML-based estimation that improves as real data replaces proxies.

Go-to-market strategy centers on procurement teams as the primary buyer. Sustainability teams set the targets, but procurement teams have the supplier relationships and purchasing leverage to drive reductions. We integrate directly with procurement platforms (SAP Ariba, Coupa, JAGGAER) to embed emissions data into sourcing workflows. Our free supplier portal — where suppliers can report emissions and get benchmarked against peers — serves as a viral adoption mechanism through the supply chain.

name: Terracycle
tagline: One factory's waste is another factory's feedstock.
description: Terracycle is an industrial waste-to-material marketplace that connects waste generators with manufacturers who can use their byproducts as raw inputs. Our logistics and quality verification platform turns linear waste streams into circular supply chains — diverting materials from landfill while reducing virgin resource consumption.
mission:
Every year, the industrial sector sends 7.6 billion tons of material to landfills and incinerators. At the same time, manufacturers spend trillions extracting virgin resources to make products that will eventually become waste themselves. This linear model — extract, make, discard — is not just environmentally catastrophic. It's economically absurd.

Terracycle was founded on a conviction that waste is a design failure, not an inevitability. Across industries, one company's waste stream is often a perfect feedstock for another company's manufacturing process. Steel slag becomes cement aggregate. Textile scraps become insulation. Food processing byproducts become animal feed or biogas. The chemistry works. The economics work. What doesn't work is the marketplace — the infrastructure for matching, logistics, and quality verification that would let these exchanges happen at scale.

That's what we build. Our platform catalogs industrial waste streams with standardized quality profiles, matches them with manufacturers seeking specific material inputs, and manages the logistics, testing, and compliance paperwork that make the exchange possible. We're the operating system for industrial symbiosis.

We start with the highest-volume, highest-value waste streams: construction and demolition debris, manufacturing scrap metals, chemical process byproducts, and food and agricultural waste. Each category has established secondary use cases but lacks the marketplace infrastructure to connect supply with demand efficiently.

Our long-term vision is an industrial economy where the concept of waste is obsolete — where every material output from every process has a known, valued next use. Terracycle is building the marketplace that makes that future possible.
marketResearch:
The global waste management market is valued at $530 billion in 2025, with the industrial waste segment representing $210 billion. The emerging circular economy marketplace segment — platforms that facilitate waste-to-resource exchanges — is projected to grow from $3.2 billion to $12.8 billion by 2030 at 32% CAGR, driven by EPR regulations, corporate circularity targets, and raw material price volatility.

Terracycle's SAM focuses on industrial waste generators and secondary material buyers in North America and Europe, representing approximately $18 billion in annual transaction value. Our SOM targets manufacturing, construction, and food processing companies with annual waste disposal costs exceeding $500K — approximately $1.8 billion in marketplace GMV opportunity.

Competitors include Rubicon (waste hauling marketplace, publicly traded), Rheaply (asset reuse platform, raised $20M), and Circular.co (plastic waste trading). In Europe, Cyrkl and Excess Materials Exchange operate similar marketplaces. Traditional waste brokers handle most B2B waste transactions but charge high margins and lack quality verification infrastructure. Terracycle differentiates through standardized material quality profiles (reducing buyer risk), integrated logistics management, and AI-powered matching that discovers non-obvious waste-to-feedstock opportunities across industries.

Our GTM strategy is supply-side first: we onboard waste generators who face rising disposal costs and tightening landfill regulations. Free waste stream audits identify marketable materials. Once supply is cataloged, we approach manufacturers with verified material offers at 20-40% below virgin material prices. Our revenue model is a 6-12% transaction fee on successful exchanges, with premium services for logistics management and quality certification.

name: Solstice
tagline: Solar power for renters, homeowners, and everyone in between.
description: Solstice is a community solar subscription platform that lets anyone access clean energy savings without installing panels. We partner with local solar farms, handle all enrollment and billing, and deliver guaranteed electricity savings to subscribers — making solar accessible to the 80% of Americans who can't put panels on their roof.
mission:
Rooftop solar has been a revolution — for the 20% of households that can install it. You need to own your home, have a suitable roof, qualify for financing, and navigate a months-long installation process. For renters, apartment dwellers, low-income families, and anyone with a shaded or aging roof, the solar economy has been off limits.

Community solar changes that equation entirely. Instead of panels on your roof, a local solar farm generates clean electricity that's credited to your utility bill. You subscribe, you save, and the grid gets cleaner. No installation, no upfront cost, no long-term commitment.

Solstice exists to make community solar as simple as signing up for Netflix. We partner with solar developers who build local projects, then handle everything the subscriber touches: enrollment, billing, savings calculations, and ongoing account management. Our platform eliminates the complexity that has kept community solar from reaching its potential.

But simplicity is only half of our mission. The other half is equity. Community solar should serve the communities that need it most — low-to-moderate income households who spend a disproportionate share of their income on electricity. Our platform includes income-qualified enrollment pathways, partnerships with housing authorities and community organizations, and savings guarantees that ensure every subscriber benefits regardless of credit score.

We envision a future where your electricity source is a choice as easy as choosing an internet provider — and where clean energy savings are available to every household, not just those with the right roof and the right credit score.
marketResearch:
The US community solar market reached 7.5 GW of installed capacity in 2025, with projections exceeding 30 GW by 2030. The subscriber management and enrollment segment is valued at $1.8 billion, growing at 28% CAGR as 22 states plus DC now have community solar programs and several more are pending legislation.

Solstice's SAM encompasses residential and small commercial subscribers in active community solar markets, representing approximately $4.2 billion in annual subscription value. Our SOM focuses on the five largest markets — New York, Massachusetts, Illinois, New Jersey, and Minnesota — with roughly $680 million in near-term subscriber acquisition and management revenue.

Competitors include Arcadia (community solar marketplace, raised $200M+), Nexamp (developer + subscriber management), and Common Energy (subscriber platform). Utility-owned community solar programs serve some markets but typically lack customer experience focus. Solstice differentiates through three vectors: an income-qualified enrollment engine that enables LMI subscriber acquisition at scale (many state programs require 40-50% LMI participation), a savings guarantee that eliminates subscriber risk, and a developer partnership model where we manage the full subscriber lifecycle so developers can focus on building projects.

Go-to-market strategy combines B2B developer partnerships (subscriber management as a service) with direct-to-consumer acquisition through utility billing data partnerships, community organization referrals, and digital marketing targeting renters in active solar markets. Our LMI enrollment capability is a significant competitive advantage as state programs increasingly mandate low-income participation thresholds.

name: Verdant
tagline: Know the biodiversity cost of building before you break ground.
description: Verdant is a biodiversity impact assessment platform for land development projects. Using ecological databases, satellite imagery, and species distribution models, we quantify how proposed developments affect local ecosystems — and design mitigation strategies that satisfy regulators, investors, and the natural world.
mission:
Every land development project transforms an ecosystem. A warehouse on wetlands. A highway through forest. A solar farm on grassland. These transformations are often necessary — but they are almost never well understood. Environmental impact assessments rely on seasonal field surveys that capture a snapshot of biodiversity, miss mobile or cryptic species, and cost developers $200K-$2M in consultant fees and 6-18 months of delay.

Verdant exists to bring the biodiversity assessment process into the 21st century. Our platform combines ecological databases covering 2.3 million species, remote sensing data from multiple satellite constellations, AI-powered species distribution models, and on-the-ground eDNA sampling to build a comprehensive picture of biodiversity at any proposed development site — in weeks rather than months, at a fraction of traditional cost.

But assessment alone isn't enough. Developers need to know what to do about what they find. Our platform doesn't just quantify impact — it designs the mitigation hierarchy: avoid, minimize, restore, and offset. We model alternative site configurations that reduce biodiversity loss, identify nearby offset opportunities, and calculate the biodiversity net gain required by emerging regulations.

The regulatory landscape is shifting dramatically. The EU's Corporate Sustainability Due Diligence Directive, the Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework's 30x30 target, and the UK's mandatory Biodiversity Net Gain requirement are creating a world where development without biodiversity assessment is no longer an option.

Our mission is to make biodiversity impact as measurable, manageable, and actionable as carbon impact. The climate crisis gets the headlines, but the biodiversity crisis is its twin — and solving one without addressing the other solves neither.
marketResearch:
The environmental impact assessment market is valued at $6.2 billion globally in 2025, with biodiversity-specific assessment growing at 22% CAGR driven by new regulations. The Taskforce on Nature-related Financial Disclosures (TNFD) framework is being adopted by 320+ organizations globally, creating demand for biodiversity data infrastructure. The biodiversity assessment technology segment is projected to reach $2.8 billion by 2029.

Verdant's SAM targets real estate developers, infrastructure firms, renewable energy developers, and extractive industries in regulated markets (EU, UK, US, Australia), representing approximately $3.4 billion. Our SOM focuses on UK developers subject to BNG requirements and EU firms facing CSDD obligations — roughly $380 million in near-term opportunity.

Competitors include NatureMetrics (eDNA biodiversity monitoring, raised $30M), TNFD-aligned consultancies (ERM, Ramboll), and traditional environmental consulting firms. GIS-based tools like NatureServe and IBAT provide species data but lack development-specific impact modeling. Verdant differentiates by combining multiple data sources (satellite, ecological databases, eDNA, acoustic monitoring) into a unified impact model with built-in mitigation design — replacing months of consultant-led fieldwork with a platform that delivers faster, more comprehensive assessments.

Go-to-market strategy targets renewable energy developers first — they face biodiversity requirements but are generally more tech-forward than traditional real estate. We partner with environmental consultancies as a platform rather than competing with them directly, enabling consultants to deliver assessments faster while maintaining their client relationships. Our free biodiversity screening tool for any global coordinate serves as lead generation.

name: Lumen Grid
tagline: Microgrids that think faster than the weather changes.
description: Lumen Grid is a smart optimization platform for renewable microgrids. Our AI controller balances solar, wind, battery storage, and grid interconnection in real-time — maximizing clean energy utilization, minimizing costs, and keeping the lights on when the main grid can't.
mission:
The energy transition is generating a paradox. We are building enormous amounts of renewable generation capacity, yet the grid infrastructure designed for centralized fossil fuel plants cannot efficiently distribute this decentralized, intermittent power. The result: curtailed solar, wasted wind, and a grid that becomes less reliable as it becomes cleaner.

Microgrids are the answer — localized energy systems that combine generation, storage, and intelligent control to serve communities, campuses, and industrial facilities with clean, reliable power. But today's microgrid controllers are primitive. They follow static dispatch schedules, react slowly to weather changes, and leave significant value on the table by failing to optimize across generation sources, storage assets, and grid market signals simultaneously.

Lumen Grid builds the brain that microgrids have been missing. Our AI controller ingests weather forecasts, load predictions, wholesale energy prices, demand response signals, and battery state-of-health data to make dispatch decisions every 15 seconds. It knows when to store solar for the evening peak, when to sell excess to the grid at premium rates, and when to island from a grid that's about to fail.

We serve three markets that are converging: commercial and industrial facilities seeking energy resilience and cost savings, remote and island communities that depend on expensive diesel generation, and utility-scale microgrid developers who need software that maximizes the financial performance of their projects.

Our north star is a world of millions of interconnected microgrids — each one optimized by AI, each one trading energy with its neighbors, forming a resilient, decentralized energy network that is cleaner, cheaper, and more reliable than the centralized grid it supplements.
marketResearch:
The global microgrid market is projected to reach $47.4 billion by 2029, growing at 12.6% CAGR. Within this, the microgrid software and controls segment — Lumen Grid's primary market — is valued at $4.1 billion and growing at 19% CAGR as hardware costs fall and the value of intelligent optimization increases.

Our SAM targets microgrid operators in North America, Australia, and the Pacific Islands with systems exceeding 100kW, representing approximately $1.8 billion in software and optimization revenue. Our initial SOM focuses on C&I microgrids in California, Texas, and Hawaii (states with high electricity costs and strong resilience incentives), approximately $210 million.

Competitors include Schneider Electric's EcoStruxure Microgrid Advisor (hardware-bundled, limited to Schneider ecosystems), Heila Technologies (acquired by Kohler, edge-based control), and Enchanted Rock (gas-focused resilience). Software-only competitors include Geli (acquired by Hanwha) and Stem (focused on standalone storage optimization). Lumen Grid differentiates through hardware-agnostic compatibility (works with any inverter, BMS, or SCADA system), AI that optimizes across generation, storage, load, and grid market participation simultaneously, and a predictive islanding capability that disconnects from the grid before — not during — outages.

Our GTM strategy targets microgrid EPC contractors and developers who need a controls platform for their projects. We integrate with their preferred hardware and provide ongoing optimization as a SaaS subscription. Direct enterprise sales target large C&I campuses (data centers, manufacturing facilities, military bases) where energy costs and resilience are board-level priorities. Partnerships with battery manufacturers (Tesla, BYD, Sungrow) provide co-selling opportunities.
