name: Rewild
tagline: Fund the return of wild places.
description: Rewild is a habitat restoration project funding platform connecting conservation organizations with impact investors, corporate sponsors, and individual donors. We provide transparent project tracking, ecological outcome measurement, and financial reporting — making it possible to invest in nature with the same rigor as any other asset class.
mission:
The world has lost 69% of its wildlife populations since 1970. Deforestation claims 10 million hectares annually. Wetlands, grasslands, and coral reefs are disappearing faster than we can study them. The science is clear: protecting what remains is not enough. We must actively restore degraded ecosystems at a scale never before attempted.

The funding exists. The Kunming-Montreal framework commits $200 billion annually for biodiversity by 2030. Corporate nature-positive pledges are multiplying. Impact investors are searching for credible nature-based assets. But the money can't find the projects, and the projects can't find the money. Conservation organizations lack the fundraising infrastructure to reach capital markets. Investors lack the outcome data to underwrite ecological restoration with confidence.

Rewild bridges this gap. We are the platform where habitat restoration projects meet their funders. Every project on Rewild — from mangrove replanting in Indonesia to prairie restoration in the American Midwest to coral reef rehabilitation in the Caribbean — undergoes ecological baseline assessment, milestone planning, and outcome measurement before it's listed for funding.

For funders, we provide portfolio-grade transparency: satellite monitoring of restoration progress, biodiversity surveys at defined intervals, financial reporting on fund deployment, and impact metrics aligned with TNFD and GBF targets. For project developers, we provide access to capital, technical assistance on monitoring and reporting, and a community of practice with peer organizations.

Rewild is not a donation platform. It's infrastructure for a new asset class: verified ecological restoration. We believe that when nature's recovery can be measured and invested in with the same rigor as real estate or infrastructure, the capital will flow — and the wild places will return.
marketResearch:
The biodiversity and ecosystem restoration funding market is estimated at $154 billion annually in 2025, with a projected gap of $700 billion between current flows and what the Kunming-Montreal framework requires. Biodiversity credit markets, while nascent, are projected to reach $2-4 billion by 2030. The broader conservation finance market — including debt-for-nature swaps, green bonds, and impact investments — is $18 billion and growing at 15% CAGR.

Rewild's SAM focuses on institutional and corporate funders of habitat restoration projects globally, representing approximately $4.5 billion in annual funding flows. Our initial SOM targets corporate sponsors with nature-positive commitments and impact funds with conservation mandates in North America and Europe — roughly $280 million.

Competitors include Restor (ecological data platform backed by Google, focused on mapping not funding), TerraMatch (World Resources Institute's restoration project marketplace), and various carbon-credit-adjacent platforms (Pachama, NCX) that include some habitat components. Traditional conservation fundraising through organizations like The Nature Conservancy and WWF dwarfs platform funding but lacks the transparency and outcome measurement that institutional investors require. Rewild differentiates through investment-grade project due diligence, continuous ecological outcome monitoring (satellite + in-situ), and financial structures that allow investors to fund restoration with measurable return expectations.

Go-to-market strategy starts with curating a portfolio of 50 high-quality restoration projects across five ecosystem types, funded through a blended finance model combining philanthropic grants (catalytic capital) with impact investment tranches. We market to corporate sustainability teams seeking TNFD-aligned nature investments and to family offices with conservation mandates. Our platform fee is 5-8% of funds deployed, with premium analytics and reporting packages for institutional investors.

name: Ember
tagline: A clear path from carbon-heavy building to net-zero asset.
description: Ember is a building decarbonization planning platform for property owners. We model electrification pathways, heat pump retrofits, envelope upgrades, and renewable energy integration to create phased decarbonization plans with accurate cost projections, incentive eligibility, and contractor matching.
mission:
Buildings are responsible for 39% of global carbon emissions — 28% from operations and 11% from construction materials. Decarbonizing the built environment is not optional for meeting climate targets. But for most property owners, the path from a gas-heated, poorly insulated building to a net-zero asset is opaque, expensive, and overwhelming.

The typical building owner faces a maze of decisions: Which heating system to replace first? Is a heat pump viable for this climate? What envelope improvements are needed to make electrification work? Which incentives apply? What's the payback? Who can install it? These questions interact in complex ways — a heat pump without envelope upgrades may fail in a cold climate, but doing both at once may exceed the capital budget.

Ember was built to navigate this complexity. Our platform creates a digital energy model of any building using utility data, building characteristics, and local climate data. It then simulates hundreds of decarbonization pathways — combinations of HVAC electrification, envelope improvements, renewable generation, and operational changes — and ranks them by carbon reduction, cost, payback period, and incentive eligibility.

The output is not a generic recommendation. It's a phased plan: what to do in Year 1, Year 3, Year 5. Which equipment to replace at end-of-life versus proactively. Which incentives to stack (IRA tax credits, state rebates, utility programs). And when we connect you with vetted contractors who've completed similar projects in your area.

We believe that every building owner who wants to decarbonize should have access to the same quality of analysis that a Fortune 500 company gets from a Big Four sustainability practice — at a price point that makes action possible rather than paralyzing.
marketResearch:
The building decarbonization market is projected to reach $280 billion globally by 2030, encompassing heat pump installations, building envelope retrofits, and energy management systems. The software and advisory segment for building decarb planning is valued at $2.4 billion and growing at 26% CAGR, driven by building performance standards, IRA incentives, and corporate ESG commitments.

Ember's SAM targets commercial and multifamily property owners in the US and UK with buildings over 10,000 square feet, representing approximately $1.6 billion in annual planning and advisory spend. Our SOM focuses on multifamily buildings in cities with active building performance standards (NYC, Boston, DC, Denver, St. Louis) — roughly $190 million.

Competitors include BlocPower (electrification-as-a-service, raised $180M, focused on underserved communities), Audette (AI decarb planning, raised $8M), and Arcadia (utility data platform with some decarb features). Traditional engineering firms (AECOM, WSP) offer custom decarb studies at $50K-$200K per building. Ember differentiates through automation (plans generated in days, not months), affordability (starting at $2,500 per building vs. $50K+ for consultant studies), and contractor matching that closes the gap between plan and execution.

Go-to-market strategy targets property management companies with 20-500 unit portfolios facing compliance deadlines. Our free building energy score — generated from address and utility data alone — serves as top-of-funnel. Partnerships with heat pump manufacturers (Mitsubishi, Daikin) and insulation companies provide referral channels and co-marketing opportunities. We take a 3-5% referral fee from contractors matched through our platform, creating a revenue stream aligned with plan execution.

name: Drift
tagline: Track, fund, and verify ocean plastic cleanup — ton by ton.
description: Drift is a platform for tracking and investing in ocean plastic cleanup operations worldwide. We provide GPS-verified collection data, transparent financial reporting, and impact certification — making it possible for brands, investors, and individuals to fund ocean cleanup with the same accountability they expect from any other investment.
mission:
There are an estimated 170 trillion pieces of plastic in the world's oceans, with 11 million metric tons added every year. The scale of the problem is staggering, and the cleanup efforts — while growing — remain critically underfunded and poorly tracked. Most ocean plastic collection happens through small, decentralized operations: coastal community cleanups, river interception systems, and fishing-for-litter programs. These operations do vital work, but they struggle to attract institutional funding because they can't provide the verification and reporting that funders require.

Drift was founded to solve the accountability gap in ocean plastic cleanup. We equip cleanup operations with GPS tracking, weight verification hardware, and material documentation tools that create an auditable record of every ton collected. This data feeds into our platform, where funders can browse verified operations, commit capital, and track the impact of their funding in real-time.

We serve both sides of the equation. For cleanup operators — from a 10-person crew in Bali to a river barrier system in the Philippines — we provide the technology and reporting infrastructure that makes their work fundable. For brands seeking plastic credits, investors looking for impact, and individuals who want their money to provably remove plastic from the ocean, we provide verification they can trust.

Our approach is deliberately bottoms-up. We don't build our own cleanup technology. We empower the thousands of existing operations worldwide with the tools to prove their impact and access the capital they deserve.

We believe the ocean plastic crisis is solvable — not by one giant machine, but by thousands of funded, verified, and accountable cleanup operations working in every affected waterway on the planet. Drift is the infrastructure that makes that network possible.
marketResearch:
The ocean plastic cleanup and prevention market is estimated at $12 billion annually, encompassing collection, recycling, and prevention technologies. The plastic credit market — where companies purchase verified plastic removal to offset their plastic footprint — reached $120 million in 2025 and is projected to grow to $1 billion by 2030 as corporate plastic neutrality commitments accelerate. Over 100 major brands have committed to plastic neutrality or net-zero plastic waste.

Drift's SAM targets the plastic credit and ocean cleanup investment market globally, representing approximately $2.2 billion by 2028. Our SOM focuses on consumer brands with plastic neutrality commitments and impact investors with ocean conservation mandates in North America and Europe — roughly $160 million in near-term platform revenue.

Competitors include Plastic Bank (social plastic collection in developing countries, raised $20M), CleanHub (brand-facing plastic credit platform, raised $10M), and rePurpose Global (plastic offset marketplace). The Ocean Cleanup builds proprietary hardware but doesn't aggregate third-party operations. Drift differentiates through GPS-verified collection tracking (competitors rely on manual weight certificates), a marketplace model that aggregates thousands of small operators (competitors work with their own networks only), and impact analytics that allow funders to compare operations by cost-per-ton, material type, and geographic impact zone.

Go-to-market strategy combines B2B enterprise sales to CPG brands (plastic credit procurement), a consumer platform for individual impact subscriptions, and partnerships with plastic credit standards bodies (Verra Plastic Standard, Zero Plastic Oceans) to ensure our verification meets evolving certification requirements. Revenue model: 8-12% platform fee on credit transactions plus SaaS subscriptions for cleanup operators using our tracking tools.

name: Rootstock
tagline: Precision agriculture that fits in your pocket, not your budget
description: Rootstock builds affordable precision agriculture sensors designed for small and mid-size farms. Our solar-powered soil probes, weather stations, and crop health monitors cost a fraction of enterprise systems — delivering the same data-driven insights that industrial farms rely on to family operations and specialty growers.
mission:
The precision agriculture revolution has been happening for a decade, but it's been a revolution for the top 2%. Massive operations running $300K combine harvesters with GPS-guided autosteer and satellite imagery subscriptions. Meanwhile, the 2 million small farms in America — the ones growing your tomatoes at the farmers market, the ones experimenting with regenerative practices — are still guessing when to irrigate and hoping the frost holds off.

Rootstocks exists to democratize farm data. We build rugged, solar-powered sensor networks that any farmer can install in an afternoon. Soil moisture, temperature, pH, nitrogen levels, microclimate weather data — all streaming to a phone app that speaks plain English, not agronomy jargon. When your south field is trending dry, you get a text. When conditions are right for blight, you know before you see it.

We price our hardware at cost and charge a modest subscription for the intelligence layer. A full 40-acre deployment costs less than a single precision ag consultation from the big players. We believe this is the only way to actually reach the farmers who need this technology most — the ones operating on thin margins who can't afford to gamble on a bad season.

Our founding team includes a third-generation Iowa farmer, a hardware engineer from John Deere, and a soil scientist from UC Davis. We've lived the problem from every angle. We know that the best sensor in the world is worthless if it breaks in a hailstorm, if the battery dies in January, or if the dashboard requires a PhD to interpret.

The future of farming is data-informed, not data-overwhelmed. Rootstock is building the infrastructure to make every acre smarter — starting with the farms that feed your community, not just the ones that feed the commodity markets.
marketResearch:
The global precision agriculture market reached $9.4B in 2025 and is projected to hit $18.6B by 2030 at 14.6% CAGR. However, adoption remains concentrated among large-scale commodity operations (1,000+ acres). Farms under 200 acres — which represent 91% of US farms — have less than 8% precision ag adoption, creating a massive underserved segment worth an estimated $3.2B in the US alone.

Rootstock's serviceable addressable market focuses on specialty crop growers, organic farms, and small diversified operations in North America and Western Europe. These 1.8 million farms spend approximately $2.1B annually on crop management tools and services. Our initial SOM targets direct-to-consumer farms, CSA operations, and specialty growers in the Midwest, Pacific Northwest, and Northeast — roughly $280M in near-term opportunity.

The competitive landscape includes enterprise players like Trimble, John Deere Operations Center, and Climate Corp (Bayer), all priced for large operations at $5-15/acre/year. Budget options like Davis Instruments offer basic weather stations without intelligence. Emerging competitors include Arable (crop monitoring) and CropX (soil sensing), but both target mid-market at premium pricing. Rootstock differentiates through radical affordability ($1.50/acre/year), zero-maintenance solar hardware, and an app designed for farmers who don't self-identify as tech-forward.

Early traction includes 340 farms across 12 states in a beta program, with 87% monthly active usage — unusually high for agricultural IoT. Our hardware-at-cost model drives subscription retention of 93% annually. Distribution partnerships with rural co-ops and farm supply stores provide a capital-efficient channel that enterprise ag-tech companies have ignored.

name: Mise
tagline: Every ingredient, prepped and portioned. Just cook.
description: Mise delivers pre-measured, pre-prepped ingredients for adventurous home cooks who want to make restaurant-quality meals without spending 45 minutes on knife work. Unlike traditional meal kits, Mise lets you choose your own recipes — we just handle the tedious prep so you can focus on the joy of cooking.
mission:
The meal kit industry got one thing right and everything else wrong. They proved people want help getting dinner on the table. But they also proved that most home cooks don't want to be told what to eat, don't want a subscription they forget to pause, and definitely don't want to pay $14 per serving for a recipe they could have found on YouTube.

Mise takes a different approach. We're not a meal kit company — we're a prep kitchen. You tell us what you're making this week (or browse our recipe library for inspiration), and we deliver every ingredient washed, chopped, measured, and organized. Onions diced. Garlic minced. Spices pre-measured into labeled packets. Proteins trimmed and portioned. Your mise en place, done.

We exist because the real barrier to cooking isn't skill or desire — it's the 30-45 minutes of thankless prep that happens before you even turn on the stove. The grocery shopping. The washing. The peeling. The dicing. That's the work that makes people order takeout on a Tuesday night, even when they'd rather be cooking.

Our prep kitchens operate in a hub-and-spoke model, sourcing from local farms and suppliers within 100 miles of each facility. Ingredients are prepped to order — never sitting in a warehouse — and delivered in compostable packaging designed to go straight into your fridge's organization system.

We believe cooking should feel like the best part of your day, not a chore you're guilted into. Mise removes the drudgery so you can skip straight to the sizzle.
marketResearch:
The US meal kit market is worth $11.6B in 2025 but facing significant headwinds: churn rates exceed 70% annually, with the top complaint being lack of recipe flexibility and high per-serving costs. Meanwhile, the broader prepared food and grocery delivery market is $68B and growing at 12% CAGR, indicating strong demand for food convenience solutions that don't follow the rigid subscription model.

Mise targets the underserved segment of engaged home cooks — people who watch cooking content, own good knives, and cook 3-5 times per week but are frustrated by prep time. This demographic represents roughly 28 million US households with a combined spending potential of $8.4B on cooking convenience products. Our initial SOM focuses on metropolitan areas with dense populations of food-engaged millennials and Gen-X households, starting with the Northeast corridor — approximately $420M.

Direct competitors are few: traditional meal kits (HelloFresh, Blue Apron) compete on recipe curation, not prep convenience. Grocery delivery (Instacart, Amazon Fresh) delivers whole ingredients. Local prep services exist in scattered markets but lack technology platforms and scale. Mise's moat is our proprietary ingredient parsing engine that breaks any recipe into a prep manifest, combined with a hub-spoke kitchen network optimized for day-of prep and delivery.

Beta results from our Brooklyn pilot show 4.1 orders per month per active user (vs. 2.2 for meal kits), average order value of $38, and a 6-month retention rate of 61%. Customer acquisition cost is $22, driven primarily by organic social content from users sharing their cooking experiences — a viral loop that meal kits rarely achieve because the food looks the same for every subscriber.

name: Grazer
tagline: Regenerative meat from ranchers who are healing the land
description: Grazer is a direct-to-consumer marketplace connecting consumers with ranchers practicing verified regenerative agriculture. Every cut is traceable to a specific ranch, verified by third-party soil health data, and shipped frozen to your door. We prove that the meat you eat can be part of the climate solution.
mission:
The meat industry has a trust problem. Consumers are told to eat less meat to save the planet — and for commodity feedlot beef, that's fair. But the conversation ignores an inconvenient truth: well-managed grazing is one of the most powerful tools we have for rebuilding soil carbon, restoring grassland ecosystems, and reversing desertification. The problem isn't cows. It's how we manage them.

Grazer exists to connect people who care about the land with ranchers who are actively healing it. Every ranch on our platform practices adaptive multi-paddock grazing, maintains year-round ground cover, and submits to annual third-party soil health testing. We don't just claim regenerative — we measure it, publish the data, and let the soil tell the story.

We're building the marketplace that regenerative ranching has always needed. These ranchers produce exceptional meat — animals that spend their lives on grass, moving across diverse pastures, building topsoil with every step. But most of them are stuck selling into commodity markets that pay the same price regardless of how the land is managed. Grazer gives them a direct channel to consumers willing to pay fair prices for food that's part of the solution.

Our platform handles everything the rancher shouldn't have to: e-commerce, cold chain logistics, cut sheet management, customer acquisition, and the soil verification that gives buyers confidence. We take a 15% platform fee and pass the rest to the rancher — roughly 2-3x what they'd earn through conventional channels.

We believe that what you eat is the most powerful environmental vote you cast. Grazer makes it easy to vote for a food system that regenerates rather than extracts.
marketResearch:
The US grass-fed and regenerative meat market is valued at $4.8B in 2025, growing at 18% CAGR — roughly 3x the growth rate of conventional meat. Consumer willingness to pay a premium for verified sustainability claims has increased 42% since 2021, driven by Gen Z and millennial households. The broader DTC meat market (including all premium proteins) is $8.2B.

Grazer's SAM is the regenerative-verified segment: consumers who specifically seek soil-health-verified, ranch-traceable meat. This segment is approximately $1.4B and growing rapidly. Our initial SOM targets environmentally conscious households in major metro areas with high organic food spending — roughly $180M across 15 metro regions.

Competitors include ButcherBox (DTC meat subscription, $600M revenue, but no regenerative verification), Crowd Cow (marketplace model with ranch stories but limited soil data), and White Oak Pastures (single-ranch DTC, gold standard but not a marketplace). Grazer's differentiation is the verification layer: third-party soil health data published per ranch, creating a trust moat that storytelling alone cannot replicate. No competitor currently offers quantified, transparent soil carbon data at the individual ranch level.

Pilot data from 12 partner ranches shows a $142 average order value, 38% repeat purchase rate within 90 days, and NPS of 74. Rancher earnings average 2.4x commodity prices, which drives supply-side retention of 96%. Our challenge is cold chain unit economics — we've partnered with regional processing facilities and use consolidated shipping windows to reduce per-order fulfillment cost to $11.40, approaching profitability at current volumes.

name: Ferment
tagline: Craft fermentation, precisely monitored
description: Ferment builds IoT monitoring systems for craft fermentation — from kombucha brewers and sauerkraut producers to craft breweries and artisan cheese makers. Our wireless sensors track pH, temperature, CO2, and microbial activity in real-time, turning the art of fermentation into a repeatable science without losing the craft.
mission:
Fermentation is the oldest biotechnology on earth, and it's experiencing a massive renaissance. Kombucha is a $4B industry. Craft beer keeps growing despite consolidation. Fermented foods line every grocery aisle. But the producers behind this boom — the small-batch brewers, the artisan pickle makers, the garage hot sauce brands — are still monitoring their ferments the same way humans have for centuries: by tasting, smelling, and hoping.

Ferment was founded by a former brewery quality manager and an embedded systems engineer who met at a fermentation festival. The brewery manager was tired of losing $3,000 batches to temperature swings overnight. The engineer was tired of building IoT sensors for applications that didn't matter. Together, they realized fermentation monitoring was a perfect collision of urgent need and available technology.

Our wireless sensor pods attach to any fermentation vessel — from a 5-gallon carboy to a 200-barrel brite tank. They continuously monitor pH, temperature, dissolved CO2, and pressure, streaming data to a dashboard that tracks every ferment against your target profiles. When conditions drift, you get an alert before your batch is compromised.

But we're building more than monitoring hardware. Ferment's real value is the fermentation intelligence platform. Every batch you track builds a dataset that our models use to predict outcomes, suggest adjustments, and help you nail consistency across production runs. For craft producers, consistency is the difference between a farmers market hobby and a scalable business.

We believe the future of food is fermented, and the producers leading that future deserve tools as sophisticated as their craft.
marketResearch:
The global fermented food and beverage market reached $762B in 2025, growing at 8.5% CAGR. The craft segment — small-batch producers making premium fermented products — represents approximately $48B and is growing at 14% CAGR. These producers range from kombucha brands and craft breweries to artisan cheese makers and specialty vinegar producers, creating a diverse but underserved market for production technology.

Ferment's TAM is the fermentation monitoring and quality control segment, estimated at $2.1B globally. Our SAM focuses on craft-scale producers (annual revenue $100K-$20M) in North America and Europe — approximately $680M. The initial SOM targets US craft breweries, kombucha producers, and fermented food startups, representing $95M in near-term opportunity.

The competitive landscape is fragmented. Large-scale fermentation monitoring (Hach, Hamilton) serves industrial breweries and biotech at $50K+ per installation. Consumer-grade tools (Tilt hydrometer, Inkbird temperature controllers) are cheap but limited to single-metric monitoring. Precision Fermentation (a UK startup) and BrewMonitor (US) are the closest competitors, but both focus exclusively on beer. Ferment differentiates by supporting all fermentation types — beer, kombucha, sauerkraut, cheese, vinegar, hot sauce, miso — with cross-category fermentation models that improve predictions across the entire platform.

Pilot data from 68 producers shows 73% reduction in batch failures, average payback period of 2.3 months, and a sensor attachment rate of 3.4 vessels per customer within 6 months of first purchase. Monthly software subscription retention is 91%.

name: Canteen
tagline: Corporate dining that employees actually want — with zero waste
description: Canteen is a corporate cafeteria management platform that uses predictive ordering, dynamic menus, and real-time waste tracking to transform workplace dining. We help companies serve better food, reduce waste by 60%+, and turn the cafeteria from a cost center into an employee retention tool.
mission:
Corporate cafeterias are broken in a way that everyone sees but nobody fixes. Employees complain the food is boring. Finance complains it's expensive. Sustainability teams are horrified by the waste. And the food service operators caught in the middle are running on spreadsheets and intuition, overproducing by 30-40% because running out is worse than throwing away.

Canteen exists to solve all of these problems simultaneously — because they're actually the same problem. Bad cafeterias waste food because they don't know what employees want. They serve boring menus because they have no feedback loop. They're expensive because waste and dissatisfaction compound into a cycle that nobody has the data to break.

Our platform integrates with a company's existing food service operation — whether that's an in-house kitchen, a contract caterer, or a mix. We provide demand prediction (what will employees actually eat today?), dynamic menu optimization (what should we serve based on historical preferences, dietary needs, and seasonal ingredients?), and real-time waste tracking (how much went uneaten and why?).

The result is cafeterias that serve food employees choose over DoorDash, waste 60% less food, and cost 25% less to operate. For companies competing for talent in return-to-office mandates, a great cafeteria is no longer a perk — it's a retention strategy. Nobody admits that lunch is a reason they come to the office, but the data says otherwise.

name: Honeycomb
tagline: Healthy bees, healthy harvests. Monitored hive by hive.
description: Honeycomb builds in-hive monitoring systems that track colony health in real-time. Our non-invasive sensors measure temperature, humidity, acoustic patterns, weight, and bee traffic — detecting disease, queen loss, swarming risk, and nutritional stress before visible symptoms appear. Built for commercial beekeepers and pollination services managing hundreds of hives.
mission:
One in three bites of food depends on pollination, and honeybees do the heavy lifting. But bee colony losses have averaged 40% annually for the past decade, and commercial beekeepers are burning out trying to keep pace. A single beekeeper might manage 2,000 hives spread across hundreds of miles. The only way they know a colony is in trouble is by opening the hive and looking — a process that's slow, stressful for the bees, and impossible to do at the frequency needed across large operations.

Honeycomb changes this equation entirely. Our sensor package slides into the hive body without disturbing the colony. It continuously monitors five critical dimensions of hive health: internal temperature patterns (which reveal brood health and thermoregulation), humidity (linked to disease risk), acoustic signatures (which can detect queen loss, swarming intent, and colony stress), hive weight (tracking food stores and foraging success), and entrance traffic (measuring the daily rhythm of a healthy colony).

We built Honeycomb because we saw an industry desperate for better tools. Commercial beekeepers are losing 30-50% of their colonies annually, each colony replacement costing $150-200. Pollination contracts — worth $20B globally — depend on delivering healthy colonies to farms at precisely the right time. The beekeeper who knows a colony is struggling three weeks before it collapses can intervene. The one who finds out at the next inspection often can't.

Our platform aggregates data across entire operations, flagging the hives that need attention and letting beekeepers prioritize their limited field time. Instead of opening every hive on a two-week rotation, they can focus on the 15% that actually need intervention — and often catch problems that a visual inspection would miss entirely.

We're not replacing the beekeeper's skill and intuition. We're extending it across thousands of hives simultaneously.
marketResearch:
The global beekeeping industry is valued at $11.3B in 2025, with the commercial segment (500+ hives) representing $6.8B. Annual colony losses cost the US beekeeping industry approximately $2.4B in replacement and lost productivity. The pollination services market alone is $8.2B globally and growing at 9% CAGR, driven by increasing agricultural demand for managed pollination.

Honeycomb's TAM is the precision beekeeping technology market, estimated at $1.8B globally. Our SAM focuses on commercial beekeepers (500+ hives) and pollination service providers in North America, Europe, and Australia — approximately $540M. Our initial SOM targets US commercial operations managing 1,000+ hives, representing $72M in immediate opportunity.

Competitors include Arnia (UK, academic-origin hive monitoring), BeeHero (Israel, $40M raised, focused on pollination analytics), and Broodminder (US, hobbyist-scale weight monitoring). BeeHero is the primary competitive threat but focuses on the pollination analytics layer rather than colony health intervention. Honeycomb's differentiation is the multi-sensor fusion approach — combining acoustic, thermal, weight, humidity, and traffic data to detect problems 2-3 weeks earlier than any single-metric system. Our acoustic models for queen loss detection have 94% accuracy, vs. 60-70% for competitors relying on temperature alone.

Beta deployment across 4 commercial operations (6,200 hives total) shows 31% reduction in colony losses, 22% fewer field inspection trips, and estimated annual savings of $84 per monitored hive. At $12/hive/month ($144/year), the ROI is immediately clear. Beekeepers report that the queen loss alerts alone justify the subscription.

name: Steep
tagline: Single-origin tea, curated and delivered to your cup
description: Steep is a single-origin tea subscription that connects tea drinkers directly with small-estate growers in China, Japan, India, and Taiwan. Each monthly shipment features two teas with detailed origin stories, brewing guides, and tasting notes — plus a community of tea enthusiasts exploring the world's most nuanced beverage together.
mission:
The specialty coffee revolution proved that people will pay more for quality, traceability, and story. Tea — a beverage with deeper history, wider variety, and more nuanced flavor — deserves the same revolution. But while coffee has its third wave, tea in the West is still largely stuck in the dark ages: commodity tea bags from anonymous blends, priced by the pound with no regard for origin, cultivar, or craft.

Steep exists to be tea's third wave. We work directly with small-estate growers — families who have tended the same gardens for generations in Yunnan, Shizuoka, Darjeeling, and Alishan. We buy at prices that reflect the quality of their work (2-4x commodity rates), and we tell their stories with the respect they deserve.

Every tea we source is single-origin, single-harvest, and selected by our tasting team in blind evaluations. We don't carry a permanent catalog — our selections change with the seasons because the best teas are seasonal by nature. A first-flush Darjeeling in April. A new-harvest sencha in May. An aged pu-erh that only appears when a family decides to release a limited pressing.

Our subscription is designed for discovery. Each month, members receive two teas they've never tried — enough to brew 30+ cups — with detailed tasting notes, brewing parameters, and the story behind each garden. Our community platform lets members share their experiences, compare notes, and go deeper into the world of tea.

We believe tea is the most underappreciated luxury in the world. Steep is making it accessible to people who care about quality, origin, and the craft behind their cup.
marketResearch:
The global specialty tea market reached $8.2B in 2025, growing at 11% CAGR — significantly outpacing the broader $72B tea market. In the US, premium and specialty tea sales grew 18% year-over-year, driven by health-conscious millennials and Gen Z consumers seeking alternatives to coffee. The subscription box market for food and beverage is $12.4B, with tea subscriptions representing a fast-growing niche.

Steep's TAM is the US specialty tea market at $3.1B. Our SAM — consumers willing to pay $30+/month for curated, single-origin tea subscriptions — is approximately $480M. Our initial SOM targets the specialty coffee crossover demographic (people who already pay for quality beans and are curious about tea) in urban markets, representing $62M.

Competitors include Ippodo (traditional Japanese tea, DTC but limited curation), Harney & Sons (broad catalog, not single-origin focused), Yunnan Sourcing (enthusiast marketplace, no curation), and Tea Runners (subscription box, but blends rather than single-origin). Steep differentiates through the curation layer: our blind-tasting process, seasonal rotation, and deep origin stories create an experience closer to a wine club than a tea shop. No competitor currently combines direct-sourcing transparency, seasonal single-origin curation, and community in a single platform.

Beta results from 2,800 subscribers show 14-month average subscriber lifetime, 71% gift conversion rate (members gifting subscriptions), and a monthly churn rate of 4.2%. Average revenue per subscriber is $38/month with 62% gross margins after sourcing, fulfillment, and shipping. Our strongest acquisition channel is member referrals (34% of new signups), indicating strong product-market fit.

name: Provision
tagline: AI meal planning for families who can't eat everything
description: Provision is an AI meal planning platform built specifically for families managing dietary restrictions. Whether it's celiac, nut allergies, dairy-free kids, diabetic grandparents, or a mix of all four — Provision creates weekly meal plans that work for everyone at the table, generates unified grocery lists, and integrates with delivery services.
mission:
Meal planning is hard enough for a family with no dietary restrictions. Now imagine planning for a household where one child has celiac disease, another is allergic to tree nuts, dad is managing type 2 diabetes, and mom is dairy-free by choice. Every single meal becomes a puzzle: What can everyone eat? What substitutions work? How do I make one dinner, not four?

Provision was born in a kitchen like this. Our founder is a parent of two kids with food allergies who spent years planning meals on spreadsheets, cross-referencing ingredient lists, and crying in the grocery store aisle trying to remember which bread brand is safe for both children. She realized that this problem — feeding a family with mixed dietary needs — was universal, exhausting, and completely unsolved by existing meal planning apps.

Every existing meal planning tool assumes everyone at the table eats the same thing. Provision doesn't. Our AI understands the constraints of each family member, finds meals that satisfy all of them, and when that's not possible, suggests smart modifications — like making the pasta dish with a side of regular bread for the non-celiac members and a safe alternative for everyone else.

We generate complete weekly meal plans (breakfast, lunch, dinner, snacks), produce unified grocery lists that can be sent directly to Instacart, Walmart Grocery, or Amazon Fresh, and track nutritional intake to ensure restricted diets remain nutritionally complete. For families managing medical conditions, we integrate with dietitians who can review and approve plans.

Feeding your family shouldn't feel like solving an optimization problem. Provision solves it for you so dinner can just be dinner again.
marketResearch:
Approximately 32 million Americans have food allergies, and 3.1 million follow a gluten-free diet for celiac disease. When expanded to include dietary preferences (vegetarian, vegan, keto), religious restrictions, and medical diets (diabetic, low-FODMAP), an estimated 45% of US households manage at least one dietary restriction. The meal planning app market is $1.2B in 2025, growing at 16% CAGR, but no market leader specifically addresses multi-restriction families.

Provision's TAM is the intersection of meal planning and dietary management — approximately $2.8B when including associated grocery delivery integration revenue. Our SAM focuses on US families managing two or more dietary restrictions within a single household — roughly 18 million households representing $860M in annual spending on meal planning tools and related services. Our initial SOM targets digitally active families with children who have diagnosed food allergies, approximately $110M.

Competitors include Mealime (general meal planning, basic filter options), Eat This Much (calorie-focused, individual-oriented), and Yummly (recipe discovery, owned by Whirlpool). None handle multi-person, multi-restriction household planning. The closest analogs are registered dietitian services ($150-300/month) which are prohibitively expensive for most families. Provision fills this gap at $14.99/month for a family plan — less than a single dietitian consultation.

Beta results from 4,200 families show 89% weekly active usage (planning meals for the upcoming week), average time savings of 3.2 hours per week on meal planning and grocery shopping, and a 4.8/5 satisfaction rating from families with 3+ dietary restrictions. Monthly churn is 3.1%, significantly below the 8% industry average for meal planning apps, indicating strong product-market fit in the multi-restriction niche.

description: Sprout builds modular indoor vertical farming systems designed for restaurants, hotels, and food service operations. mission:
Every restaurant in America receives a produce delivery that traveled an average of 1,500 miles. By the time those herbs reach the kitchen, they've lost half their flavor and most of their shelf life. Chefs know this. They compensate by over-ordering, accepting waste, and making do with whatever survived the supply chain.

Sprout changes that equation by putting the farm inside the restaurant. Our vertical growing towers fit in a closet, a hallway, a corner of the prep kitchen, or a dedicated grow room. They produce a continuous harvest of herbs, microgreens, and leafy greens — basil, cilantro, mint, arugula, specialty microgreens, edible flowers — with zero pesticides, zero food miles, and flavor that makes the delivered stuff taste like cardboard.

We designed Sprout specifically for food service operations, not home hobbyists. Our systems are built for reliability (sealed climate control, automated nutrient dosing, LED grow lights tuned for flavor compounds), volume (enough production to meaningfully offset a restaurant's herb and greens purchasing), and ease of use (a line cook can manage the system — no horticulture degree required).

The economics work because the alternative is terrible. Restaurants spend $8-15 per pound on fresh herbs that are already wilting. Sprout produces the same herbs for under $2 per pound, harvested minutes before service. Our customers typically see full payback on hardware within 8-12 months, after which the ongoing cost is just nutrients, water, and electricity.

We believe the future of restaurant produce is hyper-local — not farm-to-table, but wall-to-table. Sprout is building the infrastructure to make that possible for every kitchen, not just the ones with rooftop gardens and six-figure budgets.

name: Forage
tagline: Wild ingredients and rare finds for ambitious kitchens
description: Forage is a B2B marketplace connecting professional chefs with wild food foragers, specialty growers, and artisan producers. From ramps and morels to high-altitude honey and heritage grain flours — Forage makes the rare and seasonal ingredients that define exceptional cuisine available on demand, with full traceability and sustainable sourcing verification.
mission:
The best restaurants in the world are defined by their ingredients. Not just quality — specificity. The morels from a particular forest in Oregon. The sea beans harvested on a specific stretch of Maine coastline. The heritage wheat milled by a family in Kansas. These ingredients create dishes that can't be replicated, menus that tell stories, and dining experiences that justify the trip.

But sourcing these ingredients is a nightmare. Chefs spend hours texting foragers, calling small farms, and chasing down artisan producers who don't have websites. Supply is unpredictable. Quality varies. Logistics are improvised. The chef who finds an incredible ingredient this week might not be able to get it again for months — or ever.

Forage solves this by building the marketplace that wild and specialty ingredients have never had. We connect a vetted network of foragers, specialty growers, and artisan producers with professional kitchens — providing real-time inventory, sustainable sourcing verification, cold chain logistics, and the reliability that chefs need to put an ingredient on a menu with confidence.

Our sourcing standards are non-negotiable. Every forager on our platform follows sustainable harvest guidelines verified by our field team. Every specialty grower meets our quality benchmarks. Every artisan producer is vetted for food safety compliance. We're not just a marketplace — we're a trust layer for an industry that has always run on relationships and handshakes.

We believe that the best food comes from the most dedicated producers. Forage makes their ingredients accessible to every ambitious kitchen — not just the ones with a Rolodex full of forager phone numbers.
marketResearch:
The US specialty and artisan food ingredient market is estimated at $18.4B in 2025, growing at 13% CAGR. The wild-harvested and foraged food segment specifically is approximately $1.8B, driven by the fine dining and new American cuisine movements that prioritize hyper-local and seasonal sourcing. The broader restaurant specialty purchasing market — ingredients not available through mainstream distributors — represents $6.2B.

Forage's TAM is the specialty ingredient sourcing market for professional kitchens, approximately $6.2B in the US. Our SAM focuses on fine dining, chef-driven restaurants, and boutique hotels that actively source wild and specialty ingredients — approximately $1.4B. Our initial SOM targets Michelin-starred and James Beard-recognized restaurants, destination dining concepts, and high-end hotel restaurants in 15 metro markets, representing $120M.

The competitive landscape is highly fragmented. Specialty distributors (Baldor, Sid Wainer) carry some specialty items but lack wild-foraged depth and real-time seasonal inventory. Direct forager relationships (the current standard) are unreliable and unscalable. Regalis Foods (NYC) is the closest analog — a specialty distributor focused on truffles and luxury ingredients — but operates as a traditional distributor rather than a marketplace. Forage's differentiation is the marketplace model: real-time seasonal availability from a distributed network of 200+ foragers and producers, with sustainability verification and cold chain logistics as platform services.

Beta results from 85 restaurant partners show an average order value of $380, 3.2 orders per month per active account, and a 92% ingredient quality satisfaction rating. Supply-side retention is 94% — foragers and producers earn 75% of the sale price (vs. 40-50% through traditional distribution). The seasonal nature of our inventory drives urgency-based purchasing patterns with strong email open rates (48%) for new availability alerts.

name: Storefront
tagline: Turn your Instagram into a store in sixty seconds
description: Storefront transforms Instagram profiles into fully functional online stores with a single tap. It scans your feed, identifies products, generates descriptions, and builds a shoppable storefront with checkout — no design or coding required. Built for creators and small brands who sell through social but need a real store.
mission:
There are 200 million businesses on Instagram, and the vast majority of them are selling through DMs. They post a photo, caption it with a price, and wait for someone to comment "interested." Then they negotiate in messages, send a payment link, and pray the buyer follows through. It works, barely, until it doesn't scale.

Storefront exists because we believe every creator who sells on Instagram deserves an actual storefront — not a Linktree page with seven links, not a half-finished Shopify site they started three months ago. A real, beautiful, functional store that looks like it was designed by a professional, built in the time it takes to post a story.

Our approach is radical in its simplicity. Point Storefront at your Instagram, and our AI does the rest. It identifies your products from your posts, extracts pricing from captions, generates SEO-friendly descriptions, groups items into collections, and builds a complete storefront with your brand aesthetic. Checkout, inventory tracking, and order management are included from day one.

We're not competing with Shopify or BigCommerce. Those platforms serve businesses that have already graduated from social selling. We serve the millions of creators and micro-brands in the gap between Instagram DMs and a real e-commerce platform — people who have products and an audience but not the time or technical skills to build an online store.

Our vision is to make launching a store as easy as posting on Instagram. When the barrier to e-commerce drops to zero, millions of creators who never thought of themselves as business owners will discover they already are.
marketResearch:
The social commerce market reached $728B globally in 2025 and is projected to hit $1.2T by 2028 at a 25% CAGR. Within this, the tools-for-creators segment — platforms helping individual sellers professionalize their social selling — represents a $12B addressable market growing at 38% annually. Instagram alone hosts 200M+ business accounts, with 44% of users shopping weekly on the platform.

Storefront's SAM focuses on Instagram-native sellers doing $1K-$100K in annual revenue who currently lack a dedicated storefront. This represents approximately 8M sellers globally, or a $3.2B annual opportunity at our average price point. Our initial SOM targets English-speaking creators in fashion, beauty, home goods, and handmade categories across North America and the UK — roughly 1.2M sellers and $480M in near-term revenue.

The competitive landscape includes Shopify Starter (too complex for casual sellers), Stan Store (focused on digital products), and Koji (link-in-bio with basic commerce). None offer automated store generation from existing Instagram content. Our key differentiator is the zero-effort onboarding: sellers don't build a store, Storefront builds it from their existing content. Our moat deepens as we accumulate product-image-to-listing training data across categories.

Our GTM leverages viral mechanics inherent to our product — every Storefront-generated store includes a subtle "Built with Storefront" badge that drives organic discovery. Early data shows a 6.2% visitor-to-signup conversion rate from these badges. We supplement with Instagram ad campaigns targeting sellers who use commerce-related hashtags, achieving a $4.80 CAC against a $14/month average plan value.

name: Refund
tagline: Returns don't have to be lost revenue
description: Refund is a returns management platform that turns the most dreaded part of e-commerce into a revenue recovery engine. By offering instant exchanges, store credit incentives, and intelligent routing, Refund helps DTC brands retain up to 40% of revenue that would otherwise walk out the door as refunds.
mission:
Returns are the silent killer of e-commerce profitability. The average online retailer sees 20-30% of orders come back, and for fashion brands, that number can hit 40%. Most brands treat returns as an unavoidable cost — a logistics problem to be managed, not a revenue opportunity to be captured.

We founded Refund because we saw the data: 67% of customers who initiate a return would accept an exchange or store credit if the process were instant and frictionless. But most return flows are designed around the refund — a clunky portal, a shipping label, a two-week wait. By the time the customer gets their money back, they've already bought from a competitor.

Refund flips the returns experience from a refund-first flow to a retention-first flow. When a customer initiates a return, our AI instantly presents personalized exchange recommendations, bonus store credit offers, and flexible options like size swaps or color changes. The result: brands keep the revenue, and customers get what they actually wanted faster.

Behind the scenes, Refund provides intelligent return routing, fraud detection, and disposition optimization — deciding whether returned items should be restocked, sent to outlet, or donated based on condition, demand, and margin data. We turn the entire returns operation from a cost center into a strategic advantage.

Our long-term vision is that returns become a positive touchpoint in the customer journey. Not a failure of the purchase, but an opportunity to deepen the relationship and increase lifetime value.
marketResearch:
E-commerce returns cost US retailers $247B annually, with reverse logistics and processing consuming 59% of the original item's price on average. The returns management software market is valued at $640M in 2025, growing at 22% CAGR as brands shift from treating returns as a cost center to a strategic lever. The total addressable market, including returns logistics optimization, reaches $2.1B.

Refund's SAM targets DTC and Shopify-based brands doing $5M-$200M in annual revenue with return rates above 15%. This represents approximately 18,000 brands in North America and Europe, yielding a $720M annual opportunity. Our initial SOM focuses on fashion, footwear, and home goods verticals in North America — roughly 5,400 brands and $216M in near-term addressable revenue.

Key competitors include Loop Returns (market leader with $50M+ ARR but focused on enterprise), Returnly (acquired by Affirm, stalled product), and Happy Returns (acquired by PayPal, focused on physical drop-off). Refund differentiates through AI-driven exchange recommendations that personalize based on the specific return reason and customer history, dynamic store credit bonuses calibrated to maximize retention without over-discounting, and a self-service implementation that takes hours instead of the weeks competitors require.

Early traction validates the thesis: pilot brands see an average 38% return-to-exchange conversion rate (vs. 12% industry average), $8.40 incremental revenue per return, and a 15% increase in repeat purchase rates among customers who used the exchange flow. Our pricing model charges a per-return fee ($0.50-$2.00 based on volume), aligning our revenue with the value we create.

name: Sizing
tagline: The fitting room your website is missing
description: Sizing brings virtual try-on to any fashion e-commerce store. Using phone camera scans and AI body modeling, shoppers see exactly how clothes will fit their unique body before buying — reducing returns by 52% and increasing conversion by 28%. No hardware required.
mission:
Online fashion has a $100 billion fitting problem. Shoppers can't try clothes on, so they guess. They order three sizes, keep one, and return two. Brands absorb the shipping costs both ways, and the returned items often can't be resold at full price. It's a losing game for everyone.

Sizing was founded on a conviction that the technology to solve this finally exists. Computer vision has reached the point where a 10-second phone camera scan can capture body measurements more accurately than a tape measure. Generative AI can now render photorealistic visualizations of how a specific garment will drape, stretch, and fit on a specific body. The pieces are here — they just haven't been assembled into a product that works for real shoppers.

Our approach puts zero burden on the shopper. No body measurements to input, no size charts to decode. Open the camera, do a quick scan, and see yourself wearing the clothes. The visualization isn't a cartoon avatar — it's a realistic rendering that shows fabric behavior, fit around problem areas, and how the garment moves. If it looks good on your screen, it'll look good in your mirror.

For brands, Sizing is a revenue tool disguised as a fitting tool. Our data shows that shoppers who use virtual try-on convert at 2.8x the rate of those who don't, return 52% fewer items, and buy 1.4 more items per order. The fitting room isn't a cost center — it's the highest-converting feature on the product page.
marketResearch:
The virtual try-on and fit technology market is valued at $5.2B in 2025, projected to reach $14.8B by 2029 at a 30% CAGR, driven by the fashion industry's urgent need to reduce returns (which cost $100B+ annually) and improve online conversion rates that still lag physical retail by 3-5x. The broader fashion e-commerce tools market exceeds $22B.

Sizing's SAM targets fashion and apparel brands doing $2M-$500M in online revenue with return rates above 20%. This covers approximately 25,000 brands across North America and Europe, representing a $2B annual opportunity at our average price point. Our SOM focuses on mid-market DTC fashion brands on Shopify Plus and custom platforms — roughly 6,000 brands and $480M in addressable revenue.

Competitors include Zeekit (acquired by Walmart, closed ecosystem), True Fit (size recommendation only, no visualization), and Vue.ai (broad AI suite, virtual try-on is secondary). Sizing differentiates through three key advantages: no-app-required browser-based body scanning, photorealistic garment visualization (not avatar-based), and a Shopify app that installs in under an hour with automatic garment digitization from existing product photos.

Early results from 40+ brand pilots show 52% return reduction, 28% conversion lift, and 23% increase in average order value. Our pricing model — a per-scan fee of $0.02-$0.08 based on volume — makes Sizing accessible to brands of all sizes while scaling revenue with usage. The unit economics are compelling: brands save $8-15 per avoided return while paying $0.04 per scan on average.

name: Bazaar
tagline: Where artisans meet the world
description: Bazaar is a curated marketplace connecting independent artisans and craftspeople with conscious consumers globally. From hand-thrown ceramics in Oaxaca to woven textiles in Rajasthan, Bazaar handles discovery, translation, payments, and logistics so makers can focus on their craft and buyers can shop with meaning.
mission:
The world's most extraordinary products are made by people who will never set foot in a trade show or pitch a buyer at Nordstrom. In villages across Mexico, India, Morocco, and Indonesia, artisans create objects of stunning beauty and craftsmanship using techniques passed down through generations. Most of these makers earn a fraction of what their work is worth because they have no way to reach the customers who would value it most.

Bazaar was born from trips to artisan communities where we watched master craftspeople sell $200 worth of pottery for $15 to a middleman because that was their only channel. The internet was supposed to flatten this. Instead, platforms like Etsy became saturated with mass-produced goods marketed as handmade, and the real artisans got buried.

We're building a different kind of marketplace — one where curation is the product. Every maker on Bazaar is verified through our on-the-ground network of scouts and cultural liaisons. Every listing tells the story of the maker and the tradition behind the craft. Buyers aren't just shopping; they're connecting with the human hands behind every object.

The logistics challenge is real and we don't pretend otherwise. Shipping handmade ceramics from a workshop in rural Portugal to an apartment in Brooklyn requires specialized packaging, customs navigation, and quality assurance. Bazaar handles all of it, providing makers with shipping kits, pre-negotiated carrier rates, and a support team fluent in 14 languages.

We believe commerce can be a force for cultural preservation. Every sale on Bazaar directly funds the continuation of craft traditions that are disappearing. That's not marketing — it's the reason we exist.
marketResearch:
The global handmade and artisan goods market is valued at $780B, with online artisan commerce growing at 18% CAGR. The conscious consumer segment — buyers willing to pay premium prices for ethically sourced, handmade products — represents $120B and is expanding at 24% annually, driven by Gen Z and millennial purchasing preferences for authenticity and sustainability.

Bazaar's SAM focuses on the curated artisan marketplace opportunity, estimated at $18B globally. Our SOM targets English-speaking conscious consumers in North America and Western Europe with household incomes above $75K, representing approximately $3.6B in near-term addressable spend. We prioritize categories with high artisan value-add and shippability: ceramics, textiles, jewelry, leather goods, and home decor.

The competitive landscape includes Etsy (massive but diluted by mass-produced goods), Novica (National Geographic-affiliated but dated UX), and The Citizenry (curated but brand-owned, not a marketplace). Bazaar's differentiators are threefold: verified artisan provenance with maker stories and process documentation, an end-to-end logistics solution designed for fragile handmade goods, and a curation model that maintains quality as the platform scales through regional scouts rather than open listing.

Our business model takes a 20% commission on sales (competitive with Etsy's effective 20-25% take rate) while providing significantly more value through logistics coordination, translation, and customer support. Early metrics show a $94 average order value (3x Etsy's), 42% repeat purchase rate within 6 months, and NPS of 78. Our primary acquisition channels are Instagram content marketing featuring maker stories and partnerships with home and design publications.

name: Restock
tagline: Never run out. Never overstock. Just right.
description: Restock is an AI-powered inventory demand forecasting platform for DTC brands. It predicts exactly when you'll run out of every SKU, recommends optimal reorder quantities, and factors in seasonality, promotions, and supply chain lead times. Stop guessing — start forecasting.
mission:
Inventory is the biggest bet every product brand makes, and most of them are making it blind. A DTC brand founder ordering their next production run is essentially guessing how much demand they'll see in 60-90 days. Order too much and you're sitting on dead stock that eats your cash flow. Order too little and you're out of stock on your best sellers, losing revenue and frustrating customers who won't come back.

Restock was built by a team that lived this problem firsthand. Our founders ran a DTC brand that nearly went under twice — once from a $400K overstock of a product that didn't sell, and once from a stockout on their hero SKU during Black Friday that cost them their best month of the year. Both problems were preventable with better forecasting.

The challenge is that demand forecasting for DTC brands requires synthesizing dozens of signals: historical sales velocity, seasonality patterns, marketing calendar effects, website traffic trends, social media momentum, competitor activity, and supply chain lead times. Enterprise retailers have teams of demand planners and million-dollar forecasting tools. DTC brands have a spreadsheet and a gut feeling.

Restock brings enterprise-grade demand intelligence to brands of every size. Our AI ingests your sales data, connects to your marketing and analytics tools, and produces SKU-level demand forecasts with confidence intervals. It tells you not just how much to order, but when to order it, factoring in your supplier lead times and cash flow constraints.

We're building toward a future where no product brand loses a sale to stockouts or a dollar to dead stock. Inventory should be a solved problem, not a source of existential anxiety.
marketResearch:
The demand forecasting software market is valued at $7.9B globally in 2025, growing at 21% CAGR. The DTC-specific segment — brands selling primarily through owned channels — is underserved by existing enterprise tools (SAP IBP, Oracle Demantra) that cost $100K+ annually and require dedicated planning teams. The addressable market for DTC-focused demand forecasting is estimated at $3.4B.

Restock's SAM targets DTC and digitally-native brands with $1M-$100M in annual revenue managing 50-10,000 active SKUs. This encompasses approximately 45,000 brands in North America and Europe, representing a $1.8B annual opportunity. Our initial SOM focuses on Shopify-based brands in fashion, beauty, supplements, and food/beverage — roughly 12,000 brands and $480M in near-term addressable revenue.

Competitors include Inventory Planner by Sage (spreadsheet-like, rules-based), Flieber (newer entrant, limited ML capabilities), and Cogsy (consumer-focused, shallow forecasting). Restock differentiates through genuine machine learning that improves with each demand cycle, multi-signal ingestion (marketing data, traffic, social signals — not just historical sales), and a cash-flow-aware reorder engine that optimizes for working capital constraints, not just demand matching.

Pilot brand results show 34% reduction in stockout events, 28% decrease in overstock inventory, and 18% improvement in inventory turnover. Our pricing scales with SKU count: $199/month for up to 200 SKUs, $499/month for up to 2,000 SKUs, and custom pricing above that. The average pilot brand reports $4.20 in recovered revenue for every $1 spent on Restock.

name: Lookbook
tagline: Editorial content that sells
description: Lookbook transforms fashion brand content into shoppable experiences. Embed product tags in editorial shoots, style guides, and influencer content — letting readers buy what they see without ever leaving the story. Content becomes commerce, seamlessly.
mission:
Fashion brands spend millions on editorial content — stunning photo shoots, carefully curated style guides, influencer collaborations — and then dump all of it into a social feed where it lives for 24 hours and dies. Meanwhile, their product pages are clinical grids of white-background images that strip away all the context and aspiration that makes fashion compelling.

Lookbook bridges this absurd gap. We believe content and commerce shouldn't live in separate worlds. When a reader sees a model in a beautiful outfit, they should be able to buy every piece in that look without switching tabs, searching product names, or guessing at links. The editorial experience should be the shopping experience.

Our platform lets fashion brands tag products in any visual content — photoshoots, style articles, influencer posts, even video — and create shoppable editorial pages that live on their own domain. The reader browses the content as they naturally would, tapping on items that catch their eye to see details, sizes, and price, adding to cart without ever leaving the editorial flow.

The data we've seen from early brands is striking: shoppable editorial content converts at 4.6x the rate of standard product pages. This makes intuitive sense. When you see a dress on a product page, you see a dress. When you see it styled in an editorial with the right bag, shoes, and jewelry, you see yourself. Context sells.

Our vision is to make every piece of fashion content a potential point of sale. The future of fashion retail isn't better product pages — it's better stories with seamless commerce woven in.

Competitors include Curalate (acquired by Bazaarvoice, broadly focused on UGC), LikeToKnow.It (consumer app, not embeddable), and Shopify's native content tools (basic, limited editorial capability). Lookbook differentiates by creating full editorial experiences rather than simple product tagging, offering a WYSIWYG editor designed for fashion creatives, and providing content attribution analytics that track revenue from every editorial piece, influencer, and individual product placement.

Pilot brand data shows a 4.6x conversion rate from editorial pages vs. standard PDPs, 2.1x average order value (styled looks drive multi-item purchases), and 340% more time-on-page compared to traditional product pages. Our pricing model — $499-$2,499/month based on pageviews and features — positions us as a premium but justifiable investment for content-forward fashion brands.

name: Crate
tagline: Build a subscription box your community will obsess over
description: Crate is a full-stack subscription box platform for niche communities. From curation tools and supplier management to fulfillment logistics and subscriber analytics, Crate gives passionate entrepreneurs everything they need to launch and scale a subscription box business without the operational nightmare.
mission:
Subscription boxes are a $38 billion market, and it's growing because the model works. People love receiving curated surprises tailored to their passions — whether that's specialty coffee, indie board games, Japanese snacks, or vintage vinyl. The problem isn't demand. The problem is that launching a subscription box is an operational hellscape.

A subscription box founder needs to source products from multiple suppliers, negotiate wholesale pricing, design packaging, coordinate fulfillment for thousands of boxes on the same day each month, manage subscriber billing with upgrade/downgrade/pause/cancel flows, and handle customer service — all while curating a box compelling enough to reduce churn. Most founders burn out within six months.

Crate consolidates the entire subscription box operation into a single platform. Our supplier marketplace connects box creators with vetted product suppliers across dozens of niche categories. Our curation tools help design each month's box with cost tracking, margin analysis, and subscriber preference matching. Our fulfillment engine coordinates with 3PL partners to ship thousands of boxes on schedule. And our subscriber management platform handles billing, pausing, gifting, and all the edge cases that break generic subscription tools.

We're building for the long tail of passion — the person who wants to build a monthly astronomy box, a Korean beauty box, or a vintage tea box. These niche communities are small individually but massive in aggregate, and they're dramatically underserved by generic e-commerce tools that treat subscriptions as an afterthought.
marketResearch:
The global subscription box market reached $38.2B in 2025, growing at 14% CAGR. While major players (Birchbox, FabFitFun) have defined the category, the market is fragmenting toward niche communities. Over 70% of new subscription box launches target specific interest communities with fewer than 50,000 potential subscribers — a segment underserved by existing infrastructure.

Crate's TAM encompasses the full subscription box enablement market, estimated at $4.2B including SaaS, logistics, and supplier services. Our SAM targets aspiring and active subscription box entrepreneurs in North America and Europe, representing approximately $1.6B in annual opportunity. Our initial SOM focuses on first-time box launchers and existing boxes doing under $50K MRR seeking operational consolidation — roughly 15,000 businesses and $360M in addressable revenue.

Competitors include Cratejoy (marketplace-focused, outdated platform), Subbly (basic subscription management), and Recharge (Shopify plugin, not box-specific). None offer the end-to-end solution that subscription box businesses actually need: supplier sourcing, curation tooling, fulfillment coordination, and subscriber management in one platform. Crate's integrated approach eliminates the patchwork of 6-8 tools most box operators currently use.

Early traction includes 340 active box businesses on the platform, with an average time-to-first-box-shipped of 23 days (vs. 90+ days industry average). Retention is strong: 89% of boxes that launch on Crate are still active after 12 months, compared to the industry average of 52%. Our revenue model combines a $79-$399/month SaaS fee with a per-box fulfillment fee of $2-5, creating dual revenue streams that scale with customer success.

name: Pricetag
tagline: Pricing that thinks faster than your market moves
description: Pricetag is a dynamic pricing engine for e-commerce brands. It monitors competitor prices, demand signals, inventory levels, and margin targets in real time, then automatically adjusts your prices to maximize revenue. Stop leaving money on the table with static pricing.
mission:
Every product in your store has an optimal price at any given moment. That price depends on what competitors are charging, how much demand exists right now, how much inventory you're holding, what your margin floor is, and what your customer is willing to pay. Static pricing ignores all of this. You set a price when you launch a product and hope it's right for the next six months.

Pricetag was founded because we believe dynamic pricing shouldn't be exclusive to airlines and hotels. Every e-commerce brand — from a 50-SKU Shopify store to a 50,000-SKU marketplace seller — deserves pricing that responds to market conditions in real time.

Our engine monitors competitor prices across dozens of retailers, tracks demand signals from your own traffic and conversion data, and factors in your inventory levels and margin targets. When conditions change, Pricetag adjusts your prices automatically within the guardrails you set. You stay competitive without racing to the bottom, and you capture margin when demand allows.

What makes us different from legacy repricing tools is intelligence. We don't just match the lowest competitor price — that's a race to zero. Pricetag's AI understands price elasticity at the SKU level. It knows that your premium yoga mat can hold a $10 premium over competitors while your basic mat needs to match. It knows that demand spikes on Tuesday evenings for your product category and prices accordingly.

The future of e-commerce pricing is autonomous. Not reckless — autonomous within the strategic boundaries you define. Pricetag is building that future, one SKU at a time.
marketResearch:
The global dynamic pricing software market is valued at $4.1B in 2025, growing at 24% CAGR as e-commerce competition intensifies and price transparency increases. While dynamic pricing is standard in travel and hospitality, adoption in retail e-commerce remains below 15%, representing a massive greenfield opportunity. The total addressable market for e-commerce pricing optimization is $8.6B.

Pricetag's SAM targets online retailers and DTC brands with $2M-$500M in annual revenue managing price-sensitive product catalogs. This encompasses approximately 30,000 businesses in North America and Europe, representing a $2.4B annual opportunity. Our SOM initially targets Shopify Plus merchants and Amazon/marketplace sellers in electronics, fashion, home goods, and sporting goods — roughly 8,000 businesses and $640M in near-term addressable revenue.

Competitors include Prisync (competitor monitoring only, no automation), Intelligence Node (enterprise-focused, $50K+ annually), and Amazon's built-in repricing (race-to-bottom algorithm). Pricetag differentiates through AI-powered price elasticity modeling (not just competitor matching), multi-channel price coordination (DTC site, Amazon, Walmart simultaneously), and margin-aware optimization that maximizes revenue within profitability constraints rather than simply undercutting competitors.

Beta results from 60+ merchants show an average 12% revenue increase and 8% margin improvement within 90 days. The revenue increase comes from both directions: capturing more margin when demand is strong and staying competitive when the market tightens. Our pricing model charges 0.15-0.25% of monthly GMV processed through the engine, aligning our revenue directly with merchant success.

name: Parcel
tagline: Ship sustainably without the headache
description: Parcel is sustainable packaging-as-a-service for online retailers. We replace plastic mailers and styrofoam with beautiful, protective, compostable packaging — designed for your brand, delivered to your warehouse, and priced competitively with conventional materials. Sustainability without sacrifice.
mission:
E-commerce generates 2.4 billion pounds of plastic packaging waste every year, and the number is growing. Most online retailers know their packaging is a problem. They've seen the social media posts of customers frustrated by excessive bubble wrap and plastic mailers. They've read the studies showing 72% of consumers prefer brands with sustainable packaging. But when they try to switch, they hit a wall.

Sustainable packaging has historically been expensive, unreliable, and ugly. Compostable mailers that fall apart in transit. Recycled boxes that look cheap. Mushroom packaging that costs three times the conventional alternative. The gap between intention and adoption isn't awareness — it's execution.

Parcel closes that gap. We design custom sustainable packaging for e-commerce brands that is beautiful, protective, and priced within 10-15% of conventional materials. Our packaging engineers work with each brand to create packaging that reflects their identity — because a luxury skincare brand and an outdoor gear company need very different unboxing experiences, even if both want to ditch plastic.

We handle the entire supply chain: material sourcing from certified compostable and recycled suppliers, design and prototyping, manufacturing, quality testing, and delivery to your warehouse or 3PL. Brands get one invoice, one point of contact, and packaging that their customers will Instagram instead of cursing.

Our long-term play is to make sustainable packaging the default, not the premium option. As we scale, our material costs drop. As material science advances, our options expand. We're already seeing compostable materials approach price parity with plastic in several categories, and we're investing in next-generation materials that will eliminate the gap entirely.

Parcel's SAM focuses on mid-market e-commerce brands spending $10K-$500K annually on packaging materials. Parcel differentiates through our full-service model: unlike competitors that sell packaging products, we provide a packaging service — from brand-specific design through delivery, with ongoing optimization. Our packaging engineers become an extension of the brand's team.

Pilot data shows brands experience a 22% increase in social media mentions of packaging after switching to Parcel, 15% improvement in customer satisfaction scores, and measurably lower return rates (well-designed protective packaging reduces damage). Our pricing model is a per-unit packaging fee with annual commitments, typically 10-15% above conventional packaging costs. At scale, we project reaching parity by 2027.
