name: Ensemble
tagline: Your AI stylist lives on every product page
description: Ensemble is an AI personal stylist that integrates into fashion e-commerce stores. It understands each shopper's style, body type, existing wardrobe, and occasion needs, then curates personalized outfit recommendations from the store's catalog. Not product recs — complete styled looks that drive multi-item purchases.
mission:
Fashion e-commerce has a styling problem. Product recommendation engines can tell you that people who bought this dress also bought that necklace. What they can't do is understand that you're a pear-shaped creative director who dresses minimalist for work but loves bold prints on weekends, and that you need an outfit for a rooftop wedding in May.

Ensemble was founded on the belief that every online shopper deserves the experience of working with a great personal stylist — someone who knows your body, your style, your life, and your budget, and who can pull together complete looks that make you feel confident. That experience has historically been reserved for people who can afford $500-an-hour styling sessions or who live near a Nordstrom with a good personal shopping team.

Our AI stylist integrates directly into fashion retailers' websites. When a shopper visits a product page, Ensemble doesn't just say "you might also like." It assembles a complete outfit: this top with these pants, this belt, these shoes, this bag. The outfit is styled for the shopper's expressed preferences, body type (if provided), and the occasion they're shopping for. Every recommendation comes from the retailer's own catalog, driving multi-item purchases rather than single-product conversions.

The economic impact for retailers is transformative. Shoppers who engage with Ensemble add 2.4 items to cart on average versus 1.1 for standard browsing. Average order value increases 68%. Return rates drop because customers buy coordinated outfits rather than individual pieces that may not work together.

We see a future where personal styling is a standard feature of every fashion website — as expected as search or filtering. Ensemble is building that future by making world-class styling accessible to every shopper and affordable for every retailer.

tagline: One prompt. An entire brand identity.
description: Pallete generates complete brand identity systems from a single text prompt. Logos, color palettes, typography pairings, brand guidelines, and social templates — all coherent, all production-ready, all in under sixty seconds. mission:
Starting a company already demands everything you have. You shouldn't also need to become a brand designer. Yet the alternatives are brutal: spend $5K-$30K on an agency (money most founders don't have), DIY something forgettable with free tools, or launch with no visual identity at all and hope nobody notices.

Pallete was founded on a conviction that brand identity is a solvable design problem. Not because branding is simple — it's deeply complex — but because the underlying principles of effective visual identity (contrast, harmony, hierarchy, cultural resonance) are learnable by machines when trained on the right data. We've studied tens of thousands of successful brand systems, from Fortune 500 companies to breakout D2C startups, and distilled the patterns that make identities feel both distinctive and trustworthy.

Our system doesn't generate random aesthetics. You describe your company, your audience, and the feeling you want to evoke, and Pallete produces a coordinated identity system: primary and secondary logos, a curated color palette with accessibility-checked combinations, typography pairings with usage rules, and ready-to-use templates for social media, pitch decks, and business cards. Every element is connected by an internal design logic that ensures coherence.

We're building toward a future where every startup launches with the visual credibility of a company ten times its size. Not because appearances are everything, but because they shape first impressions — and first impressions determine whether someone reads your pitch, clicks your ad, or opens your email.

name: Waveform
tagline: Edit podcasts by editing text.
description: Waveform reimagines podcast post-production by turning audio into an editable transcript. Cut filler words, rearrange segments, and remove tangents by highlighting and deleting text. The audio follows. Built for podcasters who'd rather tell stories than wrestle with waveforms.
mission:
Podcast editing is stuck in the DAW era. Tools built for music production — multi-track timelines, waveform scrubbing, sample-level precision — are wildly overpowered for what most podcasters actually need: removing ums, tightening transitions, and cutting the segment where the guest's dog started barking.

Waveform started when our founders, both podcasters, realized they spent more time editing than recording. The bottleneck wasn't audio quality or microphone technique — it was the tedious, mechanical process of scrubbing through hours of audio to find and remove the parts that didn't belong. They could identify bad sections instantly by reading a transcript. But translating transcript edits to timeline edits required constant back-and-forth between text and waveform.

So we built the tool that should have existed from the start: an editor where the transcript is the timeline. Select text, delete it, and the audio cuts cleanly. Drag a paragraph to rearrange your episode structure. Highlight filler words across the entire episode and remove them in one click. The audio follows the text, not the other way around.

We're not replacing professional audio engineering. We're eliminating the 90% of podcast editing that's mechanical, repetitive, and doesn't require an audio degree. Our goal is to make weekly publishing sustainable for solo creators and small teams who currently spend six hours editing every hour of content.

The podcast market has surpassed 4 million active shows globally, with 72% of podcasters editing their own content. The podcast tools and hosting market is valued at $4.1B in 2025, with editing software representing approximately $800M. AI-powered audio editing is the fastest-growing segment at 38% CAGR, driven by solo creators and small production teams seeking efficiency.

Direct competitors include Descript (transcript-based editing pioneer, $100M+ ARR, recently acquired features that dilute podcast focus), Riverside (recording-focused with basic editing), and Adobe Podcast (AI enhancement but limited editing). Traditional DAWs like Audacity and GarageBand remain the default for budget-conscious creators but offer no transcript-based workflow. Waveform differentiates by being podcast-obsessed: every feature is designed for spoken-word content, from smart silence detection to cross-talk handling to show-notes generation.

Our ICP is the weekly podcaster producing 1-4 episodes per month who currently spends 3-6 hours per episode on post-production. This represents roughly 1.8 million creators globally. With an average willingness-to-pay of $19/month, our SOM is approximately $410M annually.

Go-to-market is community-driven: partnerships with podcast hosting platforms (Buzzsprout, Transistor, Podbean), presence in podcasting subreddits and Facebook groups, and a YouTube channel demonstrating real editing workflows. Our free tier (2 hours/month of transcription and editing) converts at 14% to paid plans, with the highest conversion trigger being the filler-word removal feature.

name: Prisma
tagline: 3D assets for games — generated, not modeled.
description: Prisma generates production-quality 3D models, textures, and animations from text descriptions and reference images. Purpose-built for game developers who need dozens of assets fast without sacrificing art direction. From props to characters, Prisma outputs game-engine-ready files with proper topology, UV maps, and LOD variants.
mission:
Game development has a brutal asset bottleneck. A single environment in a modern game can require hundreds of unique 3D models, each needing proper topology, UV unwrapping, texturing, rigging, and LOD optimization. Even experienced 3D artists spend days on a single character model. For indie studios, the math simply doesn't work — you can't ship a visually competitive game when your art pipeline moves at human speed.

Prisma exists to break the asset bottleneck. We're not building a novelty tool that generates impressive-looking renders with broken geometry underneath. We're building a production pipeline that outputs game-engine-ready assets with clean topology, efficient UV layouts, PBR texture sets, and multiple LOD variants. Every model we generate can go straight into Unity or Unreal without manual cleanup.

Our approach is game-art-native. We trained our models on game assets, not general 3D datasets. This means Prisma understands polygon budgets, knows that a background prop needs different topology than a hero character, and generates textures that tile correctly on modular environment pieces. It thinks like a technical artist because we built it with technical artists.

The studio of the future ships great games with small teams. Not because the games are simpler, but because AI handles the production volume while humans focus on art direction, narrative, and the creative decisions that make a game feel authored rather than generated. Prisma is the asset pipeline for that studio.
marketResearch:
The game development tools market is valued at $3.2B in 2025, with 3D asset creation representing the largest subsegment at approximately $1.4B. AI-assisted 3D generation is projected to grow at 42% CAGR through 2029 as game studios seek to reduce the 60-70% of production budgets consumed by art asset creation. The addressable market for game-ready AI asset generation is approximately $2.1B.

Competitors span two categories: general 3D generators (Meshy, Kaedim, Luma AI) that produce impressive visuals but lack game-production optimization, and traditional DCC tools (Blender, Maya, 3ds Max) augmented with AI plugins. No existing solution combines text-to-3D generation with game-engine-ready output including proper topology, LODs, PBR textures, and animation-ready rigging.

Prisma's technical moat is our game-art training data and engine-specific output optimization. Models generated for Unreal include Nanite-optimized meshes; Unity outputs include properly configured prefabs. Our topology is consistently quad-dominant with edge flow suitable for animation, not the triangulated soup that competing tools produce.

Our ICP includes indie studios (2-20 people), mid-size studios needing to accelerate pre-production, and solo developers building ambitious projects. We price per-asset with subscription tiers: Free (10 assets/month), Pro ($39/month, 100 assets), and Studio ($149/month, unlimited with API access). Early traction includes partnerships with three indie studios on Steam's trending list.

name: Inkwell
tagline: Write the story. Let AI draw the panels.
description: Inkwell is an AI-powered comic creation studio where writers craft narratives and the AI generates consistent artwork panel by panel. Maintain character consistency across entire issues, switch between art styles, and export print-ready pages. Comics and graphic novels, from script to shelf, without needing to draw a single line.
mission:
Every writer has a graphic novel trapped inside them. The medium is uniquely powerful — combining visual storytelling with narrative depth in ways that neither prose nor film can match. But the barrier to entry is impossibly high. Creating a single issue requires hundreds of individually drawn, inked, and colored panels with consistent characters across every page. Unless you can draw at a professional level or afford to hire an artist for months, your story stays a script.

Inkwell was built to break that barrier. We believe the creative bottleneck in comics should be storytelling, not illustration skill. Our platform lets writers focus on what they do best — crafting dialogue, pacing scenes, building worlds — while AI handles the visual execution with a level of consistency that previous tools couldn't achieve.

Character consistency is where other AI art tools fail catastrophically for sequential art. A hero who looks different in every panel isn't a character — it's a collage. Inkwell solves this with character locking: define a character once and our system maintains their appearance, proportions, and style across hundreds of panels. Same face. Same build. Same costume details. This isn't trivial — it's the core technical challenge we've spent two years solving.

Our ambition extends beyond making comics easier to make. We want to expand who makes them. The comics industry has been gatekept by illustration ability for a century. Inkwell opens the medium to the millions of writers, worldbuilders, and storytellers who think visually but can't draw — and in doing so, we believe entirely new kinds of stories will emerge.
marketResearch:
The global comic book and graphic novel market is valued at $14.2B in 2025, with digital comics growing at 9.1% CAGR. The adjacent market of webtoons and digital sequential art is exploding — platforms like Webtoon and Tapas collectively reach 180M+ monthly users. The AI creative tools market intersects here at roughly $2.6B, with comic-specific AI tools representing an early but fast-growing $340M segment.

Competitors include general AI image generators (Midjourney, DALL-E) which lack panel consistency, comic-specific tools like ComicAI and Neural Canvas which handle simple strips but not long-form narratives, and traditional digital art tools (Clip Studio Paint, Procreate) which still require drawing skill. Inkwell is unique in combining narrative-aware panel generation with cross-issue character consistency.

Our key differentiator is the Character Persistence Engine — a proprietary system that maintains visual identity across unlimited panels. Combined with panel-aware composition (AI understands comic page layouts, speech bubble placement, and visual flow), Inkwell is the first tool that can produce a 24-page comic issue where characters look consistent from cover to back page.

Target segments include aspiring comic creators (25M+ globally who consume but can't create), indie authors looking to adapt their novels, educators creating visual learning materials, and professional writers prototyping visual narratives before hiring illustrators. Pricing: Free (5 pages/month), Creator ($24/month, 50 pages), and Publisher ($69/month, unlimited pages with print-ready export).

name: Cadence
tagline: Licensed music for creators who actually care about music.
description: Cadence is a music licensing marketplace connecting independent musicians with content creators. Every track is pre-cleared for YouTube, TikTok, podcasts, and commercial use. No copyright strikes, no claim disputes, no royalty surprises. Creators find the perfect track. Musicians earn real money. Everyone's license is clean.
mission:
The music licensing industry is broken from both sides. Creators wade through millions of generic stock tracks, terrified of copyright strikes that can tank a channel overnight. Musicians watch their work get stolen or earn fractions of a cent through streaming while stock music libraries pay flat buyout fees that don't reflect actual usage.

Cadence was founded to fix the transaction, not just the catalog. We built a marketplace where independent artists set their own prices, retain ownership of their masters, and earn usage-based royalties that grow as a creator's content grows. On the other side, creators get instant, unambiguous licenses with automated Content ID whitelisting — no more disputing claims or worrying about monetization being stolen by rights-holders.

Our catalog is curated, not flooded. We reject 70% of submissions to maintain quality parity with custom composition at a fraction of the cost. Every track on Cadence is produced to broadcast standard, properly mastered, and tagged with mood, energy, tempo, and instrumentation metadata that makes discovery genuinely useful rather than keyword roulette.

We believe music licensing should feel like collaboration, not a legal transaction. When a creator finds the perfect track for their video, it should be a moment of creative alignment — not a moment of anxiety about whether they'll get a copyright notice three months later. And when a musician's track scores a viral video, they should share in that success, not receive a one-time $50 buyout.
marketResearch:
The music licensing and sync market is valued at $5.8B globally in 2025, with the creator economy segment (YouTubers, podcasters, social media creators) growing at 28% CAGR. An estimated 50M content creators need licensed music regularly, yet 63% report difficulty finding quality tracks they can afford and trust to be properly cleared.

Competitors include Epidemic Sound ($200M+ ARR, subscription model but limited to their in-house catalog), Artlist (growing but similar closed-catalog approach), Musicbed (premium positioning, high prices), and free/low-cost libraries like Pixabay Music and YouTube's Audio Library (poor quality and limited selection). Cadence differentiates as a two-sided marketplace: open to independent artists while maintaining curation standards, with transparent usage-based pricing rather than all-you-can-eat subscriptions.

Our marketplace model creates a natural moat: more quality artists attract more creators, more usage generates more artist earnings, attracting more artists. We take a 20% platform fee — lower than Spotify's effective cut and dramatically more transparent. Artists on Cadence earn an average of $340/track/month versus $0.003-$0.005 per stream on Spotify.

Our SOM targets mid-tier content creators (10K-1M followers) producing weekly content across YouTube, TikTok, and podcasts, representing approximately $1.4B in annual music licensing spend. GTM strategy combines creator community partnerships, artist referral programs, and integration with major video editing tools (Premiere Pro, DaVinci Resolve, CapCut).

name: Moodboard
tagline: Visual research, organized. Finally.
description: Moodboard is a collaborative visual research platform for design teams. Collect references from anywhere on the web, organize them into spatial canvases with AI-powered clustering, and share living moodboards that stay in sync across your team. Stop drowning in Pinterest boards and Figma frames full of screenshots.
mission:
The visual research phase of design is simultaneously the most important and the most chaotic. Before a single pixel gets pushed, designers spend hours — sometimes days — collecting references, screenshots, color palettes, typography samples, and inspiration from across the web. This research shapes every downstream decision. And yet it lives in the most disorganized places imaginable: browser bookmarks, Pinterest boards, scattered Figma frames, and Slack threads that disappear into the void.

Moodboard was born from watching this chaos repeat across every design team we worked with. The research is critical, but the tools are afterthoughts. Pinterest wasn't built for professional design research. Figma's infinite canvas is a powerful design tool, not a research organizer. And dedicated tools like Eagle or Milanote don't understand visual design well enough to help with organization — they're just folders with thumbnails.

We built Moodboard to be the first tool that actually understands visual research. Our AI analyzes collected references not just by tags or titles, but by visual properties: color palette, composition style, typography approach, texture, and mood. It can cluster your references automatically, suggest related imagery you haven't found yet, and identify the common visual threads across a messy collection of 200 references that your team has been staring at for a week.

Collaborative design research shouldn't be an oxymoron. When a team of four designers is researching a rebrand, they should be able to work in the same visual space, see each other's additions in real-time, and converge on a direction together rather than merging four separate Pinterest boards in a meeting.
marketResearch:
The design collaboration tools market is valued at $7.8B in 2025, with Figma, Miro, and Canva dominating broad collaboration. The niche of visual research and moodboarding tools — including Eagle, Milanote, Pinterest business, and Savee — represents approximately $620M in annual spend. This segment is growing at 22% CAGR driven by remote design teams needing better asynchronous visual communication.

Current solutions fall into three categories: consumer platforms repurposed for professional use (Pinterest — good discovery, terrible organization), general-purpose canvases (Miro, FigJam — lack visual intelligence), and asset management tools (Eagle, Ember — local-first, weak collaboration). No existing tool combines web clipping, AI-powered visual analysis, spatial organization, and real-time team collaboration.

Moodboard's technical differentiator is our Visual DNA engine — a proprietary system that analyzes every collected reference across 23 visual dimensions (color distribution, compositional balance, typographic style, texture density, etc.) and uses these vectors for intelligent clustering, similarity search, and trend identification. This lets design leads ask questions like 'show me the references that share this color energy but have more geometric compositions.'

Our ICP is design teams of 3-15 people at agencies, tech companies, and brand studios. Average contract value is $18/seat/month with team sizes averaging 7 seats. Early adoption is strongest at branding agencies where visual research is billable work. GTM combines Figma community presence, design Twitter/X thought leadership, and partnerships with design education platforms.

name: Reel
tagline: Short-form video that doesn't take all day to make.
description: Reel is a browser-based short-form video editor built for speed. Auto-captioning, one-click templates, smart cut detection, and platform-specific export for TikTok, Reels, and Shorts. Go from raw footage to published content in minutes, not hours. Designed for creators and social media teams who post daily.
mission:
Short-form video has eaten the internet. TikTok, Instagram Reels, YouTube Shorts — collectively they consume more attention than any other content format. For creators and brands, posting regularly isn't optional; it's survival. But the production workflow is still agonizingly slow. Shoot a video, transfer it to your desktop, open a heavyweight editor, add captions manually frame by frame, export at the right aspect ratio, and upload to three different platforms. For a 60-second video, you easily burn two hours.

Reel exists because the editing tool should match the speed of the format. Short-form video is meant to be quick, raw, and high-volume. The editor should be too. We built everything in the browser — no downloads, no installations, no waiting for imports. Drag in your clip and start editing immediately.

Our killer feature is intelligent auto-captioning with style templates. Captions aren't just accessibility anymore — they're a creative element that defines your content's visual identity. Reel generates word-level accurate captions and lets you style them with animations, highlights, and emoji reactions in a few clicks. The same captioning that takes 45 minutes in Premiere takes 30 seconds in Reel.

We're building the production stack that makes daily posting sustainable. Not by lowering quality, but by eliminating every mechanical step between having footage and having a post. When creation takes minutes instead of hours, creators can actually experiment, iterate, and find what resonates — instead of burning their energy on production busywork.
marketResearch:
The video editing software market is valued at $4.6B in 2025, with the mobile and browser-based segment growing at 31% CAGR. Short-form video tools specifically represent a $1.8B opportunity driven by 200M+ active content creators globally. The average creator spends 6.3 hours per week on video editing, creating massive demand for tools that compress this workflow.

Direct competitors include CapCut (ByteDance's free editor with 400M+ downloads, dominant but primarily mobile), Opus Clip (AI-powered clip extraction from long-form, narrow use case), and traditional editors like Premiere Pro and DaVinci Resolve (powerful but overkill for short-form). Browser-based competitors like Kapwing and Veed.io are closest but lack the speed-focused UX and intelligent captioning depth that daily creators need.

Reel differentiates on three axes: browser-native speed (no downloads, instant import, sub-second previews), captioning as a first-class creative tool (not an afterthought checkbox), and platform intelligence (we understand TikTok's safe zones, Reels' aspect ratios, and Shorts' metadata requirements, exporting optimized versions for each). Our Smart Cut feature uses transcript analysis to identify and remove dead air, hesitations, and off-topic tangents automatically.

Our ICP spans solo creators posting 5+ times per week, social media teams at D2C brands, and agency teams managing multiple client accounts. Pricing is freemium: Free (3 exports/month with watermark), Pro ($14/month, unlimited exports, all caption styles), and Team ($29/seat/month, brand kits, shared templates, approval workflows).

name: Typecast
tagline: Your voice. Your audiobook. No studio required.
description: Typecast creates studio-quality AI voice clones for audiobook narration. Record 30 minutes of your voice, and Typecast generates a narrator that sounds like you — with natural pacing, emotional range, and consistent delivery across an entire book. Authors and publishers produce professional audiobooks at a fraction of traditional recording costs.
mission:
Only 7% of published books have an audiobook edition. Not because demand is low — audiobook revenue grew 25% last year — but because production is prohibitively expensive. A professional narrator charges $200-$400 per finished hour. A 10-hour audiobook costs $2,000-$4,000 in narrator fees alone, plus studio time, editing, and mastering. For indie authors earning $500-$2,000 per title, the math doesn't work.

Typecast was built to democratize audiobook production. We don't use generic text-to-speech voices that sound robotic and lifeless. We clone the author's own voice — or let them choose from a library of professional narrator voices — and produce narration with natural pacing, emotional inflection, and the subtle prosodic variations that make audiobooks engaging rather than exhausting to listen to.

The technical challenge is enormous. Audiobook narration isn't just reading text aloud. It's performance. A great narrator handles dialogue with distinct character voices, adjusts pacing for tension and release, and maintains consistency across 80,000+ words. Our models are trained specifically for long-form narration, understanding paragraph-level context to deliver appropriate emotional tone, and maintaining voice stability across chapters that might take 12+ hours to render.

We see a future where every book has an audiobook. Where indie authors can reach the 45% of book consumers who prefer audio. Where publishers can produce audiobook editions simultaneously with print and digital, not months or years later. Typecast is the production engine that makes that future economically viable.
marketResearch:
The global audiobook market reached $7.8B in 2025 and is projected to hit $15B by 2030 at 14% CAGR. Yet supply is severely constrained: only 7% of the 4M+ books published annually get audiobook editions. The AI voice technology market, valued at $4.2B, is converging with audiobook production to create a new category worth an estimated $1.6B by 2028.

Competitors include ElevenLabs (powerful voice cloning but general-purpose, not optimized for long-form narration), Google and Amazon's TTS services (adequate for navigation, inadequate for storytelling), DeepZen (audiobook-focused but limited voice variety and high pricing), and Apple's AI narration (limited to Apple Books, restricted voice options). Typecast differentiates by combining author voice cloning with narration-specific training that handles dialogue, pacing, and emotional range at book length.

Our core technical moat is long-form coherence. Competitors produce impressive 30-second samples that degrade over minutes. Typecast maintains voice quality, emotional consistency, and prosodic naturalness across 10+ hour narrations. Our Chapter Context Engine reads ahead to understand narrative arc and adjusts delivery accordingly — quieter for intimate scenes, faster for action sequences, distinct voices for different characters.

Primary segments include indie authors (2.3M self-published titles annually, $29/book pricing), small publishers (500-5,000 titles/year, volume licensing), and corporate/educational publishers needing training materials and course narration. GTM starts with integrations into self-publishing platforms (KDP, IngramSpark, Draft2Digital) where authors are already producing books without audiobook editions.

name: Easel
tagline: Digital paint that feels like the real thing.
description: Easel is a digital painting application built around natural brush physics. Real bristle simulation, paint mixing that behaves like actual pigment, and canvas textures you can feel through your stylus. No layers palette, no vector tools, no feature bloat — just the purest digital painting experience for artists who care about the craft.
mission:
Digital painting tools have spent thirty years adding features and forgetting what painting actually feels like. Photoshop has 300+ brushes but none that behave like a real sable round. Procreate is elegant but its brushes are stamp-based simulations. Corel Painter comes closest but it's buried under decades of enterprise feature creep. The tools optimized for painters — actual painters — don't exist.

Easel started from a radically simple premise: what if we built a painting app for people who love painting? Not photo manipulation, not graphic design, not illustration workflows — painting. The act of loading a brush with color, touching it to a textured surface, and watching the pigment spread, thin, and blend in ways that respond to pressure, angle, and speed.

Our brush engine simulates individual bristles interacting with canvas texture at the fiber level. When you press harder, the bristles splay. When paint runs low, the stroke dries out naturally. When two wet colors meet, they mix the way real pigments do — following subtractive color theory, not additive RGB blending. The result is a painting experience that makes artists forget they're using a screen.

We deliberately left features out. No layers palette (paint over it or scrape it off, like real paint). No selection tools. No filters. Easel is an opinionated tool that says: if you want to paint, we'll give you the best digital painting experience ever built. If you want to do graphic design, use a graphic design tool. This focus lets us pour all of our engineering into the one thing that matters — how the brush feels on the canvas.
marketResearch:
The digital art software market is valued at $3.9B in 2025, with painting-specific applications representing approximately $680M. The growing overlap between fine art and digital tools is driven by 15M+ digital artists globally, with the traditional/fine art crossover segment growing at 18% CAGR as established painters explore digital workflows and digital artists seek more natural, tactile experiences.

Direct competitors include Procreate ($12.8M annual revenue, dominant on iPad but stamp-based brushes), Corel Painter ($200+ perpetual license, powerful but complex and aging), Adobe Fresco (free tier but shallow brush physics, part of Adobe ecosystem), and Rebelle (closest in natural media simulation but limited platform support and rough UX). Easel occupies a unique position: production-grade brush physics with the simplicity of a focused, modern app.

Our technical moat is the Bristle Physics Engine — a real-time simulation of individual brush fibers interacting with canvas surface topology. Unlike stamp-based engines (which tile a pre-drawn brush shape), our engine calculates bristle flex, paint load, and surface friction on every frame. This produces brush behavior that traditional painters describe as 'the first digital tool that doesn't feel like a computer.'

Target segments include traditional artists transitioning to digital (5M+), digital artists seeking natural media aesthetics, art educators teaching painting fundamentals, and concept artists who prefer a painterly workflow. Pricing: $39.99 one-time purchase (iPad/desktop), with optional brush pack and canvas texture subscriptions at $4.99/month. Our App Store rating is 4.9/5 with particular praise for brush feel.

name: Montage
tagline: Remote video teams, one seamless timeline.
description: Montage is a video collaboration platform for distributed production teams. Editors, directors, colorists, and sound designers work on the same project simultaneously from anywhere. Real-time timeline sync, frame-accurate commenting, version branching, and role-based workflows replace the fragmented mess of shared drives and review links.
mission:
Video production went remote but the tools didn't follow. Post-production workflows still assume everyone is in the same edit suite. Editors upload cuts to Frame.io for review. Directors leave timecoded comments that get manually translated back into timeline edits. Colorists receive exported XMLs that don't round-trip cleanly. Sound designers work with stems that are already outdated by the time they receive them. The entire process is a chain of exports, uploads, downloads, and version conflicts.

Montage replaces that chain with a single, synchronized workspace. When an editor makes a cut, the director sees it in real-time. When a colorist adjusts a grade, it's immediately visible in the editor's timeline. When a sound designer adds a mix, everyone hears it. No exports. No uploads. No 'which version is current?' The project is one living thing that the whole team shapes together.

We built this because our founding team spent a decade in post-production, and the pandemic made the existing workflow's fragility impossible to ignore. Remote editors wasted 30% of their time on file management. Review cycles that should take hours stretched into days of async back-and-forth. Version control was a spreadsheet and a prayer. The creative work suffered because the logistics consumed everyone's energy.

Montage is the infrastructure layer that makes distributed video production feel like being in the same room. Not through video calls and screen shares, but through a shared creative workspace where every team member's contribution is immediately integrated into the living project.

The video post-production software market is valued at $4.1B in 2025, with cloud-based and collaborative solutions growing at 26% CAGR. No existing platform offers true simultaneous multi-role editing on a shared timeline.

Montage's technical moat is our Conflict-Free Replicated Timeline (CRDT-based) that allows multiple editors to work on the same sequence without merge conflicts. Combined with role-based access (editors can cut, colorists can grade, sound designers can mix — each in their lane without stepping on each other), Montage enables genuine real-time collaboration rather than turn-taking.

Our ICP includes independent production studios (15-50 person teams), advertising agencies with video departments, corporate video teams at large enterprises, and YouTube production teams with distributed editors. Pricing starts at $49/seat/month for teams, with enterprise plans including dedicated rendering infrastructure, compliance features, and custom integrations. name: Vector
tagline: Electrify your fleet without the guesswork
description: Vector helps logistics companies plan and execute fleet electrification with confidence. From route-level energy modeling to charging infrastructure placement, we turn the messy EV transition into a phased, data-driven rollout that actually pencils out.
mission:
Every major logistics company has an electrification target on paper. Almost none of them have a credible plan to get there. The gap between commitment and execution is enormous — fleet managers face a maze of vehicle options, charging infrastructure decisions, utility rate structures, and route constraints that make the transition feel impossibly complex.

Vector was built to close that gap. We model every route in your fleet against real-world EV performance data — accounting for payload, terrain, weather, and charging availability — to produce a phased electrification roadmap that maximizes ROI at each stage. No more pilot programs that stall after five trucks.

Our founding team spent years at fleet management companies watching electrification initiatives die in spreadsheet purgatory. The technology exists to make fleets electric. What's missing is an intelligent planning layer that tells you which vehicles to replace first, where to put chargers, how to negotiate utility rates, and when the economics flip in your favor.

We're starting with regional delivery fleets in the 50-500 vehicle range — large enough to benefit from structured planning, small enough to move quickly. Our first customers are saving an average of $12,000 per vehicle annually once they transition, and our planning tool cuts the typical 18-month analysis phase down to weeks.
marketResearch:
The commercial fleet electrification market is expected to reach $180B globally by 2030, with fleet management software for EVs representing an $8.5B addressable market. North American medium-duty delivery fleets — our beachhead — account for roughly $2.3B of that. Our initial SOM targets regional carriers and last-mile delivery companies with 50-500 vehicles, representing $380M in near-term software spend.

description: Anchor is a lease management platform for growing companies navigating commercial real estate. We centralize lease data, automate critical date tracking, and surface cost-saving opportunities hidden in your portfolio — so your ops team stops drowning in PDFs.
mission:
Growing companies sign commercial leases the way most people sign gym memberships — with optimism and very little ongoing attention. Then renewal deadlines sneak up, escalation clauses kick in unnoticed, and CAM reconciliations arrive as incomprehensible spreadsheets. By the time anyone realizes there was a problem, the leverage is gone.

Anchor exists because we watched this pattern repeat at every company we worked at. The CFO finds out about an auto-renewal two weeks too late. The ops manager discovers they've been overpaying common area maintenance for three years. The head of real estate keeps critical dates in a personal calendar that nobody else can access.

We're building the system of record for commercial leases that growing companies actually deserve. Not enterprise software designed for REITs with 500-person real estate teams, but a focused tool that extracts the critical data from your leases, tracks every deadline, benchmarks your rates against market data, and flags when it's time to negotiate or exit.

Our long-term play is to become the intelligence layer between tenants and their real estate decisions. When you're ready to expand, Anchor already knows your lease terms, your space utilization patterns, and the market conditions in your target cities. The best real estate decision is an informed one, and right now most growing companies are flying blind.

tagline: Pick faster. Walk less. Ship more.
description: Silo optimizes warehouse slotting — the art of deciding where every SKU lives on the shelf. By analyzing order patterns, pick sequences, and velocity data, we rearrange your warehouse so pickers walk less and throughput climbs. No racking changes required.
mission:
In most warehouses, products end up where they end up. Fast movers sit in the back because that's where they were put during the last big receiving day. Slow movers hog prime pick slots because nobody reassigned them when demand shifted. The result: pickers walk miles of unnecessary distance every shift, and throughput hits a ceiling that no amount of overtime can fix.

Silo was born in a 200,000 square foot fulfillment center where we watched pickers average 8.3 miles per shift — not because the warehouse was large, but because it was badly slotted. We ran a manual reslotting project that took six weeks of analysis and cut pick time by 22%. Then demand patterns changed two months later and we were back to square one.

That experience made one thing clear: warehouse slotting isn't a project, it's a continuous optimization problem. Silo treats it that way. We ingest your WMS data, analyze order co-occurrence patterns, velocity curves, and physical constraints, then generate reslotting recommendations that your team can execute in waves — no forklift rodeo required.

We're not replacing your WMS. We're making the one you have dramatically more effective by ensuring every item lives in the right place at the right time. Our customers see 15-30% pick time reductions within the first reslotting wave, and the gains compound as Silo continuously adapts to shifting demand.

name: Waypoint
tagline: Last-mile delivery that stops burning money on wrong turns
description: Waypoint optimizes last-mile delivery routes in real time, balancing delivery windows, driver capacity, traffic patterns, and fuel costs. Built for regional delivery fleets that need enterprise-grade routing without enterprise-grade budgets.
mission:
Last-mile delivery is the most expensive, most chaotic, and most customer-visible part of the supply chain. A single bad routing decision cascades — late deliveries, angry customers, exhausted drivers, and margins that evaporate with every extra mile driven.

Waypoint was founded by a team that ran delivery operations for a regional grocery chain and lived through the daily chaos firsthand. Dispatchers using Google Maps and tribal knowledge to plan 200 deliveries across 30 drivers. Routes built on assumptions from last Tuesday's traffic. Delivery windows missed because nobody accounted for a school zone on Third Street.

We built the routing engine we wished we'd had: one that ingests real-time traffic, historical delivery times, customer time windows, vehicle capacity, and driver hours-of-service constraints — then produces routes that are genuinely optimal, not just directionally correct. And it does this in minutes, not the hours it takes a human dispatcher.

Our vision is simple: every regional delivery fleet should have access to the same routing intelligence that Amazon and FedEx spend billions developing in-house. The technology isn't the hard part anymore. The hard part was making it accessible, affordable, and fast enough for a dispatcher to use at 5am before the trucks roll out.
marketResearch:
The route optimization software market is valued at $7.4B and growing at 11.2% CAGR, driven by e-commerce growth and rising fuel costs. The last-mile segment specifically represents $3.1B of this market. Our SAM focuses on regional delivery fleets in North America — grocery, beverage, building materials, and home services — with 10-200 vehicles, representing roughly $850M. Our SOM targets the eastern US corridor, approximately $140M.

The competitive field includes enterprise platforms (Descartes, ORTEC, PTV Group) with complex implementations and six-figure annual costs, mid-market tools (OptimoRoute, Routific, Route4Me) with varying levels of sophistication, and free tools (Google Maps, Circuit) that lack multi-constraint optimization. Waypoint positions between mid-market and enterprise: real optimization that handles complex constraints (time windows, vehicle types, driver skills, live traffic) at a price point mid-market fleets can absorb.

Our differentiation is speed and accuracy in constrained environments. Most competitors optimize for distance; Waypoint optimizes for total delivery cost including fuel, labor, failed delivery penalties, and customer satisfaction scores. Our engine produces routes in under 90 seconds for 500-stop problems, versus 10-30 minutes for comparable solutions.

GTM strategy combines content marketing targeting fleet operations managers with partnerships with fleet management platforms (Fleetio, Azuga) and delivery management software providers. Free tier handles up to 50 stops/day, converting to paid plans for multi-driver, multi-depot operations.

Member lifecycle management, automated billing with flexible plan structures, room and desk booking with real-time availability, access control integration, community features, and the analytics operators need to make smart decisions about pricing and space utilization.

name: Manifest
tagline: Stop overpaying on freight. Start auditing automatically.
description: Manifest automates freight bill auditing and payment for shippers who are tired of overpaying carriers. We catch billing errors, duplicate charges, and contract non-compliance that manual processes miss — then handle payment so your AP team can focus on literally anything else.
mission:
Freight invoices are wrong more often than most shippers realize. Industry studies put the error rate between 5-15%, but in our experience it's often higher. Duplicate charges, incorrect accessorial fees, weight discrepancies, fuel surcharge miscalculations, and rates that don't match contracted terms. Multiply that by thousands of shipments per month and you're bleeding money you'll never recover.

Manifest started because our founder spent a decade in logistics finance and watched companies hire entire teams just to check invoices against contracts — a process that's tedious, error-prone, and always behind. The worst part: even the best manual audit catches maybe 60% of errors. The other 40% gets paid without question.

We built an engine that ingests every freight invoice, matches it against your carrier contracts and shipment records, flags discrepancies with specific dollar amounts and root causes, and either auto-approves clean invoices or routes exceptions to your team with all the context they need to resolve them. No more spreadsheet reconciliation. No more paying invoices on faith.

But auditing is just the entry point. Our vision is to become the financial intelligence layer for freight operations — helping shippers understand their true landed cost per shipment, identify carrier performance trends, and negotiate better contracts with data they've never had access to before.

They're not real estate professionals — they're teachers, engineers, and small business owners who own a duplex or a handful of rental units as an investment. And the software industry has mostly ignored them.

Enterprise property management platforms like Yardi and AppFolio are designed for professional management companies with hundreds of units and dedicated office staff. They're powerful, expensive, and wildly over-engineered for someone managing four apartments. On the other end, tools like Cozy (now Apartments.com) have been hollowed out or absorbed into platforms that prioritize listing revenue over landlord experience.

Domicile fills this gap with genuine care for the small landlord. We automate the operational burden — rent collection with automatic late fees and receipts, maintenance requests that tenants submit through the app instead of 11pm text messages, lease management with e-signatures, and accounting that generates Schedule E tax reports without a bookkeeper.

We believe small landlords provide essential housing in communities across America, and they deserve tools that respect their time and intelligence. Not dumbed-down versions of enterprise software, and not consumer apps that treat property management as an afterthought.

name: Berth
tagline: Port scheduling that actually keeps ships moving
description: Berth optimizes dock and port scheduling for maritime terminals, reducing vessel wait times and maximizing berth utilization. We replace the whiteboards, phone calls, and spreadsheets that most ports still use to manage the most expensive parking spots on earth.
mission:
A single container vessel sitting idle at anchor costs between $30,000 and $80,000 per day. Multiply that by the dozens of ships waiting outside every major port and you start to understand the scale of the scheduling problem in maritime logistics. Ports are the critical bottleneck in global trade, and most of them still coordinate berth assignments with phone calls, emails, and whiteboards.

Berth was founded by a team with deep roots in port operations who saw this inefficiency from the inside. The problem isn't that port operators lack skill — it's that they lack tools. A modern container terminal juggles vessel arrivals, tide windows, crane availability, berth depth restrictions, cargo type compatibility, and labor scheduling simultaneously. Doing this in spreadsheets means decisions are reactive instead of optimized.

We built a scheduling engine purpose-built for the unique constraints of port operations. Berth considers vessel dimensions, draft requirements, cargo handling equipment, terminal operating system data, tide tables, and weather forecasts to produce berth schedules that maximize throughput while minimizing vessel wait times.

Our initial focus is mid-size ports and private terminals that lack the IT budgets of mega-ports like Rotterdam or Shanghai but face the same scheduling complexity. These are the ports where a 15% improvement in berth utilization means the difference between profitability and requesting government subsidies.
marketResearch:
The port management software market is projected to reach $6.8B by 2030, with berth scheduling and terminal optimization representing approximately $1.9B. The global shift toward port digitization — driven by congestion crises, emissions regulations, and vessel size increases — is accelerating adoption. Our SAM targets mid-size container and bulk terminals in North America, Europe, and Southeast Asia, roughly $520M. Our initial SOM focuses on US and Canadian ports with 200K-2M TEU annual throughput, approximately $65M.

Competitors include terminal operating system (TOS) vendors like Navis (Cargotec) and TBA Group that offer berth planning as modules within larger systems, standalone optimization tools from companies like INFORM and PortLink, and in-house Excel-based systems used by 60%+ of mid-size ports. Berth differentiates through standalone deployment (no TOS replacement required), real-time optimization that adapts to disruptions, and a modern UX that operations teams can actually use without weeks of training.

Our GTM strategy targets port operations directors and terminal managers through industry conferences (TOC, AAPA), partnerships with maritime consultancies, and a free simulation tool that lets ports model their current operations and see optimization potential before committing. Sales cycles are 3-6 months with average contract values of $120K-$400K annually depending on terminal size.

Key market tailwinds: the IMO's 2030 carbon intensity targets are pushing ports to reduce idle time (less fuel burned at anchor), chassis and container dwell time regulations in California, and the trend toward port automation that requires digital scheduling as a foundation layer.

name: Threshold
tagline: Your building is wasting energy. We can see exactly where.
description: Threshold is a smart building energy management platform that connects to existing BMS and IoT sensors to identify waste, automate savings, and help commercial buildings hit sustainability targets — without replacing any hardware.
mission:
Commercial buildings consume 35% of all electricity in the United States, and studies consistently show that 20-30% of that energy is wasted. HVAC systems heat empty floors. Lights burn in unoccupied conference rooms. Chillers run at full capacity when outdoor air could do the job. The waste isn't from bad equipment — it's from dumb controls and zero visibility.

Threshold exists because we believe every commercial building already has the data it needs to cut energy costs dramatically. The BMS has temperature readings. The meters have consumption data. The access control system knows which floors are occupied. The problem is that these systems don't talk to each other, and nobody is watching the patterns at 2am when the real waste happens.

We connect to the systems your building already has — BACnet BMS, smart meters, occupancy sensors, weather feeds — and layer on intelligence that identifies waste patterns, automates setpoint adjustments, and surfaces the changes that will save the most money with the least disruption. No new hardware. No construction. Just software that makes your existing building perform like it was designed to.

Our team comes from the intersection of building science and machine learning. We've operated buildings, designed HVAC systems, and built the models that predict when a chiller is about to fail. Threshold is the tool we wish we'd had: one that turns building data into action without requiring a PhD in mechanical engineering.
marketResearch:
The smart building energy management market is projected to hit $15.3B by 2030, growing at 14% CAGR. Key drivers include ESG reporting mandates (EU CSRD, SEC climate disclosure rules), rising energy costs, and local building performance standards (NYC LL97, Boston BERDO). The compliance pressure alone is creating $4.2B in demand for energy optimization software.

name: Cartage
tagline: The freight marketplace where shippers and carriers actually find each other
description: Cartage is a digital freight marketplace that connects shippers with vetted carriers for LTL, FTL, and drayage loads. Transparent pricing, real-time tracking, and none of the phone tag that makes freight brokerage feel stuck in 1995.
mission:
Shipping freight in America is a $900 billion industry that still runs on phone calls, faxes, and relationships. A shipper with a load to move calls their broker. The broker calls five carriers. Three don't answer. One quotes too high. One can do it but not until Thursday. An hour later, a truck is booked at whatever price emerged from this chaotic process. Repeat 50 times a day.

Cartage was founded because we believe freight matching should work like every other marketplace in 2026 — transparent, instant, and data-driven. Shippers post loads with origin, destination, commodity, and timing. Carriers see loads that match their lanes, equipment, and availability. Pricing is informed by real market data, not whatever the broker feels like quoting.

But we're not naive about why brokers exist. They provide trust, credit, and problem-solving that a simple load board can't replace. So we built Cartage to capture the best parts of brokerage — carrier vetting, payment guarantees, and exception management — while eliminating the worst parts: opacity, phone tag, and the 15-20% margin that ultimately comes out of both sides' pockets.

Our long-term play is building the freight operating system for mid-market shippers. Marketplace access today, freight analytics tomorrow, and eventually, automated procurement that dynamically routes loads across carriers based on cost, reliability, and capacity — without a human broker in the middle.
marketResearch:
The US freight brokerage market generates $90B+ annually, with digital freight brokerages growing at 25% CAGR as shippers demand transparency and carriers seek to fill empty miles. The total addressable market for digital freight matching platforms is approximately $18B. Our SAM targets mid-market shippers ($1M-$50M annual freight spend) and carriers with 5-200 trucks in the US, representing roughly $5.2B. Our SOM focuses on the eastern US LTL and FTL market, approximately $800M.

Competitors include digital freight brokerages (Convoy — paused operations, Uber Freight — scaling back, Loadsmart) that have struggled with unit economics, traditional brokerages going digital (CH Robinson's Navisphere, Echo Global), and load boards (DAT, Truckstop) that offer matching without transaction services. Cartage differentiates by operating as a true two-sided marketplace with transparent pricing — not a digital brokerage that still takes a hidden spread. Our 8% take rate versus the industry's 15-20% margin creates a structural cost advantage.

Our GTM strategy starts with lane density in the I-95 corridor where we can offer reliable carrier coverage. Shippers join through a free RFQ tool that benchmarks their current rates against market data. Carriers are acquired through an app that shows available loads with guaranteed payment terms. Network effects kick in as lane density increases: more carriers means better pricing, which attracts more shippers.

Key market tailwinds: broker fee transparency regulations under consideration, carrier consolidation creating more digitally-savvy fleets, and rising shipper demand for real-time visibility that traditional brokers can't provide.

name: Bastion
tagline: Your network gets attacked every day — now it fights back
description: Bastion runs continuous, autonomous penetration tests against your infrastructure so you find the holes before attackers do. No more annual pen tests that are outdated the day after the report lands.
mission:
Annual penetration tests are a relic. You pay a consultancy six figures, wait three weeks for a PDF, patch the critical findings, and then spend the next eleven months hoping nothing new has broken. Meanwhile, your attack surface changes every time someone pushes code, spins up a cloud instance, or adds an integration.

Bastion was built by red teamers who got tired of writing the same reports for the same clients year after year. We took the methodology of a skilled human pentester — reconnaissance, enumeration, exploitation, lateral movement, reporting — and turned it into a platform that runs continuously against your live infrastructure. Not a vulnerability scanner. An actual attack simulation engine that thinks like an adversary.

Our philosophy is simple: defense without offense is guesswork. You can't know if your controls work until something tries to break them. Bastion tries to break them every single day, then tells you exactly what it found, how it got in, and what to fix first.

We're a team of former offensive security researchers from Mandiant, NCC Group, and the US Cyber Command. We've spent careers breaking into organizations and we believe that capability should be democratized — not locked behind $200K consulting engagements that happen once a year.

Competitors include legacy pen test firms (Bishop Fox, Rapid7), vulnerability scanners (Qualys, Tenable) that lack exploitation capability, and BAS platforms (SafeBreach, AttackIQ, Pentera). Bastion differentiates by combining real exploitation with continuous cadence — we don't simulate attacks, we execute them safely using containment boundaries and rollback mechanisms. Our finding severity accuracy is 94% vs. the 60-70% typical of scanner-based approaches.

Primary buyers are CISOs and security engineering leads at companies with 200-5,000 employees, particularly in fintech, healthcare, and SaaS. The pain point is universal: compliance mandates require pen testing, but annual assessments provide a false sense of security. name: Tessera
tagline: Hire for what people can do, not where they went to school
description: Tessera is a skills-based hiring platform that replaces resume screening with structured skill assessments and blind evaluation. It removes the biases baked into traditional hiring — school name, employer brand, gaps in employment — and surfaces candidates based on demonstrated ability.
mission:
The resume is a terrible predictor of job performance. Study after study shows that unstructured resume screening introduces bias at every level — against women, against minorities, against career changers, against anyone whose path doesn't match the recruiter's mental model of what a "good" candidate looks like. And yet resumes remain the foundation of nearly every hiring process on Earth.

Tessera was founded on a radical but evidence-backed premise: if you evaluate candidates on what they can do instead of where they've been, you get better hires and more diverse teams simultaneously. These aren't competing goals — they're the same goal, because bias is noise, and removing noise improves signal.

Our platform replaces the resume screen with structured skill evaluations designed by I/O psychologists and calibrated to actual job performance. Candidates complete relevant assessments — coding challenges, writing samples, case analyses, design exercises — and their work is evaluated blindly by reviewers who never see a name, photo, school, or employer. Only skills and demonstrated ability.

We're not anti-resume as a philosophical stance. We're anti-resume because the data is overwhelming: structured skill evaluation predicts job performance 2-4x better than resume screening. Companies that switch to skills-based hiring see broader talent pools, faster time-to-hire, higher offer acceptance rates, and dramatically better diversity outcomes. It's not a trade-off. It's strictly better.

name: Lockstep
tagline: Know what's in your supply chain before attackers do
description: Lockstep scans your open-source dependencies for security vulnerabilities, malicious packages, license risks, and maintainer health signals. It goes beyond CVE databases to assess the actual risk of every package in your dependency tree.
mission:
The average modern application has over 1,200 dependencies. Most engineering teams can name maybe a dozen of them. The rest are transitive — pulled in by libraries that pulled in other libraries — forming an invisible supply chain that nobody audited and everybody trusts implicitly.

Then Log4Shell happened. Then the ua-parser-js compromise. Then the colors.js sabotage. Each incident reminded the industry of something supply chain security researchers had been saying for years: your application is only as secure as your least-maintained transitive dependency.

Lockstep was founded to make supply chain risk visible and manageable. We don't just check CVE databases — that's table stakes. We analyze maintainer activity, funding status, bus factor, known vulnerabilities in transitive deps, typosquatting risk, behavioral anomalies in recent releases, and license compliance across your entire dependency tree. The question isn't just "is this package vulnerable?" — it's "should you trust this package at all?"

Our founding team built dependency management systems at npm and GitHub, and we saw firsthand how little visibility most organizations had into what they were actually shipping. We're building the supply chain intelligence layer that every engineering organization needs but almost none have today.

Lockstep differentiates through depth of analysis — we assess 14 risk signals per package vs. the 2-3 that CVE-focused tools check — and through our maintainer health scoring, which predicts abandonment and compromise risk before incidents occur.

Target buyers are security engineering leads and VP Engineering at software companies with 50+ engineers. The sales trigger is typically a supply chain incident (their own or a high-profile public one) or a compliance mandate requiring SBOMs. Early traction: 92 companies, $1.7M ARR, scanning 340M+ packages monthly. Our open-source CLI drives bottom-up adoption, converting 18% of active users to paid team plans within 120 days.

description: Arbiter is an online dispute resolution platform for e-commerce marketplaces, SaaS companies, and digital platforms. When buyers and sellers disagree, Arbiter provides structured negotiation, mediation, and binding resolution — all without lawyers, courts, or months of waiting.
mission:

Arbiter was built to give digital commerce a native dispute resolution layer. Our platform guides both parties through a structured process — first attempting automated resolution based on platform policies, then offering mediated negotiation with AI assistance, and finally providing binding arbitration by qualified human neutrals when needed. The entire process happens online, typically resolves in 3-5 days, and costs a fraction of traditional alternatives.

We believe that trust is the infrastructure of commerce. Marketplaces that resolve disputes fairly and quickly see higher buyer confidence, higher seller retention, and fewer chargebacks. Our mission is to make fair resolution accessible to every transaction, regardless of size or geography.

Our founding team includes former eBay dispute resolution architects, AAA arbitrators, and marketplace operators. We've collectively resolved over 2 million disputes and we're bringing that expertise to every platform that needs it.

name: Cadre
tagline: Equity shouldn't require a law degree to understand
description: Cadre is an employee equity management platform for startups. It handles cap table management, offer letter generation, vesting schedules, 409A valuations, and employee equity education — so founders stop explaining stock options on napkins and employees actually understand what they own.
mission:
Startup equity is broken — not the concept, but the execution. Founders grant options without understanding dilution. Employees accept equity packages without grasping vesting cliffs, exercise windows, or tax implications. Early hires leave money on the table because nobody explained the difference between ISOs and NSOs. And the cap table lives in a spreadsheet that hasn't been reconciled since the seed round.

Cadre exists because equity is the most powerful tool startups have for attracting and retaining talent, and it's being wasted by bad tooling and worse communication. We've built a platform that handles the mechanics — cap table management, option grants, vesting tracking, 409A valuations, exercise workflows — and, just as importantly, the education. Every employee gets a personalized equity dashboard that shows what they own, what it could be worth, and what decisions they need to make (and when).

We're a team of former startup CFOs, equity compensation lawyers, and product designers who watched the same equity literacy gap cause problems at every company we worked at. The engineer who didn't exercise before the 90-day window. The early employee who didn't understand their tax obligation. The founder who accidentally issued more shares than authorized.

Our mission is to make equity work the way it was supposed to: as a genuine wealth-creation mechanism that aligns incentives, attracts exceptional people, and rewards the risk of joining early. That only happens when everyone — founders, employees, and investors — can see the same clear picture.
marketResearch:
The equity management software market is valued at $620M in 2025, projected to reach $1.8B by 2030 at 23% CAGR. Growth is driven by the increasing use of equity compensation beyond tech (healthcare, biotech, professional services), regulatory changes around equity tax treatment, and the sheer volume of VC-backed startups granting options. TAM is $1.8B, SAM targeting VC-backed startups with 10-500 employees in North America is $520M, SOM is $68M.

Competitors include Carta (dominant incumbent, $7.4B valuation but increasingly expensive and enterprise-focused), Pulley (strong SMB challenger, narrower feature set), and Shareworks/E*Trade (enterprise, post-IPO focus). Cadre differentiates through two dimensions: radical simplicity for early-stage companies (setup in under an hour, not weeks) and best-in-class employee equity education (personalized dashboards, tax scenario modeling, exercise decision guidance).

Target buyers are founders, CFOs, and heads of people at VC-backed startups from seed through Series C. The trigger event is typically hiring employee #10-20 when equity administration becomes too complex for spreadsheets. Early traction: 180 companies, $1.1M ARR, managing $2.4B in total equity value. Our PLG motion starts with a free cap table tool for up to 20 stakeholders, converting 26% to paid when companies need option grants, 409A valuations, or employee portals.

name: Perimeter
tagline: Zero trust that doesn't make your team want to quit
description: Perimeter is a zero-trust network access platform built for remote-first companies. It replaces VPNs with identity-based access controls that are invisible when they should be and ironclad when they need to be. Security without the friction.
mission:
VPNs were designed for a world where the office was the perimeter. You connected to the corporate network and you were "inside" — trusted to access everything. That model was already crumbling when remote work accelerated its collapse. Now your "network" is 400 employees on home wifi, coffee shop connections, and airport lounges, and the VPN is a bottleneck that everyone hates and many bypass.

Perimeter replaces the VPN with zero-trust network access — the principle that no user, device, or connection is inherently trusted. Every access request is verified against identity, device health, location, behavior patterns, and the specific resource being requested. The result is security that's simultaneously stronger and less annoying than a VPN.

We built Perimeter because we watched security teams deploy zero-trust architectures that were technically sound and operationally miserable. Constant MFA prompts. Broken workflows. Developers who couldn't access staging because their device score dropped. Zero trust doesn't have to mean zero productivity.

Our approach is invisible by default and strict when it matters. Accessing your normal tools from your managed device on your home network? Seamless. Accessing the production database from an unrecognized device in a new country? That's when Perimeter asks questions. Context-aware security that adapts its posture to actual risk, not blanket paranoia.
marketResearch:
The zero-trust security market is valued at $31.6B in 2025, projected to reach $67B by 2030 at 16.5% CAGR. The ZTNA sub-segment specifically — replacing VPNs with identity-based access — is $4.8B and growing at 25% CAGR. TAM is $4.8B, SAM targeting remote-first and hybrid companies with 50-5,000 employees is $1.6B, SOM is $190M.

Competitors include established ZTNA vendors (Zscaler, Cloudflare Access, Palo Alto Prisma) that are powerful but complex and enterprise-priced, and newer entrants (Tailscale, Twingate) that simplify access but offer limited policy engines. Perimeter differentiates by combining frictionless user experience with deep policy controls — context-aware access that adapts to risk signals in real time without interrupting low-risk workflows.

Target buyers are CISOs, IT leads, and heads of remote at companies with 100-2,000 remote employees. The pain point is universal: VPNs are a security liability and a productivity drain. The trigger event is usually a security incident traced to VPN credentials, or a new CISO mandate to implement zero trust. Early traction: 56 companies, $2.8M ARR, 98% user adoption rate (vs. 60-70% typical for VPN). Our free tier for up to 10 users drives bottom-up adoption in engineering teams, expanding to company-wide deployment.
